questions.why: Rectocele: bulge at lower 2/3rd of posterior vaginal wall.

questions.q: Cough impulse in an enterocele is:
questions.why: Enterocele: cough impulse +.

questions.q: Cough impulse in a rectocele is:
questions.why: Rectocele: cough impulse −.

questions.q: On P/R examination, the bulge of an enterocele is felt at the:
questions.why: Enterocele: bulge at tip of finger.

questions.q: On P/R examination, the bulge of a rectocele is felt at the:
questions.why: Rectocele: bulge at pulp of finger.

questions.q: Transillumination is positive in:
questions.why: Enterocele transilluminates (+ve); rectocele does not.

questions.q: Transillumination is negative in:
questions.why: Rectocele: transillumination −ve.

questions.q: A posterior vaginal wall bulge with absent cough impulse that is felt at the pulp of the finger per rectum is:
questions.why: These are features of rectocele.

questions.q: A posterior vaginal wall bulge with a positive cough impulse, bulge at the tip of the finger on P/R and positive transillumination is:
questions.why: These are features of enterocele.

questions.q: De Lancey's Level 1 supports the:
questions.why: Level 1 = upper 1/3rd of vagina.

questions.q: De Lancey's Level 2 supports the:
questions.why: Level 2 = middle 1/3rd of vagina.

questions.q: De Lancey's Level 3 supports the:
questions.why: Level 3 = lower 1/3rd of vagina.

questions.q: Level 1 support is provided by the cardinal ligament and the:
questions.why: Level 1 support = cardinal ligament + uterosacral ligament.

questions.q: Level 2 support is provided by the:
questions.why: Level 2 support = arcus tendineus fascia.

questions.q: Level 3 support is provided by the urogenital diaphragm muscles and the:
questions.why: Level 3 support = perineal body + muscles and urogenital diaphragm muscles.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Level 1 defect?
questions.why: Level 1 defects: uterocervical prolapse, apical prolapse, vault prolapse, enterocele, supravaginal elongation of cervix.

questions.q: Vault prolapse is a defect of De Lancey's level:
questions.why: Vault prolapse is a Level 1 defect.

questions.q: Supravaginal elongation of the cervix is a defect of:
questions.why: Level 1 defect.

questions.q: Apical prolapse is a defect of:
questions.why: Level 1 defect.

questions.q: Uterocervical prolapse is a defect of:
questions.why: Level 1 defect.

questions.q: Cystocele is a defect of De Lancey's level:
questions.why: Level 2 defects: cystocele and rectocele.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Level 2 defect along with cystocele?
questions.why: Level 2 defects: cystocele and rectocele.

questions.q: Urethrocele is a defect of De Lancey's level:
questions.why: Level 3 defects: urethrocele, lax perineum, rectocele ±.

questions.q: Lax perineum is a defect of De Lancey's level:
questions.why: Level 3 defect.

questions.q: Rectocele can be a defect of which levels?
questions.why: Rectocele is a Level 2 defect and also a Level 3 defect (±).

questions.q: The vault is the:
options: Upper end of the cervical canal
Part of the vagina left after hysterectomy
questions.why: Vault = part of vagina left after hysterectomy.

questions.q: In congenital elongation of the cervix, which part is elongated?
questions.why: In congenital elongation the vaginal part is elongated.

questions.q: Which fornix finding is seen in congenital elongation of the cervix?
questions.why: Congenital cervical elongation is associated with deep fornices.

sections.name: Symptoms and Vaginal Wall Prolapse Management

questions.q: A woman complains of vaginal fullness and a feeling of something coming out of the vagina. This is most suggestive of:
questions.why: Vaginal fullness and 'something coming out of vagina' are classic symptoms of prolapse.

questions.q: Low backache in prolapse is due to:
questions.why: Low backache occurs because of stretching of the uterosacral ligaments.

questions.q: Urinary symptoms in prolapse are mainly seen with:
questions.why: Urinary symptoms are produced by cystocele/urethrocele.

questions.q: Which urinary symptom is seen with cystocele or urethrocele?
questions.why: Cystocele/urethrocele cause incomplete voiding of urine.

questions.q: Cystocele or urethrocele increases the risk of:
questions.why: Incomplete voiding increases the risk of UTI.

questions.q: Stress urinary incontinence in prolapse is due to:
questions.why: SUI results from descent of the bladder neck.

questions.q: Bowel symptoms in prolapse are seen with:
questions.why: Bowel symptoms occur in rectocele/enterocele.

questions.q: Which skin/mucosal complication can occur in a prolapsed uterus protruding outside the introitus?
questions.why: Decubitus ulcer is a listed symptom/complication of prolapse.

questions.q: The pathology of the decubitus ulcer in prolapse is:
options: Venous congestion due to hampered venous return
questions.why: The ulcer is due to venous congestion from hampered venous return.

questions.q: The decubitus ulcer of prolapse is NOT due to:
questions.why: It is not due to friction.

questions.q: Packing used for a decubitus ulcer in prolapse consists of acriflavine and:
questions.why: Acriflavine (antiseptic) + glycerine (hygroscopic agent) packing.

questions.q: In acriflavine-glycerine packing, acriflavine acts as a(n):
questions.why: Acriflavine is the antiseptic.

questions.q: In acriflavine-glycerine packing, glycerine acts as a(n):
questions.why: Glycerine is the hygroscopic agent.

questions.q: A decubitus ulcer treated with acriflavine and glycerine packing heals in about:
questions.why: Healing takes 10-15 days.

questions.q: Which topical antiseptic is also used for a decubitus ulcer in prolapse?
questions.why: Betadine is also used.

questions.q: Kegel's exercise is a form of:
questions.why: Kegel's exercise strengthens the pelvic floor muscles.

questions.q: Kegel's exercises are advised:
questions.why: They are advised during pregnancy and after child birth.

questions.q: Kegel's exercise consists of:
options: Alternate contraction and relaxation of the pelvic floor
Sustained relaxation of the pelvic floor
questions.why: Alternate contraction and relaxation of pelvic floor.

questions.q: The prescribed schedule of Kegel's exercise is:
questions.why: 10 cycles x 3 times/day.

questions.q: The best prevention/treatment of 1st degree prolapse is:
questions.why: Kegel's exercise is the best prevention/Rx of 1st degree prolapse.

questions.q: Management of vaginal wall prolapse is:
questions.why: Management of vaginal prolapse is independent of age/parity.

questions.q: Surgery for cystocele/urethrocele is:
questions.why: Anterior colporrhaphy is done for cystocele/urethrocele.

questions.q: Anterior colporrhaphy involves excision of the prolapsed vaginal wall and repair of the retained walls with:
questions.why: Retained walls are repaired with interrupted sutures.

questions.q: Surgery for enterocele is:
questions.why: McCall culdoplasty is the surgery for enterocele.

questions.q: McCall culdoplasty is also done prophylactically:
questions.why: It is done prophylactically post hysterectomy to prevent enterocele.

questions.q: Which of the following is an outdated surgery for enterocele?
questions.why: Outdated surgeries: Moschcowitz and Halban repair.

questions.q: Along with Moschcowitz repair, which operation is listed as an outdated surgery for enterocele?
questions.why: Halban repair is an outdated surgery for enterocele.

questions.q: Surgery for rectocele or lax perineum is:
questions.why: Posterior colpoperineorrhaphy for rectocele/laxed perineum.

units.title: Uterine Prolapse: Age-Dependent Management and Slings

questions.q: Management of uterine prolapse is:
questions.why: Uterine prolapse management is age dependent.

questions.q: Uterocervical prolapse in a female who wants future child bearing is managed by:
questions.why: Sling surgery/cervicopexy is used when future child bearing is desired.

questions.q: The pre-requisite for sling surgery in a woman wanting future child bearing is:
questions.why: Uterocervical length must be normal.

questions.q: The sling used in these operations is made of:
questions.why: Sling made of mersilene tape.

questions.q: The sling surgery provides:
questions.why: The sling provides artificial support to the uterus.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the sling surgeries listed for uterine prolapse?
questions.why: Listed slings: Purandare, Shirodkar, Composite/Virkud and Khanna.

questions.q: The anterior sling for uterine prolapse is the:
questions.why: Anterior = Purandare sling.

questions.q: In the Purandare sling, one end is attached to the isthmus of the uterus and the other to the:
questions.why: The other side is the rectus sheath.

questions.q: The Purandare sling is a:
questions.why: Purandare sling is dynamic.

questions.q: Complications of the Purandare sling are:
questions.why: Complications are less.

questions.q: The success rate of the Purandare sling is:
questions.why: Success rate is low.

questions.q: The posterior sling for uterine prolapse is the:
questions.why: Posterior = Shirodkar sling.

questions.q: In the Shirodkar sling, one side is attached to the isthmus of the uterus and the other side to:
options: Ligaments attached to the sacral promontory
questions.why: The other side is ligaments attached to the sacral promontory.

questions.q: The Shirodkar sling is a:
questions.why: Shirodkar sling is static.

questions.q: Complications of the Shirodkar sling are seen on which side?
questions.why: Complications are seen on the left side.

questions.q: Which bowel complication is seen on the left side with the Shirodkar sling?
questions.why: Sigmoid colon intestinal obstruction.

questions.q: Which of the following is a complication of the Shirodkar sling?
questions.why: Mesenteric injury is a listed complication.

questions.q: Which nerve may be injured in the Shirodkar sling?
questions.why: Injury to the genitofemoral nerve is a listed complication.

questions.q: Sigmoid colon obstruction in the Shirodkar sling is avoided by making a hook from the:
questions.why: A hook made from the psoas muscle avoids sigmoid colon obstruction.

questions.q: The success rate of the Shirodkar sling is:
questions.why: Success rate is high.

questions.q: The sling with a higher success rate is the:
questions.why: Shirodkar (static, posterior) has a high success rate whereas Purandare has a low success rate.

questions.q: The sling that is dynamic with fewer complications but a low success rate is:
questions.why: Purandare = dynamic, fewer complications, low success rate.

questions.q: The composite sling is also known as the:
questions.why: Composite sling = Virkud sling.

questions.q: In the Virkud (composite) sling, the left side uses the:
questions.why: Left side: Purandare sling.

questions.q: In the Virkud (composite) sling, the right side uses the:
questions.why: Right side: Shirodkar's sling.

questions.q: The Khanna sling is an:
questions.why: Khanna sling is an anterior sling surgery.

questions.q: In the Khanna sling, one side is attached to the isthmus of the uterus and the other to the:
questions.why: The other side is the anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS).

questions.q: Prolapse in a reproductive age female who does not need future child bearing is managed by:
questions.why: Fothergill/Manchester repair is the operation.

questions.q: Another name for the Fothergill repair is:
questions.why: Fothergill repair = Manchester repair.

questions.q: The first step of the Fothergill repair is:
questions.why: Step 1: cervical amputation.

questions.q: The second step of the Fothergill repair is:
questions.why: Step 2: plication of cardinal ligament.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recognised complication of the Manchester repair?
questions.why: Complications: cervical stenosis, fibrosis, cervical incompetence.

questions.q: Fothergill surgery may result in which of the following cervical complications?
questions.why: Cervical incompetence is a listed complication.

questions.q: Which tissue complication is listed after Fothergill surgery?
questions.why: Fibrosis is a listed complication.

questions.q: Cervical stenosis after Fothergill surgery is prevented by:
options: Prophylactic D&C plus dilatation of the cervix
questions.why: Prophylactic D & C + dilatation of the cervix prevents cervical stenosis.

questions.q: The Shirodkar modification of Fothergill surgery involves:
options: Only plication of the cardinal ligament
questions.why: Shirodkar modification = only plication of cardinal ligament.

questions.q: The Shirodkar modification of Fothergill surgery can be done in females who:
questions.why: Since the cervix is not amputated, it can be done in women needing future child bearing.

questions.q: Nulliparous prolapse, or prolapse in a female who wants to retain the uterus, is managed by:
questions.why: Sacrohysteropexy is indicated.

questions.q: In sacrohysteropexy, the mesh is placed between the sacrum and the:
questions.why: The mesh runs from the uterine isthmus to the sacrum.

questions.q: Prolapse is prevented after sacrohysteropexy because the mesh leads to granulation tissue, then scar, then:
questions.why: Mesh → granulation tissue → scar → fibrosis → prevents prolapse.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of surgical options in females wanting future child bearing?
options: Sacrohysteropexy > Sling surgery > Shirodkar modification of Fothergill repair
Sling surgery > Sacrohysteropexy > Shirodkar modification of Fothergill repair
Sling surgery > Shirodkar modification of Fothergill repair > Sacrohysteropexy
Shirodkar modification of Fothergill repair > Sling surgery > Sacrohysteropexy
questions.why: Order of preference: sacrohysteropexy > sling surgery > Shirodkar modification of Fothergill repair.

questions.q: The best surgical option in a female with prolapse wanting future child bearing is:
questions.why: Sacrohysteropexy is at the top of the order.

units.title: Prolapse in Menopause, Elderly and Pregnancy

questions.q: Prolapse in a menopausal female is managed by:
questions.why: Vaginal hysterectomy is the treatment in menopausal females.

questions.q: Prolapse in a 60-65 year female with some contraindications to surgery (diabetes/hypertension) is managed by:
questions.why: Lefort's colpocleisis is for 60-65 year females with contraindications to major surgery.

questions.q: Lefort's colpocleisis involves:
options: Stitching the anterior and posterior walls of the vagina
Suspension of the vault to the sacrum
questions.why: The anterior and posterior vaginal walls are stitched together.

questions.q: Lefort's colpocleisis can be done under:
questions.why: It can be done under local anaesthesia, which suits patients with comorbidities.

questions.q: A pre-requisite for Lefort's colpocleisis is to rule out:
questions.why: Endometrial and cervical cancers must be ruled out.

questions.q: Lefort's colpocleisis is NOT done in:
questions.why: It is not done in reproductive age females.

questions.q: Lefort's colpocleisis is also done in the management of:
questions.why: It is also done in vault prolapse.

questions.q: Prolapse in an old female (>65 years) with comorbidities and unfit for any surgery is managed by:
questions.why: A ring pessary is used in females unfit for any surgery.

questions.q: A ring pessary is a:
questions.why: Ring pessary is a space occupying device.

questions.q: A ring pessary offers:
questions.why: Ring pessary is a temporary cure.

questions.q: A ring pessary is changed every:
questions.why: Changed every 3-6 months.

questions.q: Which pessaries are used for prolapse during pregnancy and puerperium?
options: Ring, Gell horn or donut pessary
questions.why: Ring/Gell horn/donut pessary.

questions.q: A pessary used for prolapse in pregnancy is removed at about:
questions.why: At about 16-18 weeks the pessary is removed.

questions.q: Why can the pessary be removed at about 16-18 weeks of pregnancy?
options: The uterus becomes an abdominal organ, correcting the prolapse automatically
questions.why: The uterus becomes an abdominal organ, so prolapse is automatically corrected.

questions.q: Vault prolapse is:
options: Prolapse of the uterus with intact cervix
Prolapse of the vaginal stump after hysterectomy
questions.why: Vault prolapse = prolapse of vaginal stump after hysterectomy.

questions.q: Vault prolapse is prevented by:
questions.why: Uterosacral suspension prevents vault prolapse.

questions.q: Prophylactic uterosacral suspension is done during:
questions.why: It is done during vaginal hysterectomy.

questions.q: Uterosacral suspension is used for:
options: Both prevention and treatment of vault prolapse
questions.why: Uterosacral suspension is used for prevention and also for Rx.

questions.q: Which vaginal-route surgery fixes the vault to the sacrospinous ligament?
questions.why: Vaginal surgeries: uterosacral suspension, sacrospinous fixation, Lefort's colpocleisis.

questions.q: Which vaginal surgery is used for both prevention and treatment of vault prolapse?
questions.why: Uterosacral suspension is a vaginal surgery for vault prolapse.

questions.q: Which obliterative vaginal operation is an option for vault prolapse?
questions.why: Lefort's colpocleisis is also done for vault prolapse.

questions.q: The abdominal surgery for vault prolapse is:
questions.why: Abdominal surgery = sacral colpopexy.

questions.q: Burch colposuspension is the management of:
questions.why: Burch colposuspension is for SUI.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a management of vault prolapse?
questions.why: Burch colposuspension is not a management of vault prolapse.

questions.q: Uterosacral suspension is:
questions.why: Uterosacral suspension is easy to perform.

questions.q: In uterosacral suspension, sutures are passed through the:
questions.why: Sutures go through the uterosacral ligament to suspend the vault.

questions.q: The best management for vault prolapse is:
questions.why: Sacral colpopexy is the best management.

questions.q: Sacral colpopexy is:
options: Done only in reproductive age females
questions.why: It is difficult to perform.

questions.q: In sacral colpopexy, a mesh is placed between the:
options: Pubic symphysis and the vaginal vault
questions.why: Mesh between sacrum and vaginal vault.

questions.q: To check for stress urinary incontinence, the prolapsed part is first put into the normal anatomical position:
questions.why: The prolapse is reduced without emptying the bladder and SUI is checked.

questions.q: The P/V examination for prolapse is done after:
questions.why: The bladder is emptied before the P/V examination.

questions.q: P/V examination in prolapse assesses the size of the uterus, its position and:
options: Whether there is uterocervical descent or only vaginal descent
questions.why: The examiner checks for uterocervical descent versus only vaginal descent.

questions.q: The position of the uterus assessed on P/V examination in prolapse is mainly checked for:
questions.why: Position (retroversion) is checked.

questions.q: The degree of prolapse is assessed by asking the patient to:
options: Strain or perform the Valsalva manoeuvre
questions.why: Ask the patient to strain/perform Valsalva.

questions.q: After reducing the prolapse to its normal position, which measurement is taken?
questions.why: Total uterovaginal length is measured.

questions.q: Cystocele plus rectocele is managed by anterior colporrhaphy and:
questions.why: Anterior + posterior colporrhaphy.

questions.q: Anterior colporrhaphy combined with posterior colporrhaphy is called:
questions.why: Together they constitute pelvic floor repair.

questions.q: An old female with 3rd degree uterine prolapse plus cystocele and rectocele is managed by vaginal hysterectomy plus:
questions.why: Vaginal hysterectomy + pelvic floor repair.

questions.q: Vaginal hysterectomy plus pelvic floor repair is known as:
questions.why: This combination is Ward Mayo's hysterectomy.

questions.q: In an old female with 3rd degree uterine prolapse, cystocele and rectocele, McCall culdoplasty is added to prevent:
questions.why: McCall culdoplasty prevents enterocele.

questions.q: In an old female with 3rd degree uterine prolapse, cystocele and rectocele, uterosacral suspension is added to prevent:
questions.why: Uterosacral suspension prevents vault prolapse.

questions.q: Ward Mayo's hysterectomy is combined with McCall culdoplasty to prevent enterocele and with which procedure to prevent vault prolapse?
questions.why: Ward Mayo's hysterectomy + McCall culdoplasty + uterosacral suspension.

questions.q: The gonads in early intrauterine life are described as:
questions.why: Gonads are bipotential; they can become testis or ovary.

questions.q: The gonads are derived from the:
questions.why: Gonads arise from the genital ridge.

questions.q: The genital ridge gives rise to gonads at about:
questions.why: Gonads are derived from the genital ridge at 5-6 weeks.

questions.q: The gene that determines whether the bipotential gonad becomes testis or ovary is:
questions.why: Based on the SRY gene the gonads develop into testis or ovary.

questions.q: In the presence of the SRY gene, the gonads develop into:
questions.why: SRY present leads to male gonads (testis).

questions.q: In the absence of the SRY gene, the gonads develop into:
questions.why: SRY absent leads to female gonads (ovaries).

questions.q: SRY is best described as a:
options: Sex related gene on the Y chromosome
Steroid receptor on the X chromosome
questions.why: SRY is the sex related gene on the Y chromosome.

questions.q: SRY is also known as the:
questions.why: SRY = testis determining factor.

questions.q: The SRY gene is located on the:
options: Long arm of the X chromosome
Distal end of the short arm of the Y chromosome
Long arm of the Y chromosome
Short arm of the X chromosome
questions.why: SRY lies at the distal end of the short arm of the Y chromosome.

questions.q: Sex determination of the child depends on the SRY gene: if it is present the child is:
questions.why: SRY present leads to a male child.

questions.q: Sex determination of the child depends on the SRY gene: if it is absent the child is:
questions.why: SRY absent leads to a female child.

questions.q: The micronutrient necessary for SRY function/sex determination is:
questions.why: Zinc is the micronutrient necessary.

questions.q: In the intrauterine period, how many pairs of genital ducts are present?
questions.why: Two pairs: mullerian and Wolffian ducts.

questions.q: Which two pairs of genital ducts are present in the embryo?
questions.why: Mullerian duct and Wolffian duct.

questions.q: Another name for the mullerian duct is the:
questions.why: Mullerian = paramesonephric duct.

questions.q: Another name for the Wolffian duct is the:
questions.why: Wolffian = mesonephric duct.

questions.q: The mullerian duct is derived from:
questions.why: Mullerian duct arises from an outgrowth of coelomic epithelium.

questions.q: The Wolffian duct is derived from:
questions.why: Wolffian duct arises from intermediate mesoderm.

questions.q: Of the two pairs of genital ducts, in each individual:
options: One pair forms internal genital organs while the other regresses
questions.why: One pair forms internal genital organs; the other regresses and leaves remnants.

questions.q: According to the timeline given, at 9 weeks one pair of ducts goes on to form the:
questions.why: At 9 weeks one pair of ducts forms the internal genital organs.

questions.q: According to the timeline given, at 10 weeks the other pair of ducts:
questions.why: At 10 weeks the other pair regresses and leaves remnants.

questions.q: Which of the following is an internal genital organ in males derived from the Wolffian duct?
questions.why: Male internal organs: seminal vesicles, epididymis, ejaculatory duct, vas deferens.

questions.q: Which structure is listed among the male internal genital organs along with the seminal vesicles?
questions.why: Epididymis is a male internal genital organ.

questions.q: The ejaculatory duct belongs to which group of genital derivatives?
questions.why: Ejaculatory duct is a male internal genital organ.

questions.q: The vas deferens develops from which genital duct?
questions.why: Vas deferens is a male internal genital organ developing from the Wolffian duct.

questions.q: Which of the following is a female internal genital organ derived from the mullerian duct?
questions.why: Female internal organs: fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, upper vagina.

questions.q: Which of the following is a female internal genital organ?
questions.why: Uterus is derived from the mullerian ducts.

questions.q: The cervix is derived from the:
questions.why: Cervix is a mullerian derivative.

questions.q: Which part of the vagina is a mullerian derivative?
questions.why: The upper vagina is mullerian; the lower vagina is from the sinovaginal bulb of the urogenital sinus.

questions.q: The most common method of determining sex is:
questions.why: Appearance of external genitalia is the most common method.

questions.q: The applied aspect of using external genitalia to determine sex is the problem of:
questions.why: Ambiguous genitalia make it difficult to determine sex of a child.

questions.q: The best method of sex determination is:
questions.why: Karyotyping is the best method.

questions.q: On karyotyping, presence of the Y chromosome indicates:
questions.why: Y chromosome present = male.

questions.q: On karyotyping, absence of the Y chromosome indicates:
questions.why: Y chromosome absent = female.

questions.q: The karyotype of Turner syndrome is:
questions.why: Turner syndrome is 45,XO.

questions.q: The phenotypic sex of an individual with Turner syndrome is:
questions.why: Turner syndrome (45,XO) is female.

questions.q: The karyotype of Klinefelter syndrome is:
questions.why: Klinefelter syndrome is 47,XXY.

questions.q: The phenotypic sex of an individual with Klinefelter syndrome is:
questions.why: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is male.

questions.q: The number of Barr bodies equals:
questions.why: Barr bodies = number of X chromosomes - 1.

questions.q: Barr body count is NOT effective in all cases of sex determination, for example in:
options: Normal males and normal females only
questions.why: Eg. Turner syndrome and Klinefelter syndrome.

questions.q: Which method of sex determination can be misleading in Turner and Klinefelter syndromes?
questions.why: Barr body count is not effective in all cases, eg. Turner and Klinefelter syndromes.

questions.q: The most important gene for formation of the testis is:
questions.why: SRY > SOX-9 in importance.

questions.q: The SRY gene activates which gene to form the testis?
questions.why: SRY activates SOX-9, leading to formation of testis.

questions.q: The testis forms at:
questions.why: Formation of testis at 6-7 weeks.

questions.q: After formation, the testis is:
questions.why: The testis is hormonally active, unlike the ovary in intrauterine life.

questions.q: The number of cell types in the testis that are hormonally active in intrauterine life is:
questions.why: Sertoli cells and Leydig cells.

questions.q: The two types of hormone-producing cells in the fetal testis are:
questions.why: Sertoli cells and Leydig cells.

questions.q: The first feature of testis development seen on USG is:
questions.why: First feature on USG: appearance of testicular cords.

questions.q: Sertoli cells are stimulated by:
questions.why: FSH acts on Sertoli cells.

questions.q: Sertoli cells secrete:
questions.why: Sertoli cells produce inhibin B.

questions.q: Inhibin B exerts which effect on FSH?
questions.why: Inhibin B negatively feeds back on FSH.

questions.q: Sertoli cells are also known as:
questions.why: AKA sustentacular cells.

questions.q: Sertoli cells secrete which hormone that acts on the mullerian duct?
questions.why: Sertoli cells secrete AMH/MIS.

questions.q: Anti-mullerian hormone is also known as:
questions.why: AMH = MIS.

questions.q: Anti-mullerian hormone synthesis in males occurs during:
questions.why: In males it is synthesised in intrauterine life.

questions.q: In females, AMH is synthesised:
options: At puberty from pre-antral follicles of the ovary
In intrauterine life from fetal ovary
questions.why: In females: at puberty, from pre-antral follicles.

questions.q: Which cells in the adult female ovary produce AMH?
questions.why: Pre-antral follicles secrete AMH at puberty.

units.title: Functions of AMH and Mullerian Remnants

questions.q: A function of AMH in males is:
questions.why: AMH is involved in abdominal descent of the testis.

questions.q: AMH acts on the mullerian duct to cause:
questions.why: AMH inhibits the mullerian duct, which regresses.

questions.q: Which of the following is a mullerian duct remnant in males?
questions.why: Remnants: prostatic utricle, appendix of testis, hydatid of Morgagni.

questions.q: Regression of the mullerian duct under AMH leaves which testicular remnant?
questions.why: Appendix of testis is a mullerian remnant.

questions.q: In males, the hydatid of Morgagni is a remnant of which duct?
questions.why: Hydatid of Morgagni is a mullerian remnant.

questions.q: How many mullerian remnants are listed in males?
questions.why: Prostatic utricle, appendix of testis, hydatid of Morgagni.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a mullerian duct remnant in males?
questions.why: Epididymis is a Wolffian derivative.

questions.q: Leydig cells are stimulated by:
questions.why: LH acts on Leydig cells.

questions.q: Leydig cells are located:
questions.why: Leydig cells lie outside the blood-testis barrier.

questions.q: Leydig cells secrete:
questions.why: Leydig cells synthesise testosterone.

questions.q: Testosterone synthesis in the fetus begins at:
questions.why: Testosterone is synthesised from 8 weeks.

questions.q: Testosterone promotes growth of the:
questions.why: Testosterone promotes Wolffian duct growth, leading to male internal genital organs.

questions.q: Wolffian duct growth by testosterone leads to development of:
questions.why: Male internal genital organs develop.

questions.q: A function of testosterone in males is:
questions.why: Testosterone causes scrotal descent; AMH helps abdominal descent.

questions.q: Testosterone exerts negative feedback on:
questions.why: Negative feedback on GnRH.

questions.q: Negative feedback of testosterone on GnRH causes:
questions.why: It reduces LH and FSH.

questions.q: Testosterone is converted to dihydrotestosterone by the enzyme:
questions.why: 5α-reductase forms DHT.

questions.q: Dihydrotestosterone causes:
questions.why: DHT masculinises the external genitalia.

questions.q: Wolffian duct growth is mediated by testosterone, whereas external genital masculinisation is mediated by:
questions.why: DHT masculinises external genitalia.

questions.q: Testosterone and dihydrotestosterone act through:
questions.why: Same receptor.

questions.q: The first stimulus for testosterone production by the fetal testis is:
questions.why: hCG is the 1st stimulus stimulating testosterone production.

questions.q: The structure that causes descent of the testis is the:
questions.why: Gubernaculum/processus vaginalis causes descent of testis.

questions.q: The female homologue of the gubernaculum is the:
questions.why: Homologous structure in females: round ligament.

questions.q: Which hormone mediates abdominal descent of the testis?
questions.why: AMH is for abdominal descent.

questions.q: Which hormone mediates scrotal descent of the testis?
questions.why: Testosterone is for scrotal descent.

questions.q: Normal female karyotype with absent SRY gene is:
questions.why: 46 XX with absent SRY gene.

questions.q: The fetal ovary in the intrauterine period is:
questions.why: Formation of ovary: hormonally silent in intrauterine period.

questions.q: In females, absence of Sertoli cells results in:
questions.why: No Sertoli cells, so absent AMH.

questions.q: Absent AMH in the female fetus leads to:
questions.why: Absent AMH allows growth of the mullerian duct.

questions.q: Growth of the mullerian duct in females results in formation of:
questions.why: Formation of the internal genital organs.

questions.q: In females, absence of Leydig cells results in:
questions.why: No Leydig cells, no testosterone.

questions.q: In the female fetus, the Wolffian duct:
questions.why: Absent testosterone causes Wolffian duct regression.

questions.q: Absence of dihydrotestosterone in the female fetus results in:
options: No masculinisation of the external genitalia
questions.why: Without DHT the external genitalia stay female.

questions.q: For development of the female external genitalia, which statement is true?
options: AMH from Sertoli cells is required
Testosterone from the ovary is required
questions.why: No external stimulus is required for development of female external genitalia.

questions.q: Which of the following is a Wolffian duct remnant in females?
questions.why: Female Wolffian remnants: epoophoron, paroophoron, Gartner's duct.

questions.q: Which Wolffian remnant in females lies in the leaves of the broad ligament along with the epoophoron?
questions.why: Paroophoron is a Wolffian remnant in the leaves of the broad ligament.

questions.q: Persistence of the mesonephric duct in females is called:
questions.why: Gartner's duct is the remnant of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct.

questions.q: The epoophoron is a remnant of the:
options: Cranial end of the mesonephric tubule
Caudal end of the mesonephric tubule
questions.why: Epoophoron = cranial end of mesonephric tubule.

questions.q: The paroophoron is a remnant of the:
options: Caudal end of the mesonephric tubule
Cranial end of the mesonephric tubule
questions.why: Paroophoron = caudal end of mesonephric tubule.

questions.q: Normal sexual development recap: Gartner's duct is a remnant of which embryological duct?
questions.why: Gartner's duct = mesonephric duct remnant.

questions.q: The epoophoron and paroophoron are located in the:
questions.why: Both lie in the leaves of the broad ligament.

questions.q: Gartner's duct lies in the:
questions.why: Gartner's duct lies in the anterolateral wall of the vagina.

questions.q: A cyst arising from a remnant in the anterolateral vaginal wall is called a:
questions.why: Gartner's duct remnant gives a Gartner's cyst.

questions.q: Complete development of the ovary requires:
questions.why: Both X chromosomes present: complete ovary.

questions.q: Ovarian development in Turner syndrome (XO) is:
questions.why: Turner syndrome has incomplete ovarian development.

questions.q: Incomplete ovarian development in Turner syndrome results in:
questions.why: Streak gonads.

questions.q: The upper vagina is derived from the:
questions.why: Upper vagina: mullerian duct.

questions.q: The lower vagina is derived from the:
options: Sinovaginal bulb of the urogenital sinus
questions.why: Lower vagina: sinovaginal bulb of urogenital sinus.

questions.q: The ovary is derived from the:
questions.why: Ovary: genital ridge.

questions.q: The testes appear at:
questions.why: Testes: 6-7 weeks.

questions.q: The ovaries appear at:
questions.why: Ovaries: 7-8 weeks.

questions.q: Differentiation of female and male occurs at:
questions.why: Differentiation of female and male: 10 weeks.

questions.q: Development of the external genitalia is complete by about:
questions.why: External genitalia development: 14 weeks.

questions.q: Differentiation of male and female genitalia, enabling sex determination by USG, is from:
questions.why: From 12-14 weeks (sex determination by USG).

questions.q: MIS/AMH acts on which mullerian duct?
questions.why: AMH acts on the ipsilateral mullerian duct.

questions.q: Because AMH acts only on the ipsilateral mullerian duct, which condition can show unilateral development?
questions.why: Unilateral development: true hermaphroditism/ovotestis.

questions.q: A role of estrogen at puberty is:
questions.why: Estrogen causes growth of uterus at puberty.

questions.q: Which of the following causes a hypoplastic/infantile uterus due to low oestrogen?
questions.why: Turner's syndrome (streak ovaries) leads to low oestrogen and an infantile uterus.

questions.q: Which of the following causes a hypoplastic uterus due to low oestrogen?
questions.why: Gonadal dysgenesis leads to low oestrogen.

questions.q: Kallmann syndrome causes a hypoplastic uterus because of:
options: Hypothalamic failure with low GnRH, LH and FSH
questions.why: Hypothalamic failure causes low GnRH, then low LH/FSH, then low oestrogen.

questions.q: A poorly developed uterus is called a:
questions.why: Hypoplastic/infantile uterus.

sections.name: External Genitalia, Homologues and Ambiguous Genitalia

questions.q: Development of external genitalia depends on:
questions.why: Depends on intrauterine testosterone (as DHT).

questions.q: The genital tubercle forms the penis in the presence of testosterone and the ___ in its absence:
questions.why: Genital tubercle: penis / clitoris.

questions.q: The labioscrotal swelling forms the scrotum with testosterone and the ___ without it:
questions.why: Labioscrotal swelling: scrotum / labia majora.

questions.q: The genital fold forms the penile urethra with testosterone and the ___ without it:
questions.why: Genital fold: penile urethra / labia minora.

questions.q: The male homologue of the clitoris is the:
questions.why: Clitoris is homologous to penis.

questions.q: The male homologue of the labia majora is the:
questions.why: Labia majora is homologous to scrotum.

questions.q: The male homologue of the labia minora is the:
questions.why: Labia minora is homologous to penile urethra.

questions.q: The structure derived from the genital tubercle in males is the:
questions.why: Genital tubercle forms the penis.

questions.q: The structure derived from the labioscrotal swelling in males is the:
questions.why: Labioscrotal swelling forms the scrotum.

questions.q: The structure derived from the genital fold in males is the:
questions.why: Genital fold forms the penile urethra.

questions.q: In males, testosterone is produced by the testis and the:
questions.why: Males: testis and adrenal gland.

questions.q: In females, the source of androgen/testosterone is the:
questions.why: Females: adrenal glands.

questions.q: In females, androgens are converted to oestrogen by the enzyme:
questions.why: Androgen converts to oestrogen through aromatase.

questions.q: An XY individual with absent testosterone has external genitalia that are:
questions.why: XY, testosterone absent: female.

questions.q: An XX individual with absent testosterone has external genitalia that are:
questions.why: XX, testosterone absent: female.

questions.q: An XY individual with normal testosterone has external genitalia that are:
questions.why: XY, normal testosterone: male.

questions.q: An XY individual with a low level of testosterone has external genitalia that are:
questions.why: XY, low testosterone: ambiguous.

questions.q: An XX individual with a low level of testosterone has external genitalia that are:
questions.why: XX, low level: ambiguous.

questions.q: Which combination gives ambiguous genitalia?
options: Low level of testosterone in either XX or XY
questions.why: Low testosterone level gives ambiguous genitalia in both.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature defining ambiguous genitalia?
options: Fully formed scrotum with descended testes
questions.why: Features: undetermined sex, clitoromegaly, micropenis, labioscrotal fold/fusion, bifid scrotum.

questions.q: Micropenis is considered a feature of:
questions.why: Micropenis is a feature defining ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: A bifid scrotum is a feature of:
questions.why: Bifid scrotum is a feature defining ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: Fusion of the labioscrotal folds is seen in which clinical situation?
questions.why: Labioscrotal fold/fusion is a feature defining ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: The most common cause of ambiguous genitalia in an XY individual is:
questions.why: In XY: partial androgen insensitivity syndrome.

questions.q: The most common cause of ambiguous genitalia in an XX individual is:
questions.why: In XX: CAH.

questions.q: Ambiguous genitalia due to congenital adrenal hyperplasia is considered a:
questions.why: CAH presents as a medical emergency.

questions.q: The first step in the physical examination of a child with ambiguous genitalia is to examine the gonads at the:
questions.why: Examine gonads at the inguinal ring.

questions.q: If the gonads are palpable at the inguinal ring in a child with ambiguous genitalia, the karyotype is most likely:
questions.why: Palpable gonads: 46 XY.

questions.q: If the gonads are NOT palpable, the karyotype is most likely:
questions.why: Not palpable: 46 XX.

questions.q: A child with ambiguous genitalia and non-palpable gonads is presumed to have:
questions.why: Not palpable, 46 XX, leads to CAH.

questions.q: Which of the following is part of the workup when CAH is suspected?
questions.why: Investigations: S. electrolytes, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, karyotyping, FISH.

questions.q: Which hormone level is measured in suspected CAH?
questions.why: 17-hydroxyprogesterone is measured.

questions.q: The investigation of choice in the work-up of ambiguous genitalia is:
questions.why: Karyotyping is the IoC.

questions.q: Which molecular cytogenetic technique is used in the work-up of ambiguous genitalia?
questions.why: FISH is listed.

questions.q: Treatment of ambiguous genitalia due to CAH should be:
options: Initiated irrespective of the status of investigations
questions.why: Rx is initiated irrespective of status of investigations.

questions.q: Homologous glands are organs with the same:
questions.why: Organs with the same embryological origin.

questions.q: The female homologue of the prostate gland is the:
questions.why: Prostate = Skene/paraurethral gland.

questions.q: The male homologue of the Skene gland is the:
questions.why: Skene gland = prostate.

questions.q: The female homologue of the bulbourethral (Cowper's) gland is the:
questions.why: Cowper's gland = Bartholin gland.

questions.q: The male homologue of the Bartholin gland is the:
questions.why: Bartholin gland = bulbourethral gland.

questions.q: The bulbourethral gland (Cowper's gland) lies in the:
questions.why: Cowper's gland: deep perineal pouch.

questions.q: The Bartholin gland lies in the:
questions.why: Bartholin gland: superficial perineal pouch.

questions.q: The Bartholin gland originates from the:
questions.why: Bartholin gland origin: urogenital sinus.

questions.q: The karyotype of a male pseudohermaphrodite is:
questions.why: Male pseudohermaphrodite: 46 XY.

questions.q: The karyotype of a female pseudohermaphrodite is:
questions.why: Female pseudohermaphrodite: 46 XX.

questions.q: The external genitalia of a male pseudohermaphrodite are:
questions.why: Male pseudohermaphrodite: female external genitalia.

questions.q: The external genitalia of a female pseudohermaphrodite are:
questions.why: Female pseudohermaphrodite: ambiguous.

questions.q: The cause of male pseudohermaphroditism in this table is:
questions.why: Male pseudohermaphrodite: CAIS.

questions.q: The cause of female pseudohermaphroditism in this table is:
questions.why: Female pseudohermaphrodite: CAH.

questions.q: An individual with 46,XY karyotype and female external genitalia is called a:
questions.why: 46 XY with female external genitalia: male pseudohermaphrodite.

questions.q: An individual with 46,XX karyotype and ambiguous external genitalia is called a:
questions.why: 46 XX with ambiguous genitalia: female pseudohermaphrodite.

questions.q: The 46XX DSD chapter opens with two broad heads. Which pair heads the tree printed at the top of the page?
options: Abnormal development of gonads and abnormal karyotype
Abnormal development of gonads and ambiguous genitalia
Abnormal development of gonads and androgen insensitivity
questions.why: Page 160 splits 46XX DSD into abnormal development of gonads (ovotestes, Turner's syndrome) and ambiguous genitalia (raised maternal androgens, placental aromatase deficiency).

questions.q: Under 'abnormal development of gonads', the two entries listed are:
questions.why: Abnormal development of gonads has 1. Ovotestes and 2. Turner's syndrome.

questions.q: Fill up: The chapter is titled 'Disorders of sexual development in ____'.
questions.why: The heading on page 160 is 'Disorders of sexual development in 46XX'.

questions.q: True/False: In the 46XX DSD tree, ovotestes is filed under 'abnormal development of gonads'.
options: False - it is filed under ambiguous genitalia
False - it is filed under placental aromatase deficiency
questions.why: Ovotestes is the first entry under abnormal development of gonads.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a branch printed under 'ambiguous genitalia' in the 46XX tree?
questions.why: Turner's syndrome sits under abnormal development of gonads; the three others are under ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: A 46XX DSD classification lists 'a. Turner's syndrome' with the sub-line '45 XO (m/c) → streak ovary'. Which additional karyotype is printed under the mosaic arm?
questions.why: The mosaic entry prints 45XO → streak ovaries and 46XY → dysgenetic testes.

questions.q: Match the Turner's karyotype with the gonad printed beside it - 1) 45XO (m/c) 2) Mosaic 45XO 3) Mosaic 46XY ... A) Streak ovaries B) Dysgenetic testes C) Streak ovary
questions.why: 45XO (m/c) → streak ovary; mosaic 45XO → streak ovaries; mosaic 46XY → dysgenetic testes.

questions.q: Under raised maternal androgens, the three sources printed are:
options: Androgen secreting tumour, luteoma and androgenic drugs
Androgen secreting tumour, luteoma and placental aromatase deficiency
Luteoma, androgenic drugs and Turner mosaic
Androgenic drugs, theca lutein cysts and luteoma
questions.why: Raised maternal androgens lists androgen secreting tumour, luteoma, and androgenic drugs.

questions.q: Which tumour of pregnancy is named as a maternal source of androgens causing 46XX DSD?
questions.why: Luteoma of pregnancy is listed as an androgen-secreting tumour under raised maternal androgens.

questions.q: Fill up: The third item under ambiguous genitalia in the 46XX tree is placental ____ deficiency.
questions.why: Placental aromatase deficiency is the third item under ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: Scenario: A pregnant woman with no history of drug intake delivers a virilised 46XX infant. Imaging shows no maternal tumour. Which listed mechanism best explains the virilisation?
questions.why: With no tumour and no drugs, the remaining printed cause is placental aromatase deficiency.

questions.q: In placental aromatase deficiency, the arrow printed is 'aromatase ↓ → estrogen ↓'. What else is marked as raised?
questions.why: The block prints 'aromatase ↓ → estrogen ↓' together with '↑ maternal androgen'.

questions.q: Which statement about the printed 46XX DSD tree is correct?
options: Turner's syndrome appears under ambiguous genitalia
Placental aromatase deficiency appears under gonadal causes
Luteoma appears under abnormal development of gonads
Turner's syndrome appears under gonadal causes, not under ambiguous genitalia
questions.why: Only the first statement matches the printed tree.

questions.q: Fill up: Ovotestes carries the old term ____ hermaphrodite.
questions.why: The page prints 'Old term: True hermaphrodite'.

questions.q: The karyotype frequency in ovotestes is printed as:
questions.why: Karyotype: 46XX > 46XY.

questions.q: A child with ovotesticular DSD is karyotyped. Which result would the printed order make the MORE likely finding?
questions.why: Because 46XX exceeds 46XY in ovotestes.

questions.q: Odd one out - which term is NOT a printed synonym or label for ovotestes?
questions.why: True hermaphrodite is the old term; Turner mosaic belongs to the Turner branch, not ovotestes.

questions.q: True/False: In ovotestes, 46XY is more common than 46XX.
options: True - they are equal in the printed text
questions.why: The printed order is 46XX > 46XY, so 46XY is not more common.

questions.q: Which of the following best states why the old label 'true hermaphrodite' was used for ovotestes?
options: The external genitalia are always female
Both Mullerian and Wolffian ducts persist in every case
Both ovarian and testicular tissue are present in the same individual
questions.why: The term reflects the presence of both ovarian and testicular tissue.

questions.q: The MOST common pattern of gonadal distribution in ovotestes is:
options: One ovary and one testis, one on each side
Ovarian plus testicular tissue on both sides
Bilateral ovaries with a unilateral testis
A single gonad containing only testicular tissue
questions.why: Pattern (a): 1 ovary + 1 testis on each side - marked most common.

questions.q: The LEAST common pattern printed for ovotestes is:
options: One ovary and one testis on each side
Ovarian and testicular tissue on both sides
Bilateral testes with a unilateral ovary
Unilateral ovotestis with a streak gonad
questions.why: Pattern (b) - ovarian + testicular tissue on both sides - is marked L/c (least common).

questions.q: Fill up: The internal genitalia in ovotestes show both ____ and ____ internal genitalia.
questions.why: 'Internal genitalia: Both male + female internal genitalia.'

questions.q: On the side of the ovary, the internal genitalia are:
questions.why: 'On the side of ovary → Female internal genitalia.'

questions.q: On the side of the testis, the internal genitalia are:
questions.why: 'On the side of testes → male internal genitalia.'

questions.q: Match the gonadal side with the internal genital duct derivative - 1) Side of ovary 2) Side of testis ... A) Male internal genitalia B) Female internal genitalia
questions.why: Ovary side gives female internal genitalia; testis side gives male internal genitalia.

questions.q: A surgeon removes a left ovary and finds a Fallopian tube and hemi-uterus on that side. According to the printed rule this is because:
options: The internal genitalia follow the gonad on that side
AMH from the contralateral testis failed
questions.why: The rule printed is that internal genitalia correspond to the gonad on the same side.

questions.q: True/False: In ovotestes the internal genitalia are uniformly female regardless of which gonad is present.
options: True - unless a testis is palpable
True - because AMH is always absent
questions.why: Both male and female internal genitalia occur, following the gonad on each side.

questions.q: Odd one out - which finding does NOT follow the printed 'side of the gonad' rule?
options: Fallopian tube on the side of the ovary
Vas deferens on the side of the testis
Bilateral Fallopian tubes with a testis on each side
Hemi-uterus on the side of the ovary
questions.why: Bilateral tubes with bilateral testes contradicts the rule; the other three follow it.

questions.q: The external genitalia in ovotestes are described as ambiguous AND resembling:
questions.why: 'Ambiguous resembling male external genitalia d/t testosterone from adrenals.'

questions.q: Fill up: The ambiguous male-like external genitalia in ovotestes are attributed to testosterone from the ____.
questions.why: Printed: 'd/t testosterone from adrenals'.

questions.q: At birth, a child with ovotestes is MOST commonly presumed to be:
questions.why: 'm/c presumed as male at birth'.

questions.q: What fraction of ovotesticular cases show gynaecomastia?
questions.why: Printed: '>= 3/4th cases: Gynaecomastia (+) (d/t estrogen)'.

questions.q: Gynaecomastia in ovotestes is attributed to:
questions.why: The bracketed cause is '(d/t estrogen)'.

questions.q: What fraction of ovotesticular patients menstruate at puberty?
questions.why: 'At puberty: 1/4th cases: menstruation (+)'.

questions.q: Match the pubertal event in ovotestes with its printed frequency - 1) Gynaecomastia 2) Menstruation ... A) 1/4th cases B) >= 3/4th cases
questions.why: Gynaecomastia in >= 3/4th; menstruation in 1/4th.

questions.q: Scenario: A 15-year-old reared male presents with breast enlargement and cyclical bleeding per urethra. Karyotype 46XX. Which ovotesticular statistic pair fits?
options: Gynaecomastia is rare; menstruation occurs in most
Gynaecomastia is expected in most; menstruation occurs in a minority
questions.why: Gynaecomastia >= 3/4th and menstruation 1/4th - common first, uncommon second.

questions.q: True/False: The external genitalia in ovotestes are virilised because of testosterone produced by the testicular tissue itself.
options: True - the testis is the only source named
True - adrenal androgen is explicitly excluded
questions.why: The page attributes the virilisation to testosterone from the adrenals.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed pubertal feature of ovotestes?
questions.why: Voice deepening is a 5-alpha reductase deficiency page feature, not printed here.

units.title: Pathophysiology of CAH - Entry and Adrenal Map

questions.q: Fill up: Pathophysiology of CAH is introduced as the ____ cause of DSD in 46XX.
questions.why: 'm/c cause of DSD in 46XX'.

questions.q: What genital outcome does CAH produce in the 46XX fetus?
questions.why: 'Ambiguous genitalia in females'.

questions.q: Which trophic hormone drives the adrenal cortex in the printed physiology diagram?
questions.why: ACTH is shown acting on the adrenal gland at the top of the diagram.

questions.q: Fill up: The adrenal steroidogenic precursor printed at the head of both pathways is ____.
questions.why: Pregnenolone is the parent steroid in the diagram.

questions.q: Which enzyme converts pregnenolone to progesterone?
questions.why: 3-beta HSD is printed on the pregnenolone-to-progesterone arrow.

questions.q: Which enzyme converts pregnenolone to 17-OH pregnenolone?
questions.why: 17-alpha hydroxylase acts on pregnenolone to give 17-OH pregnenolone.

questions.q: Fill up: 17-OH pregnenolone is converted to DHEA by ____.
questions.why: The 17,20 lyase step generates DHEA.

questions.q: DHEA is converted to androstenedione by which enzyme?
questions.why: The side box prints 'DHEA --3beta HSD--> Androstenedione'.

questions.q: Which androgen is labelled the 'stronger androgen' in the printed summary?
questions.why: 'DHEA → Androstenedione → Testosterone (Stronger androgen)'.

questions.q: In females, the printed fate of testosterone is conversion by aromatase into:
questions.why: 'In females aromatase → Estrogen'.

questions.q: Which two adrenal end-products carry the printed phrase 'negative feedback on ACTH'?
questions.why: Both aldosterone and cortisol branches show negative feedback on ACTH.

questions.q: Match the mineralocorticoid pathway - 1) Progesterone to deoxycorticosterone 2) Deoxycorticosterone to corticosterone 3) Corticosterone to aldosterone ... A) 11-beta hydroxylase B) aldosterone synthase C) 21-alpha hydroxylase
questions.why: 21-alpha hydroxylase, then 11-beta hydroxylase, then aldosterone synthase.

questions.q: Match the glucocorticoid pathway - 1) 17-OH progesterone to 11-deoxycortisol 2) 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol ... A) 11-beta hydroxylase B) 21-alpha hydroxylase
questions.why: 21-alpha hydroxylase then 11-beta hydroxylase.

questions.q: Which pair of enzymes is printed as the adrenal gland's list on the sex-steroid side?
questions.why: The right-hand list prints 1. 17-alpha hydroxylase, 2. 17,20 lyase.

questions.q: Which triplet of enzymes is printed on the adrenal gland's corticosteroid side?
questions.why: The left-hand list prints 1. 21-alpha hydroxylase, 2. 11-beta hydroxylase, 3. 3-beta HSD.

questions.q: Fill up: Two distinct estrogen products are printed as estradiol and ____ from aromatase action.
questions.why: The diagram prints 'Estrogen (E2)' and 'Estrogen (E1)'.

questions.q: Scenario: A block is placed at 3-beta HSD. Which three adrenal products all fall together?
questions.why: 3-beta HSD sits before the mineralocorticoid, glucocorticoid and androgen arms, so all three end-products drop.

questions.q: True/False: In the printed diagram, aromatase acts on androstenedione and testosterone to give estrogens.
options: False - aromatase only acts on testosterone
False - aromatase converts DHEA to androstenedione
questions.why: Aromatase arrows are shown from both androstenedione and testosterone to estrogen.

questions.q: Odd one out - which enzyme is NOT part of the printed adrenal steroidogenic map?
questions.why: 5-alpha reductase is a peripheral conversion enzyme, not in this adrenal map.

questions.q: Fill up: Hyponatraemia in CAH is listed under the consequences of deficient ____.
questions.why: Hyponatraemia is grouped under 'D/t ↓ aldosterone'.

questions.q: Which electrolyte rises in CAH because aldosterone is deficient?
questions.why: Hyperkalaemia is listed under decreased aldosterone.

questions.q: The phrase 'salt water wasting' is printed with which accompanying descriptor?
questions.why: 'Salt water wasting (dehydration)'.

questions.q: Which acid-base disturbance is listed under aldosterone deficiency in CAH?
questions.why: Metabolic acidosis is printed in the aldosterone-deficiency group.

questions.q: Hypoglycaemia in CAH is a consequence of deficient:
questions.why: Hypoglycaemia is grouped under 'D/t ↓ cortisol'.

questions.q: Match the metabolic derangement with its deficient hormone - 1) Hypoglycaemia 2) Hyperkalaemia 3) Metabolic acidosis ... A) Aldosterone B) Cortisol
questions.why: Cortisol deficiency gives hypoglycaemia; aldosterone deficiency gives hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis.

questions.q: Odd one out - which feature belongs to cortisol deficiency rather than aldosterone deficiency?
questions.why: Hypoglycaemia is the sole cortisol-deficiency item; the other three are aldosterone-deficiency items.

questions.q: Fill up: Loss of negative feedback in CAH raises ACTH, which in turn raises androgens and ____.
questions.why: 'D/t loss of negative feedback: ↑ ACTH → ↑ Androgens, 17-OH progesterone ↑'.

questions.q: As a consequence of raised androgens, the female fetus shows and the male fetus shows:
options: Normal external genitalia; normal external genitalia
questions.why: Females: ambiguous genitalia. Males: normal external genitalia.

questions.q: True/False: The newborn male with CAH has ambiguous genitalia according to this page.
questions.why: Males have normal external genitalia; only females are ambiguous.

questions.q: Scenario: A 2-week-old 46XX infant presents with vomiting, dehydration, hyperkalaemia and ambiguous genitalia. Which mechanism explains BOTH the electrolyte and the genital findings?
options: Aldosterone deficiency plus loss of negative feedback raising androgens
questions.why: One mechanism (enzyme block) produces aldosterone deficiency and, via lost feedback, androgen excess.

questions.q: Which of the four listed aldosterone-deficiency features is printed with a bracketed explanation?
questions.why: Only 'salt water wasting' carries the bracket '(dehydration)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The screening test for CAH is serum ____.
questions.why: '1. Screening test: 17-OH progesterone'.

questions.q: A screening 17-OH progesterone below 200 ng means:
questions.why: '<200 ng → Rule out CAH'.

questions.q: A screening value at or above 800 ng means:
questions.why: '>= 800 ng → Confirm CAH'.

questions.q: Which screening band mandates the ACTH stimulation test?
questions.why: '200-800 ng → Diagnostic test: ACTH stimulation test'.

questions.q: Fill up: The diagnostic test named for the intermediate 17-OH progesterone band is the ____ test.
questions.why: ACTH stimulation test is printed as the diagnostic test.

questions.q: Match the 17-OH progesterone value with the action - 1) <200 ng 2) 200-800 ng 3) >=800 ng ... A) ACTH stimulation test B) Rule out CAH C) Confirm CAH
questions.why: Below 200 rules out; 200-800 needs stimulation; 800 and above confirms.

questions.q: Scenario: A neonate with ambiguous genitalia has a screening 17-OH progesterone of 540 ng/dL. What is the correct next step per the printed algorithm?
questions.why: 540 falls in the 200-800 band, which routes to the ACTH stimulation test.

questions.q: True/False: Treatment must wait for karyotyping before it is started.
options: True - treatment starts only after the ACTH test
questions.why: Printed: 'Treatment started without waiting for karyotyping results, based on physical examination findings'.

questions.q: Which physical-examination finding makes ambiguous genitalia a medical emergency here?
questions.why: 'Ambiguous genitalia + No palpable gonads → Treated as medical emergency'.

questions.q: Fill up: The drug of choice for the emergency management of CAH is ____.
questions.why: '1. DOC: Glucocorticoids'.

questions.q: The second drug class in the emergency list is:
questions.why: '2. Mineralocorticoids'.

questions.q: The fourth step in emergency management is:
questions.why: '4. Correction surgery for clitoromegaly later'.

questions.q: Match the emergency steps with their order - 1) First 2) Second 3) Third 4) Fourth ... A) Mineralocorticoids B) Correct electrolyte imbalance C) Glucocorticoids D) Surgery for clitoromegaly later
questions.why: The printed order is glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids, correct electrolytes, later surgery.

questions.q: Which four investigations are listed under 'send for investigation later'?
options: 17-OH progesterone, serum electrolytes, glucose and karyotyping/FISH
Serum electrolytes, glucose, LH and FSH
questions.why: The deferred list is 17-OH progesterone, serum electrolytes, glucose, karyotyping/FISH.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT in the deferred investigation list?
questions.why: ACTH stimulation is the diagnostic test in the earlier algorithm, not in the deferred list.

questions.q: Scenario: A neonate with ambiguous genitalia and impalpable gonads is brought in dehydrated with hyperkalaemia. Which step must precede the reconstructive surgery?
questions.why: Surgery for clitoromegaly is listed later; correction of electrolytes is step 3.

units.title: Prenatal Dexamethasone and Chorionic Villus Sampling

questions.q: Fill up: The drug of choice named for antenatal suppression is the glucocorticoid ____.
questions.why: 'DOC: Glucocorticoids - Dexamethasone'.

questions.q: Antenatal dexamethasone is started at which gestational age?
questions.why: 'Started at 4-5 wks of pregnancy'.

questions.q: The maximum delay permitted for starting antenatal dexamethasone is:
questions.why: The bracketed note prints '(maximum delay 9 wks)'.

questions.q: Fill up: Chorionic villus sampling for sex determination and gene testing is performed at ____ weeks.
questions.why: CVS is printed at 10-11 weeks.

questions.q: The indication printed at the head of the antenatal algorithm is:
questions.why: The flow begins with 'Previous child with CAH'.

questions.q: If CVS shows a male fetus, the printed instruction is to:
questions.why: 'male fetus / unaffected female fetus → Discontinue dexamethasone'.

questions.q: If CVS shows an affected female fetus, dexamethasone is:
options: Given only in the third trimester
questions.why: 'Affected female fetus → Continue dexamethasone'.

questions.q: Match the CVS result with the instruction - 1) Male fetus 2) Unaffected female fetus 3) Affected female fetus ... A) Continue dexamethasone B) Discontinue dexamethasone
questions.why: Only the affected female fetus continues; male and unaffected female stop.

questions.q: True/False: The note on this page describes CAH as an X-linked recessive disorder.
options: False - it is described as autosomal dominant
questions.why: Printed verbatim: 'Note: CAH: X-linked recessive disorder' (a source quirk - CAH is autosomal recessive in reality).

questions.q: Scenario: A woman whose first child had CAH presents at 6 weeks of gestation. What is the correct printed plan?
options: Wait until 10 weeks to start dexamethasone
Start dexamethasone now and perform CVS at 10-11 weeks
Perform CVS first and start dexamethasone only if the fetus is female
Start dexamethasone only after amniocentesis at 16 weeks
questions.why: Start at 4-5 weeks (6 is within the 9-week maximum delay) and test by CVS at 10-11 weeks.

questions.q: Odd one out - which does NOT appear in the antenatal dexamethasone page?
questions.why: Amniocentesis is not printed; CVS is the sampling method named.

questions.q: Which enzyme deficiency block opens with the phrase 'Leads to DSD in XY individuals'?
questions.why: The 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase block carries that line.

questions.q: Fill up: In 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase deficiency the three steroids marked as decreased are DHEA, androstenedione and ____.
questions.why: The arrows read ↓DHEA, ↓Androstenedione, ↓Testosterone.

questions.q: In 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase deficiency, the female fetus has:
questions.why: Female fetus: normal external genitalia; male fetus: ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: In 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase deficiency, the male fetus has ambiguous genitalia because of:
questions.why: 'male fetus: D/t ↓ Testosterone'.

questions.q: Fill up: In 3-beta HSD deficiency the weak androgen that accumulates is ____.
questions.why: Printed: '↑ DHEA (weak androgen)'.

questions.q: In 3-beta HSD deficiency, ambiguous genitalia occur in:
questions.why: The block prints 'Ambiguous genitalia - males + females'.

questions.q: In 3-beta HSD deficiency, virilisation of the female fetus is attributed to:
questions.why: 'Female fetus: D/t ↑ DHEA'.

questions.q: Which two steroids are printed as deficient in 3-beta HSD deficiency?
questions.why: The block marks ↓Aldosterone and ↓Cortisol, alongside ↑DHEA and ↓Testosterone.

questions.q: Match the fetal genital outcome to the mechanism - 1) 3-beta HSD deficiency, female fetus 2) 3-beta HSD deficiency, male fetus 3) 17-alpha hydroxylase deficiency, female fetus ... A) D/t decreased testosterone B) Normal external genitalia C) D/t increased DHEA
questions.why: 3-beta HSD: female virilised by DHEA, male undervirilised by low testosterone; 17-alpha hydroxylase: female normal.

questions.q: Which deficiency is described as a 'newly diagnosed form of CAH'?
questions.why: P450 OR deficiency is introduced as a newly diagnosed form of CAH.

questions.q: Fill up: P450 is described as an electron ____ for many enzymes.
questions.why: 'P450: Electron donor for many enzymes'.

questions.q: The skeletal syndrome printed with P450 oxidoreductase deficiency is:
questions.why: Antley-Bixler syndrome is named beside P450 OR deficiency.

questions.q: The example of skeletal abnormality printed under Antley-Bixler syndrome is:
questions.why: 'Skeletal abnormalities (Eg: craniosynostosis)'.

questions.q: True/False: P450 oxidoreductase deficiency produces ambiguous genitalia in females only.
options: True - it spares the male fetus entirely
True - it causes no genital ambiguity at all
questions.why: It is filed under 'male + females' in the summary.

questions.q: Scenario: A newborn has ambiguous genitalia and craniosynostosis. Which enzyme block links both findings?
questions.why: P450 OR deficiency is the block printed with Antley-Bixler skeletal abnormalities.

questions.q: Odd one out - which enzyme block is NOT printed with a fetal-sex genital table on this page?
questions.why: The 21-alpha hydroxylase fetal table is on the CAH page; the 'other causes' page covers the other three.

units.title: Summary of Ambiguous Genitalia by Enzyme Defect

questions.q: Fill up: In the summary table, the most common enzyme causing ambiguous genitalia is ____ hydroxylase.
questions.why: 21-alpha hydroxylase is marked (m/c).

questions.q: The two enzyme defects filed under 'female only' ambiguous genitalia are:
questions.why: The female-only column lists 21-alpha hydroxylase (m/c) and 11-beta hydroxylase.

questions.q: The two defects filed under 'male only' are:
questions.why: The male-only column lists 17-alpha hydroxylase and 17,20 lyase.

questions.q: The two defects filed under 'male + females' are:
questions.why: The combined column lists 3-beta HSD and P450 OR.

questions.q: Match each defect with its summary column - 1) 11-beta hydroxylase 2) 17,20 lyase 3) P450 OR ... A) Male + females B) Female only C) Male only
questions.why: 11-beta is female only; 17,20 lyase is male only; P450 OR affects both.

questions.q: True/False: 21-alpha hydroxylase deficiency appears in the summary under ambiguous genitalia in males only.
options: True - it spares the female fetus
True - it is listed under male + females
questions.why: It heads the female-only column and is marked most common.

questions.q: Which single word marks 21-alpha hydroxylase in the summary?
questions.why: Printed as '21-alpha hydroxylase (m/c)'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which defect is NOT filed under 'female only'?
questions.why: 17-alpha hydroxylase is in the male-only column.

questions.q: Scenario: A 46XX newborn has ambiguous genitalia and a salt-wasting crisis. Which defect best fits the 'female only, most common' entry?
questions.why: 21-alpha hydroxylase is the female-only most common defect and matches the CAH salt-wasting picture earlier in the chapter.

questions.q: Which summary heading covers enzyme defects that virilise the female fetus while undervirilising the male fetus?
questions.why: 3-beta HSD and P450 OR are grouped under 'male + females'.

questions.q: Fill up: In the 46XX tree, Turner's syndrome is the ____ numbered entry under abnormal development of gonads.
questions.why: Ovotestes is 1 and Turner's syndrome is 2.

questions.q: Which two sub-lines are printed beneath Turner's syndrome in the tree?
options: 45XO (m/c) giving streak ovary, and a mosaic arm
45XO giving dysgenetic testis, and a 47XXY arm
46XY giving streak ovaries, and a 45XO arm
questions.why: The tree prints 45XO (m/c) → streak ovary plus the mosaic sub-branch.

questions.q: Fill up: In the mosaic arm, 45XO gives streak ovaries while 46XY gives ____ testes.
questions.why: Printed: '46XY: dysgenetic testes'.

questions.q: In the 46XX ambiguous-genitalia arm, which item is numbered 'a'?
questions.why: 'a. ↑ maternal androgens' heads the ambiguous-genitalia arm.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT printed as a source of raised maternal androgens?
questions.why: Placental aromatase deficiency is a separate numbered item, not a maternal androgen source.

questions.q: Which karyotype is printed as MOST common in the Turner's branch of the 46XX tree?
True/False: The 46XX chapter lists androgen insensitivity syndrome among its causes.
options: True - it is listed under ambiguous genitalia
True - it is the second gonadal cause
questions.why: AIS belongs to the 46XY chapter; the 46XX tree lists ovotestes, Turner's, maternal androgens and aromatase deficiency.

questions.q: Scenario: A virilised 46XX newborn's mother took danazol in early pregnancy. Which printed item covers this?
questions.why: Androgenic drugs is one of the three listed maternal androgen sources.

questions.q: Match each ovotesticular feature with its descriptor - 1) Old term 2) Karyotype order 3) Commonest pattern 4) Side of testis ... A) 46XX > 46XY B) Ovary on one side, testis on the other C) True hermaphrodite D) Male internal genitalia
questions.why: Old term true hermaphrodite; 46XX > 46XY; one ovary and one testis on each side; testis side gives male internal genitalia.

questions.q: Which single pubertal feature is explicitly bracketed as being due to estrogen?
questions.why: 'Gynaecomastia (+) (d/t estrogen)'.

units.title: Adrenal Map and CAH - Second Pass

questions.q: Fill up: The diagram's topmost regulator, ACTH, is shown acting on the ____.
questions.why: ACTH is drawn pointing at the adrenal gland.

questions.q: In the printed diagram, 17-OH progesterone is the substrate for which enzyme on the cortisol route?
questions.why: 17-OH progesterone → 11-deoxycortisol via 21-alpha hydroxylase.

questions.q: Fill up: 11-deoxycortisol is converted to cortisol by ____ hydroxylase.
questions.why: The final glucocorticoid step is 11-beta hydroxylase.

questions.q: Which enzyme is printed on the progesterone-to-deoxycorticosterone arrow?
questions.why: 21-alpha hydroxylase converts progesterone to deoxycorticosterone.

questions.q: True/False: According to the printed map, DHEA is a weaker androgen than testosterone.
options: False - DHEA is described as the stronger androgen
questions.why: DHEA is labelled a weak androgen and testosterone the stronger androgen.

questions.q: Which estrogen label is printed on the aromatase arrow from androstenedione rather than from testosterone?
questions.why: Androstenedione aromatises to E1; testosterone aromatises to E2.

questions.q: Odd one out - which steroid is NOT an end-product of the printed adrenal map?
questions.why: DHT requires peripheral 5-alpha reductase and is not in this adrenal map.

questions.q: Scenario: A 46XX neonate has ambiguous genitalia, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and hypoglycaemia. Which single enzyme block explains all of these?
questions.why: 3-beta HSD deficiency lowers aldosterone (hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia), lowers cortisol (hypoglycaemia) and virilises the female fetus via DHEA.

questions.q: Which of the five named enzyme blocks is marked as most common?
questions.why: 21-alpha hydroxylase carries the (m/c) tag in the summary.

questions.q: Fill up: The summary table's three column heads are female only, male only and male ____ females.
questions.why: The third column is headed 'male + females'.

questions.q: Match the 17-OH progesterone band with its interpretation - 1) Less than 200 ng 2) 200 to 800 ng 3) 800 ng or more ... A) Confirm CAH B) ACTH stimulation test C) Rule out CAH
questions.why: Below 200 rules out; the middle band goes to stimulation testing; 800 and above confirms.

questions.q: Which drug class is named second in the emergency list, after glucocorticoids?
questions.why: Step 2 is mineralocorticoids.

questions.q: Why is the neonate with ambiguous genitalia and impalpable gonads labelled a medical emergency?
options: They have an intra-abdominal testis at high malignant risk
They require urgent karyotyping before feeds
They are presumed to have CAH with a salt-wasting crisis
questions.why: The gonads-not-palpable arm routes to CAH and emergency glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement.

questions.q: Fill up: Antenatal dexamethasone is continued only when CVS shows an affected ____ fetus.
questions.why: 'Affected female fetus → Continue dexamethasone'.

questions.q: Which sampling window makes CVS usable before the maximum dexamethasone delay lapses?
options: 10 to 11 weeks, just after the 9-week maximum delay
questions.why: Dexamethasone must start by 9 weeks and CVS is done at 10-11 weeks.

questions.q: True/False: 3-beta HSD deficiency causes ambiguous genitalia exclusively in 46XX fetuses.
options: True - it is filed under female only
questions.why: It is filed under 'male + females'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which enzyme block is paired with a named skeletal syndrome?
questions.why: Only P450 OR deficiency is printed with Antley-Bixler syndrome.

questions.q: Scenario: A 46XY newborn has ambiguous genitalia; the 46XX sibling is entirely normal. Which defect fits the printed 'male only' column?
questions.why: The male-only column lists 17-alpha hydroxylase and 17,20 lyase deficiency.

questions.q: Which enzyme block explicitly prints the phrase 'Leads to DSD in XY individuals'?
questions.why: That sentence heads the 17-alpha hydroxylase / 17,20 lyase block.

questions.q: The 46XY DSD page divides its causes into two columns headed by the appearance of the external genitalia. Which pair?
options: Male external genitalia and ambiguous genitalia
Female external genitalia and male external genitalia
Female external genitalia and ambiguous genitalia
questions.why: Page 165 opens with 'Female external genitalia :' and 'Ambiguous genitalia :'.

questions.q: Which disorder heads the 'female external genitalia' column?
questions.why: AIS is the first entry and is marked (m/c).

questions.q: Fill up: In the 46XY tree, AIS is annotated as ____ (most common).
questions.why: The entry reads '(AIS) : m/c'.

questions.q: How many causes are printed in the 'female external genitalia' column?
questions.why: Complete AIS, Swyer's syndrome, 5-alpha reductase deficiency and LH receptor defect.

questions.q: The third cause printed in the female-external-genitalia column is:
questions.why: The order is complete AIS, Swyer's syndrome, 5-alpha reductase deficiency, LH receptor defect.

questions.q: The fourth cause in the female-external-genitalia column is:
questions.why: LH receptor defect is numbered 4.

questions.q: Match each female-external-genitalia cause with its printed rank - 1) Complete AIS 2) Swyer's syndrome 3) 5-alpha reductase deficiency 4) LH receptor defect ... A) 3 B) 1 C) 4 D) 2
questions.why: Printed order: 1 complete AIS, 2 Swyer's, 3 5-alpha reductase deficiency, 4 LH receptor defect.

questions.q: Which two disorders head the 'ambiguous genitalia' column?
questions.why: The ambiguous column opens with 1. Partial AIS, 2. Ovotestis, then CAH variants.

questions.q: Fill up: The ambiguous-genitalia column groups four enzyme defects under the heading congenital ____ hyperplasia.
questions.why: The heading reads 'Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH)'.

questions.q: Which four enzyme defects are grouped under CAH in the 46XY ambiguous-genitalia column?
options: 21-alpha hydroxylase, 11-beta hydroxylase, 3-beta HSD and P450 OR
3-beta HSD, P450 OR, 5-alpha reductase and aromatase
17-alpha hydroxylase, 17-alpha lyase, 3-beta HSD and P450 oxidoreductase
questions.why: The four listed sub-bullets are 17-alpha hydroxylase, 17-alpha lyase, 3-beta HSD and P450 OR deficiency.

questions.q: True/False: 21-alpha hydroxylase deficiency appears in the 46XY ambiguous-genitalia list.
options: True - it is listed under female external genitalia
questions.why: It is absent; the CAH sub-list here has only 17-alpha hydroxylase, 17-alpha lyase, 3-beta HSD and P450 OR.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is filed under 'ambiguous genitalia' rather than 'female external genitalia'?
questions.why: Ovotestis is the second entry of the ambiguous column; the other three are in the female-external-genitalia column.

questions.q: Scenario: A 46XY infant is born with completely female-looking external genitalia. Which column of the printed tree should be searched first?
questions.why: Complete AIS, Swyer's, 5-alpha reductase deficiency and LH receptor defect sit in the female-external-genitalia column.

questions.q: Fill up: The page heading reads '46 XY DSD (Disorders of Sexual ____)'.
questions.why: The printed title expands DSD as Disorders of Sexual Development.

units.title: Shared Characteristics and the Inguinal Hernia Clue

questions.q: Which single 46XY DSD is the stated exception to the rule that these children are considered female at birth?
questions.why: 'Considered as female child at birth - Except: Ovotestis'.

questions.q: Fill up: The presenting complaint common to these patients is ____ amenorrhoea at puberty.
questions.why: 'Complaints of: 1. 1° Amenorrhea at puberty'.

questions.q: A female with primary amenorrhoea and a complaint of inguinal hernia should raise suspicion of which karyotype?
questions.why: 'Female with 1° Amenorrhea + C/o Inguinal hernia: Suspect XY genotype'.

questions.q: Bilateral inguinal hernia in this context points to:
questions.why: 'B/L Inguinal hernia → Undescended testis'.

questions.q: Where are the abdominal gonads detected?
