questions.why: 'Abdominal gonads: Palpable on physical examination'.

questions.q: Fill up: Undescended testis in 46XY DSD carries an increased risk of ____.
questions.why: Printed: '↑ Risk of malignancy'.

questions.q: The treatment recommended for the undescended testis is:
questions.why: 'Rx: Gonadectomy'.

questions.q: The most common tumour associated with an undescended testis is:
questions.why: Printed: 'm/c tumor associated with undescended testis: Gonadoblastoma'.

questions.q: The most common malignancy associated with an undescended testis is:
questions.why: Printed: 'm/c malignancy associated with undescended testis: Dysgerminoma'.

questions.q: Match the label with the lesion - 1) m/c tumour 2) m/c malignancy ... A) Dysgerminoma B) Gonadoblastoma
questions.why: Gonadoblastoma is the commonest tumour; dysgerminoma the commonest malignancy.

questions.q: Scenario: A 16-year-old girl with primary amenorrhoea is found to have bilateral inguinal swellings that are palpable testes. What is the definitive management of those gonads?
questions.why: The printed Rx for the undescended testis in 46XY DSD is gonadectomy because of malignancy risk.

questions.q: True/False: The risk quoted for these abdominal gonads is benign degeneration, so removal is optional.
options: True - removal is deferred to age 40
True - only if the tumour marker rises
questions.why: There is an increased risk of malignancy and gonadectomy is the recommended treatment.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT printed as a shared characteristic of 46XY DSD?
options: Virilisation at birth in every case
questions.why: Virilisation at birth is not universal; the page stresses they are considered female at birth (except ovotestis).

questions.q: Fill up: Complete AIS is described as an ____ linked recessive disorder.
questions.why: The printed line is 'X linked recessive disorder'.

questions.q: In complete AIS, the SRY gene status is:
questions.why: 'SRY gene: N'.

questions.q: Which four structures are all marked 'N' (normal) at the top of the complete AIS diagram?
options: SRY gene, ovary, Leydig cells and granulosa cells
Testis, epididymis, vas deferens and seminal vesicle
SRY gene, testis, Mullerian duct and Wolffian duct
SRY gene, testis, Leydig cells and Sertoli cells
questions.why: The diagram marks SRY gene N, testis N, Leydig cells N and Sertoli cells N.

questions.q: The testis in complete AIS produces testosterone that is:
options: Normal in amount but the body is resistant to it
questions.why: 'Testosterone: N but Resistant to testosterone'.

questions.q: Fill up: Sertoli cells are stimulated by ____, which is itself normal in AIS.
questions.why: 'FSH (+)' drives Sertoli cells; 'FSH: N'.

questions.q: Sertoli cells secrete inhibin B, which does what to FSH?
questions.why: 'Inhibin B → -ve feedback on FSH'.

questions.q: The second Sertoli cell product named is Anti-Mullerian Hormone. Its action is:
questions.why: 'Antimullerian hormone → Regression of mullerian duct'.

questions.q: Fill up: Because AMH acts normally, patients with complete AIS have no fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix or ____ vagina.
questions.why: 'No fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, upper vagina'.

questions.q: Resistance to testosterone causes the Wolffian duct to:
options: Fail to grow and then regress
questions.why: 'Resistance to testosterone → Wolffian duct does not grow → Wolffian duct regresses'.

questions.q: Failure of scrotal descent in complete AIS leaves the testis:
questions.why: 'Failure of scrotal descent → Abdominal testis'.

questions.q: Which two consequences are printed next to the abdominal testis?
options: Increased chance of malignancy and bilateral inguinal hernia
questions.why: Printed: '↑ Chance of malignancy' and 'B/L inguinal hernia'.

questions.q: Fill up: Testosterone is normally converted to DHT by ____ reductase; AIS patients are resistant to both.
questions.why: The diagram shows 'Testosterone --5α reductase--> DHT' with 'Resistant to DHT'.

questions.q: Resistance to DHT produces:
options: Failure of masculinisation of the external genitalia
questions.why: 'Resistant to DHT → Failure of masculanisation of external genitalia'.

questions.q: The net genital outcome in complete AIS is:
options: Female external genitalia, female at birth
questions.why: The chain ends in 'Female external genitalia → Female at birth'.

questions.q: At puberty, testicular testosterone fails to produce secondary sexual development, giving pubic and axillary hair at Tanner stage:
questions.why: 'Scanty pubic hair / axillary hair: Tanner stage 1 or 2' and 'Failure of 2° sexual development'.

questions.q: Why does breast development still occur in complete AIS?
options: Estrogen is produced by the adrenal gland
Testosterone is aromatised to estrogen and estrogen is not resisted
questions.why: The diagram shows 'Testosterone --Aromatase--> Estrogen (Not resistant)' leading to proper breast development.

questions.q: Breast development in complete AIS reaches Tanner stage:
questions.why: 'Breast development (Proper): Tanner stage 4 or 5'.

questions.q: Fill up: AIS patients may have a ____ ending vagina.
questions.why: 'may have blind ending vagina'.

questions.q: Match each AIS finding with its mechanism - 1) No uterus 2) No vas deferens 3) Female external genitalia 4) Breast development ... A) Estrogen not resisted B) AMH acted normally C) Wolffian duct regressed D) DHT resisted
questions.why: AMH removes the uterus; testosterone resistance regresses the Wolffian duct; DHT resistance feminises the exterior; unopposed estrogen builds breast.

questions.q: Scenario: A 17-year-old with well-developed breasts, scanty axillary hair, no menarche and a blind-ending vagina. Which internal anatomy is expected?
options: No uterus, no fallopian tubes, no upper vagina
questions.why: AMH works in AIS, so Mullerian structures are absent; the vagina is blind-ending.

questions.q: True/False: In complete AIS, the external genitalia are ambiguous.
questions.why: Complete AIS gives female external genitalia; ambiguity belongs to partial AIS.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a consequence of androgen receptor resistance in complete AIS?
options: Absent masculinisation of the external genitalia
questions.why: Mullerian regression is driven by AMH, not by the androgen receptor.

questions.q: Fill up: GnRH is ____ in AIS because negative feedback is lost.
questions.why: The hormonal profile block prints '↑ GnRH' with 'loss of negative feedback on GnRH'.

questions.q: Which gonadotrophin is raised and which is normal in AIS?
questions.why: The inference line reads '↑ LH, (N) FSH'.

questions.q: Testosterone in AIS, compared with females, is:
questions.why: 'Testosterone: ↑ (Compared to Females)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The Sertoli cell marker printed in the profile is inhibin ____.
questions.why: Inhibin B is listed in the profile.

questions.q: The same 'raised LH with normal FSH' pattern is printed alongside which other diagnosis?
questions.why: The inference compares AIS with PCOS.

questions.q: How does the menstrual presentation differ between AIS and PCOS in this comparison?
options: AIS gives secondary amenorrhoea, PCOS primary
AIS gives primary amenorrhoea, PCOS gives secondary amenorrhoea
questions.why: The two columns read '1° Amenorrhea' (AIS) and '2° Amenorrhea' (PCOS).

questions.q: Fill up: The comparison labels AIS with 1° amenorrhoea and PCOS with ____ amenorrhoea.
questions.why: PCOS is printed under 2° amenorrhoea.

questions.q: Match the hormone to its printed direction in AIS - 1) GnRH 2) LH 3) FSH 4) Testosterone ... A) Normal B) Raised
questions.why: GnRH, LH and testosterone are raised; FSH is normal.

questions.q: Scenario: A phenotypic woman with primary amenorrhoea has LH 18 IU/L, FSH 5 IU/L and testosterone in the male range. Which diagnosis does the printed inference support?
questions.why: Raised LH, normal FSH and male-range testosterone with primary amenorrhoea is the AIS pattern.

questions.q: True/False: The AIS hormonal profile shows a suppressed GnRH from androgen excess.
options: True - GnRH falls with androgen feedback
questions.why: Androgen resistance removes feedback, so GnRH is raised.

questions.q: The first management instruction printed is to:
questions.why: 'Continue identity of female'.

questions.q: Fill up: Gonadectomy of the intra-abdominal testis is timed after completion of breast development, at ____ years.
questions.why: Printed: 'After breast development completion (14 to 16 yrs)'.

questions.q: Why is gonadectomy deferred rather than done in infancy in complete AIS?
options: The testis is needed for growth spurts
The testis provides testosterone that is aromatised for breast development
Anaesthetic risk in infancy is prohibitive
The diagnosis cannot be made earlier
questions.why: Pubertal oestrogen comes from aromatised testicular testosterone, so removal waits until breast development completes.

questions.q: Fill up: Estrogen replacement therapy is given, but ____ is not supplemented because the uterus is absent.
questions.why: 'Progesterone: Not supplemented d/t absent uterus'.

questions.q: Vaginoplasty in AIS is timed:
questions.why: 'Vaginoplasty - Just before/after marriage'.

questions.q: Which vaginoplasty technique is described as laparoscopic?
questions.why: 'Vecchietti technique: Laparoscopic'.

questions.q: The first named vaginoplasty technique is:
questions.why: '1. McIndoe vaginoplasty'.

questions.q: Can a woman with complete AIS have a biological child?
questions.why: Printed note: 'Complete AIS cannot have biological child'.

questions.q: Match each management step with its timing - 1) Gonadectomy 2) Vaginoplasty 3) Estrogen replacement 4) Continue female identity ... A) Just before/after marriage B) Immediately C) After thelarche, 14-16 yrs D) After gonadectomy
questions.why: Identity is continued from the outset; gonadectomy at 14-16 years; estrogen after it; vaginoplasty around marriage.

questions.q: Scenario: A 15-year-old with complete AIS has just completed breast development. What is the next step?
questions.why: Gonadectomy is scheduled once breast development completes at 14-16 years.

questions.q: True/False: Progesterone is added to the estrogen regimen in complete AIS to mimic a normal cycle.
options: True - it protects the vaginal remnant
questions.why: Progesterone is not supplemented because there is no uterus.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT part of printed complete AIS management?
questions.why: Testosterone is already high and resisted; it is never supplemented.

questions.q: Fill up: In partial AIS, males are ____ sensitive to androgens.
questions.why: Printed: 'males are partially sensitive to androgens'.

questions.q: In partial AIS, testosterone acting through a partially functional receptor allows the Wolffian duct to:
questions.why: 'Wolffian duct develops'.

questions.q: Fill up: Partial sensitivity to DHT gives ____ male internal genital organs.
questions.why: 'DHT (Partial sensitivity) → Poorly formed of male internal genital organ'.

questions.q: The genital appearance at birth in partial AIS is:
questions.why: 'Ambiguous genitalia'.

questions.q: How are partial AIS infants registered at birth?
questions.why: 'Females at birth'.

questions.q: Why does partial AIS present with primary amenorrhoea?
questions.why: '1° Amenorrhea d/t absent uterus'.

questions.q: Breast development in partial AIS reaches Tanner stage:
questions.why: 'Breast: Tanner 4/5'.

questions.q: Pubic and axillary hair in partial AIS reaches Tanner stage:
questions.why: 'Pubic & axillary hair: Tanner 1 or 2'.

questions.q: Which two local findings are printed together as features of partial AIS?
questions.why: 'Clitoromegaly / Labioscrotal fusion'.

questions.q: Fill up: Partial AIS is the most common cause of ambiguous genitalia in ____ individuals.
questions.why: Printed: 'm/c cause of ambiguous genitalia in 46 XY'.

questions.q: Partial AIS is also described as the most common cause of:
questions.why: 'm/c cause of male pseudohermaphrodite'.

questions.q: How does the management of partial AIS differ from complete AIS regarding the gonads?
options: Gonadectomy is done as soon as possible
The testes are left in place
questions.why: 'Same as AIS. Gonadectomy as soon as possible'.

questions.q: Why is early gonadectomy advised in partial AIS?
options: The testis is prone to torsion
The testis blocks the inguinal canal
questions.why: The arrow reads 'Testis → Testosterone → Virilisation at puberty'.

questions.q: Match the partial AIS feature with its description - 1) Breast 2) Pubic hair 3) Internal genitalia 4) External genitalia ... A) Poorly formed male B) Ambiguous C) Tanner 4/5 D) Tanner 1 or 2
questions.why: Breast Tanner 4/5, pubic hair Tanner 1-2, poorly formed male internal genitalia, ambiguous external genitalia.

questions.q: Scenario: A child reared female presents at 14 with clitoromegaly present since birth, Tanner 4 breasts, scanty pubic hair and no uterus. Which diagnosis fits?
questions.why: Clitoromegaly present since birth with good breast development and absent uterus is the partial AIS picture.

questions.q: True/False: In partial AIS the internal genitalia are fully formed male structures.
questions.why: They are described as poorly formed male internal genitalia.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed feature of partial AIS?
questions.why: Breasts develop to Tanner 4/5 in partial AIS.

questions.q: Fill up: Swyer syndrome has a ____ karyotype with dysgenetic testes.
questions.why: The block prints '46 XY' with 'Gonads: Testis, Dysgenetic'.

questions.q: How many causes of the dysgenetic gonad are printed?
questions.why: Causes: 1. Idiopathic, 2. Point mutation of SRY gene.

questions.q: Which gene is named in the second cause of Swyer syndrome?
questions.why: 'Point mutation of SRY gene'.

questions.q: Fill up: The first listed cause of Swyer syndrome is ____.
questions.why: '1. Idiopathic'.

questions.q: Both Leydig and Sertoli cells are described as:
questions.why: Printed: 'Leydig cells (Dysgenetic)' and 'Sertoli cells (Dysgenetic)'.

questions.q: Absent testosterone in Swyer syndrome leads to failure of:
questions.why: 'Absent testosterone → Failure of Wolffian duct development; male internal genitalia absent'.

questions.q: Absent AMH in Swyer syndrome results in:
options: Mullerian duct formation and female internal genitalia
questions.why: 'Absent AMH → Mullerian duct formation → Female internal genitalia'.

questions.q: Fill up: Absent inhibin B removes negative feedback on GnRH, so ____ rises.
questions.why: 'Absent inhibin B → Absent -ve feedback on GnRH → ↑ FSH'.

questions.q: Absent DHT in Swyer syndrome gives:
questions.why: 'Absent DHT → Female external genitalia'.

questions.q: How is a child with Swyer syndrome registered at birth?
questions.why: 'Female child at birth'.

questions.q: Match the absent hormone with its consequence in Swyer syndrome - 1) Testosterone 2) AMH 3) DHT 4) Inhibin B ... A) Female external genitalia B) Female internal genitalia C) Male internal genitalia absent D) Raised FSH
questions.why: No testosterone means no Wolffian derivatives; no AMH means Mullerian structures persist; no DHT means female exterior; no inhibin B means unopposed FSH.

questions.q: At puberty in Swyer syndrome, absent testosterone causes failure of female secondary sexual characteristics, specifically:
questions.why: 'Failure of female 2° sexual characteristics formation: Absent breast'.

questions.q: Pubic and axillary hair in Swyer syndrome is:
questions.why: 'Pubic hair & axillary hair: Scanty'.

questions.q: Which three presentations are printed for Swyer syndrome?
options: Delayed puberty, primary amenorrhoea and bilateral inguinal hernia
Bilateral inguinal hernia, virilisation and acne
questions.why: The presentation list is delayed puberty, 1° amenorrhoea and B/L inguinal hernia.

questions.q: Fill up: Gonadectomy in Swyer syndrome is advised ____ diagnosed, unlike in complete AIS.
questions.why: 'Gonadectomy: As soon as diagnosed'.

questions.q: Estrogen supplementation is given for how long to achieve breast development?
questions.why: 'Estrogen supplementation - For 1 year → Breast development'.

questions.q: Which additional procedure is listed after estrogen in Swyer management?
questions.why: Vaginoplasty is the final listed step.

questions.q: Scenario: A 17-year-old with primary amenorrhoea, absent breast development, scanty pubic hair, a 46XY karyotype and bilateral inguinal gonads. Which diagnosis?
questions.why: 46XY with absent breast development and dysgenetic gonads presenting as inguinal hernias is Swyer syndrome.

questions.q: True/False: In Swyer syndrome the uterus is absent because AMH is produced normally.
options: True - AMH is only partly reduced
True - the uterus is hypoplastic instead
questions.why: AMH is absent, so Mullerian structures including the uterus form.

questions.q: Odd one out - which finding would argue AGAINST Swyer syndrome?
options: Well-developed breasts at Tanner 5 without estrogen therapy
questions.why: Swyer patients lack endogenous estrogen, so breasts do not develop without supplementation.

questions.q: Fill up: 5-alpha reductase deficiency occurs in a ____ individual with normally formed testes.
questions.why: The block prints '46 XY' with 'Gonads: Testis (N)'.

questions.q: Which two testicular cell types are explicitly labelled normal in this condition?
questions.why: 'Sertoli cells (N)' and 'Leydig cells (N)'.

questions.q: Testosterone acts normally on the Wolffian duct to produce:
questions.why: 'Testosterone → Wolffian duct development → male internal genital organ'.

questions.q: AMH acts normally to:
questions.why: 'AMH → Mullerian duct regress'.

questions.q: Fill up: The defect is the failure of conversion of testosterone to ____.
questions.why: 'Defect: Testosterone --5α reductase--> DHT' is blocked.

questions.q: Because DHT is absent, the external genitalia at birth are:
questions.why: 'Female external genital organs → Female at birth'.

questions.q: At puberty, normal testosterone produces which two male secondary sexual characteristics?
options: Increased muscle mass and deepening of voice
questions.why: 'male 2° sexual characteristics: ↑ muscle mass, Deepening of voice'.

questions.q: Fill up: Absence of DHT means pubic and axillary hair are ____.
questions.why: 'Absent pubic or axillary hair: d/t absent DHT'.

questions.q: Breast development in 5-alpha reductase deficiency is:
questions.why: 'Absent breast development'.

questions.q: Which virilising event occurs at puberty in this condition?
questions.why: Under 'Virilisation': 'Clitoromegaly at puberty'.

questions.q: The printed note contrasts this condition with AIS by stating that in AIS:
questions.why: 'Note: In AIS: Testosterone → Estrogen'.

questions.q: Why do AIS patients develop breasts while 5-alpha reductase deficient patients do not?
options: In AIS, unopposed testosterone is aromatised to estrogen; in 5-alpha reductase deficiency testosterone drives virilisation instead
In AIS the ovaries are present
In 5-alpha reductase deficiency estrogen is destroyed
questions.why: The note attributes AIS breast development to testosterone-to-estrogen conversion, which does not produce the same effect here where testosterone acts as an androgen.

questions.q: Match the timing of clitoromegaly - 1) Partial AIS 2) 5-alpha reductase deficiency ... A) Puberty B) Since birth
questions.why: Partial AIS is since birth; 5-alpha reductase deficiency is at puberty.

questions.q: Match the breast finding - 1) Partial AIS 2) 5-alpha reductase deficiency ... A) Absent B) Tanner 4/5
questions.why: Partial AIS has Tanner 4/5 breasts; 5-alpha reductase deficiency has none.

questions.q: Match the internal genitalia - 1) Partial AIS 2) 5-alpha reductase deficiency ... A) Fully formed male genitalia B) Poorly formed male genitalia
questions.why: Partial AIS has poorly formed male internal genitalia; 5-alpha reductase deficiency has fully formed ones.

questions.q: How many rows does the printed partial AIS versus 5-alpha reductase deficiency comparison table have?
questions.why: The rows are time of clitoromegaly, breast and internal genitalia.

questions.q: Scenario: A child reared female develops clitoromegaly, increased muscle mass and voice deepening at puberty, but has no pubic hair and no breasts. Karyotype 46XY. What is the diagnosis?
questions.why: Pubertal virilisation with absent pubic hair and absent breasts in a 46XY patient is the 5-alpha reductase deficiency picture.

questions.q: True/False: In 5-alpha reductase deficiency the internal genitalia are poorly formed male structures.
questions.why: Wolffian development proceeds normally, giving fully formed male internal genitalia.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is a partial AIS feature rather than a 5-alpha reductase deficiency feature?
questions.why: Since-birth clitoromegaly belongs to partial AIS; the other three belong to 5-alpha reductase deficiency.

questions.q: Which 46XY DSD is the only one in the tree that is shared with the 46XX chapter?
questions.why: Ovotestis appeared in the 46XX chapter and reappears here under ambiguous genitalia.

questions.q: Fill up: The exception clause states that all 46XY DSD children are considered female at birth except ____.
questions.why: The printed exception names ovotestis.

questions.q: Which investigation would confirm the suspected XY genotype in a female with primary amenorrhoea and inguinal hernia?
questions.why: The chapter on ambiguous genitalia names karyotyping as the investigation of choice for suspected XY genotype.

questions.q: Fill up: Complete AIS is a receptor problem: the androgen ____ does not respond.
questions.why: The heading 'Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome' with 'resistant to testosterone' localises the defect to the receptor.

questions.q: The page prints a heading 'Location:' immediately before 'COMPLETE AIS' and 'X linked recessive disorder'. What is the location implied by the mechanism?
questions.why: The AIS block is a receptor-level defect; the location line precedes the genetics note.

questions.q: Which two hormones are produced normally by the Sertoli cells in complete AIS?
questions.why: Sertoli cells give inhibin B and AMH; testosterone comes from Leydig cells.

questions.q: Fill up: LH in complete AIS is ____ because of loss of negative feedback.
questions.why: The hormonal profile shows raised LH from lost androgen feedback.

questions.q: Why does FSH stay normal in complete AIS when LH rises?
options: FSH is not under hypothalamic control
Inhibin B from Sertoli cells still feeds back on FSH
questions.why: Intact Sertoli inhibin B keeps FSH in the normal range while androgen resistance raises LH.

questions.q: Scenario: A 46XY patient with complete AIS asks whether she can carry a pregnancy with IVF. What is the printed answer?
options: Yes, with donor oocytes and surrogacy
No - she cannot have a biological child
Yes, with gestational carrier and her own oocytes
questions.why: The printed note states complete AIS cannot have a biological child.

questions.q: Which vaginoplasty timing applies equally to complete AIS and Swyer syndrome?
questions.why: Both pages time vaginoplasty around marriage.

units.title: Second Pass - Swyer, 5-alpha Reductase and Comparisons

questions.q: Fill up: Swyer syndrome is also termed 46XY complete ____ dysgenesis.
questions.why: The condition is a dysgenetic-gonad form of gonadal dysgenesis with a 46XY karyotype.

questions.q: Which malignancy risk is printed for the intra-abdominal testis in complete AIS?
questions.why: '↑ Chance of malignancy' is printed beside the abdominal testis.

questions.q: Fill up: In Swyer syndrome, both LH and ____ are raised because of absent feedback.
questions.why: Absent inhibin B and absent sex steroids raise both gonadotrophins.

questions.q: Complete AIS management defers gonadectomy while Swyer management does it immediately. What is the reason for the difference?
options: Swyer patients are older at diagnosis
In AIS the testis supplies aromatisable testosterone for breast development; in Swyer the gonad is dysgenetic and malignant
questions.why: Functional AIS testes are kept until breast development completes; dysgenetic Swyer gonads are removed at diagnosis.

questions.q: Which two vaginoplasty techniques are named across this chapter?
questions.why: McIndoe vaginoplasty and the laparoscopic Vecchietti technique are the two named.

questions.q: Fill up: In 5-alpha reductase deficiency, the external genitalia are female at birth but ____ at puberty.
questions.why: Pubertal testosterone causes virilisation, notably clitoromegaly.

questions.q: Which single feature separates 5-alpha reductase deficiency from complete AIS at puberty?
options: Presence of virilisation and absent breasts
Presence of breasts and absent pubic hair
questions.why: 5-alpha reductase deficiency virilises without breast development; complete AIS does the opposite.

questions.q: True/False: Both complete AIS and Swyer syndrome present with primary amenorrhoea and are reared female.
options: False - Swyer patients are reared male
questions.why: Both appear in the female-external-genitalia column and both present with primary amenorrhoea.

questions.q: Match each 46XY DSD with its internal genitalia - 1) Complete AIS 2) Partial AIS 3) Swyer syndrome 4) 5-alpha reductase deficiency ... A) Female internal genitalia B) None C) Poorly formed male D) Fully formed male
questions.why: AMH removes Mullerian structures in AIS and 5-ARD; absent AMH in Swyer leaves female organs; partial AIS gives poorly formed male organs.

questions.q: Scenario: An infant with ambiguous genitalia is 46XY with palpable inguinal gonads. Which investigation choice makes the specific diagnosis rather than only the genetic sex?
options: Karyotyping plus hormonal profiling of LH, FSH and testosterone
questions.why: Karyotype establishes 46XY and the LH/FSH/testosterone pattern separates AIS from the enzyme defects in this chapter.

questions.q: Odd one out - which 46XY DSD is NOT driven by a hormone-synthesis enzyme defect?
questions.why: AIS is a receptor defect; the other three are CAH enzyme blocks.

questions.q: Fill up: Primary amenorrhoea is defined as not having menstruated ____ years after thelarche.
questions.why: Page 171 prints '>= 3 years' after thelarche with 'not menstruated'.

questions.q: The clock for the definition starts at:
questions.why: The diagram anchors the 3-year interval to thelarche.

questions.q: According to the printed Tanner staging note, breast budding is stage:
questions.why: 'Breast budding: Stage 2'.

questions.q: Fill up: The note also states that hair on the mons pubis is Tanner stage ____.
questions.why: 'Hair on mons pubis: Stage 3'.

questions.q: True/False: The definition uses a fixed chronological age rather than an interval from thelarche.
options: True - the age used is 16 years
True - the age used is 14 years
questions.why: The page uses an interval of at least 3 years from thelarche.

questions.q: Scenario: A girl had thelarche at 11 and is now 13 and 6 months with no periods. Does she meet the printed definition?
options: No - only 2.5 years have elapsed since thelarche
Yes - any girl over 13 without periods qualifies
questions.why: The threshold is at least 3 years after thelarche; 2.5 years does not meet it.

questions.q: Odd one out - which anchor is NOT used in the printed definition?
questions.why: The definition is built from thelarche, a 3-year interval and absence of menstruation.

units.title: Most Common Causes - Overall and in India

questions.q: The most common cause of primary amenorrhoea overall is:
questions.why: Overall m/c cause: gonadal dysgenesis (Turner's syndrome > Swyer syndrome).

questions.q: Within gonadal dysgenesis, the printed order of frequency overall is:
options: Swyer syndrome more than Turner's syndrome
Turner's syndrome more than Swyer syndrome
questions.why: 'Gonadal dysgenesis (Turner's syndrome > Swyer syndrome)'.

questions.q: The most common cause of primary amenorrhoea in India is:
questions.why: India: Mullerian agenesis.

questions.q: Fill up: In India, within gonadal dysgenesis the printed order is Swyer's ____ Turner's.
questions.why: India column: 'Gonadal dysgenesis (Swyer's > Turner's)'.

questions.q: Match the region with its most common cause - 1) Overall 2) India ... A) Mullerian agenesis B) Gonadal dysgenesis
questions.why: Overall it is gonadal dysgenesis; in India it is Mullerian agenesis.

questions.q: Which pair of statements about gonadal dysgenesis is printed?
options: Overall Turner's exceeds Swyer's; in India Swyer's exceeds Turner's
The two are equal in both
questions.why: The two columns reverse the order of Turner's and Swyer's.

questions.q: True/False: Mullerian agenesis is the most common cause of primary amenorrhoea worldwide.
options: True - it is the most common overall and in India
questions.why: Overall the most common is gonadal dysgenesis; Mullerian agenesis leads only in India.

questions.q: Scenario: An Indian adolescent presents with primary amenorrhoea. Which single diagnosis is statistically most likely per this page?
questions.why: India's most common cause is Mullerian agenesis.

units.title: Organic Causes by Organ and Hormone Pattern

questions.q: The organic causes table lists which organ first?
questions.why: The table begins with hypothalamus.

questions.q: Which two hypothalamic causes are printed?
questions.why: The hypothalamus row lists Kallmann syndrome and craniopharyngioma.

questions.q: Fill up: Hypothalamic causes produce a ____ hypogonadism with low LH, low FSH and low estrogen.
questions.why: '↓ LH, ↓ FSH, ↓ E: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism'.

questions.q: Which karyotype is printed as the most common gonadal dysgenesis?
questions.why: '- 45XO (Turner's syndrome): m/c'.

questions.q: The three gonadal dysgenesis karyotypes printed are:
questions.why: Turner's (45XO), Swyer (46XY) and pure gonadal dysgenesis (46XX).

questions.q: Fill up: The 46XX form of gonadal dysgenesis is called ____ gonadal dysgenesis.
questions.why: '- 46XX (Pure gonadal dysgenesis)'.

questions.q: Gonadal dysgenesis produces which hormonal picture?
options: Raised LH, raised FSH and low estrogen
Low LH, low FSH and low estrogen
Raised LH, normal FSH, normal estrogen
questions.why: '↑ LH, ↑ FSH, ↓ E (Testosterone ↓): Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism'.

questions.q: Fill up: Which hormone is specifically noted as decreased alongside estrogen in gonadal dysgenesis?
questions.why: Printed: '↓ E (Testosterone ↓)'.

questions.q: The uterine column lists Mullerian agenesis with which hormonal pattern?
options: LH, FSH and estrogen all normal
questions.why: 'Mullerian agenesis: LH, FSH, E: Normal'.

questions.q: The second entry in the uterine column is androgen insensitivity syndrome, with:
options: Low LH, low FSH and low estrogen
Raised LH, normal FSH and male levels of testosterone
questions.why: 'AIS: LH ↑, FSH normal; Testosterone: male levels'.

questions.q: Match the organ with its hormonal signature - 1) Hypothalamus 2) Ovary 3) Uterus (Mullerian agenesis) 4) Uterus (AIS) ... A) Normal LH, FSH, E B) Raised LH, normal FSH, male testosterone C) Low LH, low FSH, low E D) Raised LH, raised FSH, low E
questions.why: Hypothalamic causes are hypogonadotropic; gonadal dysgenesis hypergonadotropic; Mullerian agenesis normal; AIS has raised LH with male testosterone.

questions.q: Which single word describes the gonadal dysgenesis hormone state?
questions.why: The ovary row labels it hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.

questions.q: Scenario: A 16-year-old with primary amenorrhoea has FSH 62 IU/L and LH 48 IU/L with low estradiol. Which organ level is involved?
questions.why: Raised gonadotrophins with low estrogen is the hypergonadotropic pattern of gonadal dysgenesis.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT printed in the organic causes table?
questions.why: Prolactinoma does not appear; the pituitary row is represented by craniopharyngioma in the printed grouping.

questions.q: True/False: Cryptomenorrhoea appears in the organic causes-by-organ table on this page.
options: True - it is listed under uterus
True - it is listed under outflow tract
questions.why: Cryptomenorrhoea is dealt with later under conditions in the presence of a uterus.

questions.q: Which three conditions are grouped under 'uterus present'?
options: Mullerian agenesis, AIS and gonadal dysgenesis
Kallmann syndrome, AIS and gonadal dysgenesis
Mullerian agenesis, cryptomenorrhoea and Kallmann syndrome
questions.why: The uterus(+) column lists Kallmann syndrome and cryptomenorrhoea.

questions.q: Fill up: The uterus-negative column contains Mullerian agenesis, AIS and ____ dysgenesis.
questions.why: 'Uterus (-): Mullerian agenesis (46XX), AIS (46XY), Gonadal dysgenesis'.

questions.q: Which karyotype is printed beside Mullerian agenesis in the uterus-negative column?
questions.why: 'Mullerian agenesis (46xx)'.

questions.q: Fill up: In the same column, AIS is annotated as ____.
questions.why: 'AIS (46Xy)'.

questions.q: The axis drawn on this page runs hypothalamus to anterior pituitary to ovary to uterus via which two pituitary hormones?
questions.why: The diagram shows GnRH to anterior pituitary, then FSH and LH acting on the ovary, then estrogen and progesterone reaching the uterus.

questions.q: Which two ovarian hormones are shown acting on the uterus in the printed axis?
questions.why: The axis ends with 'Estrogen, Progesterone → uterus'.

questions.q: Fill up: The axis begins with the hypothalamus releasing ____.
questions.why: The top of the printed axis is 'Hypothalamus → GnRH'.

questions.q: Scenario: A 16-year-old has primary amenorrhoea, normal breast development and a normal uterus on imaging. Which side of the split does she fall on?
questions.why: A present uterus places her in the uterus(+) column with Kallmann syndrome and cryptomenorrhoea.

questions.q: True/False: Gonadal dysgenesis is listed in the uterus-present column.
options: True - because the uterus is hypoplastic but present
questions.why: Gonadal dysgenesis is grouped with absent-uterus conditions in this split.

questions.q: Odd one out - which belongs to the uterus-negative column rather than the uterus-positive one?
questions.why: AIS is in the uterus(-) group.

questions.q: Fill up: The first step in the printed workup is ____ examination.
questions.why: '1. Physical Examination'.

questions.q: Which two physical findings are specified in step 1?
questions.why: Step 1 is annotated 'Breast' and 'Pubic hair'.

questions.q: Fill up: Step 2 is a ____ test, especially if breast development is adequate.
questions.why: '2. UPT: Especially if adequate breast development'.

questions.q: Why is a urine pregnancy test advised specifically when breast development is adequate?
options: Breast development indicates a pituitary lesion
Adequate estrogen makes outflow obstruction or pregnancy possible
questions.why: Well-developed breasts mean the outflow tract and endometrium are estrogenised, so a pregnancy test is worthwhile.

questions.q: Fill up: Step 3 is ____ to know the status of the uterus, with per rectal examination in brackets.
questions.why: '3. USG: Know the status of uterus (Per rectal examination)'.

questions.q: Which three hormones are measured in step 4?
questions.why: '4. FSH, LH, E'.

questions.q: Fill up: Step 5, described as the best investigation, is ____.
questions.why: '5. Karyotyping: Best Ix'.

questions.q: How many steps does the printed workup have?
questions.why: Physical examination, UPT, USG, hormones and karyotyping.

questions.q: Match each workup step with its number - 1) Physical examination 2) UPT 3) USG 4) FSH, LH, E 5) Karyotyping ... A) 5 B) 3 C) 1 D) 4 E) 2
questions.why: Printed order: 1 physical examination, 2 UPT, 3 USG, 4 hormones, 5 karyotyping.

questions.q: Scenario: A 17-year-old with primary amenorrhoea and absent breast development. Which workup step is least informative here?
questions.why: The UPT is qualified as 'especially if adequate breast development'; without breasts it is least useful.

questions.q: True/False: MRI is the investigation of choice in the printed workup of primary amenorrhoea.
questions.why: Karyotyping is named the best investigation; MRI is the IOC specifically for cryptomenorrhoea.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a step in the general workup?
questions.why: Endometrial biopsy appears later in the genital tuberculosis chapter, not in this workup.

sections.name: Conditions in the Presence of a Uterus

questions.q: Fill up: Cryptomenorrhoea means normal menstruation occurs but the blood fails to come out because of outflow tract ____.
questions.why: Printed: 'Normal menstruation; menstrual blood fails to come out d/t outflow tract obstruction'.

questions.q: How many causes of cryptomenorrhoea are printed?
questions.why: Imperforate hymen, transverse vaginal septum and vaginal atresia/agenesis.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common cause of cryptomenorrhoea is ____ hymen.
questions.why: '1. Imperforate hymen: m/c cause'.

questions.q: The second cause listed is:
questions.why: '2. Transverse vaginal septum (TVS)'.

questions.q: The third cause is printed as:
questions.why: '3. Vaginal atresia / agenesis'.

questions.q: True/False: In cryptomenorrhoea, menstruation itself is absent because the endometrium does not respond.
questions.why: Menstruation occurs normally; only the outflow is blocked.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed cause of cryptomenorrhoea?
questions.why: Cervical stenosis is not listed among the three printed causes.

questions.q: Fill up: The karyotype in cryptomenorrhoea is ____.
questions.why: 'Karyotype: 46 XX'.

questions.q: The gonads in cryptomenorrhoea are:
questions.why: 'Gonads: Ovary'.

questions.q: Which three of the four hormones listed are normal in cryptomenorrhoea?
questions.why: 'LH: Normal, FSH: Normal, E: Normal'.

questions.q: Breast development in cryptomenorrhoea is:
questions.why: 'Breast: Normal'.

questions.q: The classic symptom described is:
questions.why: 'Cyclic pain every month'.

questions.q: Fill up: Besides cyclical pain and primary amenorrhoea, patients may have ____ retention.
questions.why: '+/- urinary retention'.

questions.q: Which phrase summarises the mechanism added beside the presentation list?
questions.why: Printed: 'Outflow tract obstruction (+)'.

questions.q: Match the finding with its status in cryptomenorrhoea - 1) Karyotype 2) Gonads 3) LH and FSH 4) Breast ... A) Ovary B) 46XX C) Normal D) Normal
questions.why: 46XX karyotype, ovarian gonads, normal gonadotrophins and normal breasts.

questions.q: Scenario: A 14-year-old with monthly suprapubic pain, no periods and normal breast development. Which hormonal pattern is expected?
options: Raised FSH and LH with low estrogen
Normal LH, FSH and estrogen with a 46XX karyotype
questions.why: Outflow obstruction leaves the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis entirely normal.

questions.q: True/False: Cryptomenorrhoea is associated with absent breast development.
questions.why: Breasts are normal because ovarian function and estrogen are normal.

questions.q: Fill up: Blood collected in the vagina is called ____.
questions.why: 'In vagina: Hematocolpos'.

questions.q: Blood collected in the uterus is called:
questions.why: 'In uterus: Hematometra'.

questions.q: Which process is named alongside the blood collection as a mechanism?
questions.why: 'Retrograde menstruation' is printed beside the collection sites.

questions.q: Retrograde menstruation in this setting leads to:
questions.why: The arrow reads 'Retrograde menstruation → Endometriosis'.

questions.q: Fill up: Endometriosis secondary to this obstruction causes increased ____.
questions.why: Printed: '↑ dysmenorrhoea'.

questions.q: Which additional physical sign may be present with large collections?
questions.why: '+/- Suprapubic bulge'.

questions.q: Match the collection site with its term - 1) Vagina 2) Uterus ... A) Haematometra B) Haematocolpos
questions.why: Vaginal collection is haematocolpos; uterine collection is haematometra.

questions.q: Scenario: A girl with imperforate hymen is found at surgery to have pelvic endometriosis. Which printed mechanism explains it?
options: Retrograde menstruation through the obstructed outflow
questions.why: The page links retrograde menstruation to endometriosis and rising dysmenorrhoea.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed consequence of the collected blood?
questions.why: Haematosalpinx is not printed; the named sites are vagina, uterus, retrograde spread and the suprapubic bulge.

questions.q: True/False: Chronic blood collection in cryptomenorrhoea can present with urinary retention.
questions.why: '+/- urinary retention' is printed in the presentation list.

questions.q: Fill up: On per rectal examination the uterus is present and ____.
questions.why: 'P/R: uterus (+) and enlarged'.

questions.q: Local examination in imperforate hymen shows:
options: A tense bulging hymen with no vaginal opening
A normal hymen with a patent opening
questions.why: Printed: 'Tensed bulging hymen / Vaginal opening (-)'.

questions.q: Cough impulse is positive in:
questions.why: The table pairs 'Cough Impulse (+)' with imperforate hymen and 'Cough impulse (-)' with vaginal agenesis.

questions.q: In vaginal agenesis, the hymen is:
questions.why: 'Hymen not bulging' is the vaginal agenesis entry.

questions.q: Fill up: The investigation of choice for cryptomenorrhoea is ____.
questions.why: 'IOC: MRI'.

questions.q: Which two roles are printed for MRI here?
options: Differentiate between causes and define thickness or location of the septum in transverse vaginal septum
Diagnose pregnancy and date the gestation
questions.why: Printed: 'Differentiate between causes' and 'Thickness/location of septa in TVS'.

questions.q: Match the examination finding with the diagnosis - 1) Tense bulging hymen 2) Cough impulse positive 3) Hymen not bulging 4) Cough impulse negative ... A) Vaginal agenesis B) Imperforate hymen
questions.why: Bulging hymen and a positive cough impulse indicate a distensible obstructed vagina (imperforate hymen); a flat hymen with no cough impulse indicates agenesis.

questions.q: Scenario: A 13-year-old has cyclical pain and a bluish bulging membrane at the introitus that expands on crying. Which diagnosis?
questions.why: A bulging membrane that transmits a cough impulse is the imperforate hymen picture.

questions.q: True/False: A positive cough impulse helps distinguish imperforate hymen from vaginal agenesis.
options: False - the impulse is positive in both
False - the sign is not used
questions.why: The printed table uses the cough impulse to separate the two.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed indication for MRI in cryptomenorrhoea?
questions.why: Ovarian reserve is not among the printed roles.

questions.q: How many 'other conditions' are listed for the uterus-positive group?
questions.why: 'Other Conditions: 1. Gonadal dysgenesis, 2. Kallmann syndrome'.

questions.q: Fill up: The shared mechanism of the two conditions is decreased ____ production with decreased gonadal function.
questions.why: 'D/t ↓ estrogen → ↓ Gonadal function'.

questions.q: Which shared breast finding is printed?
questions.why: '- Breast development (-)'.

questions.q: The uterus in both conditions is described as:
questions.why: '- Uterus: Hypoplastic (Infantile uterus)'.

questions.q: Fill up: Pubic and axillary hair are ____ in both conditions.
questions.why: 'Scanty pubic/axillary hair'.

questions.q: Gonadal dysgenesis is distinguished from Kallmann syndrome hormonally by:
options: Raised FSH and LH with low estrogen versus low LH and FSH with low estrogen
questions.why: Printed: Kallmann 'LH ↓, FSH ↓, E ↓'; gonadal dysgenesis 'E ↓, FSH ↑, LH ↑'.

questions.q: Match each condition with its gonadotrophin pattern - 1) Kallmann syndrome 2) Gonadal dysgenesis ... A) E low, FSH raised, LH raised B) LH low, FSH low, E low
questions.why: Kallmann is hypogonadotropic; gonadal dysgenesis is hypergonadotropic.

questions.q: Scenario: A 17-year-old has primary amenorrhoea, no breast development, a hypoplastic uterus and FSH of 1.8 IU/L. Which condition?
questions.why: Low FSH with absent breasts points to the hypogonadotropic picture of Kallmann syndrome.

questions.q: True/False: Both Kallmann syndrome and gonadal dysgenesis show scanty pubic and axillary hair.
questions.why: The printed 'similarities' block lists scanty hair for both.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common karyotype in Turner syndrome is ____.
questions.why: 'Karyotype: m/c: 45 X0'.

questions.q: The rare mosaic karyotype printed is:
questions.why: 'Turner mosaic: 45X0/46xy (Rare)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The gonads are ____ ovaries, which produce decreased estrogen.
questions.why: 'Gonads: Streak ovaries → ↓ estrogen'.

questions.q: Which combination of gonad is described as having an increased chance of malignancy?
questions.why: The mosaic arm pairs 'Streak ovary + dysgenetic testis' with '↑ chance of malignancy: Should be removed'.

questions.q: What is the printed instruction for a non-malignant streak gonad?
questions.why: 'Non-malignant: Should not be removed'.

questions.q: Fill up: Short stature in Turner syndrome is attributed to mutation of the ____ gene.
questions.why: 'Stature: Short d/t mutation of SHOX gene'.

questions.q: Which neck finding is printed?
questions.why: 'Webbing of neck'.

questions.q: The hairline finding is:
questions.why: 'Low posterior hair line'.

questions.q: Fill up: The chest is described as ____ shaped with widely spaced nipples.
questions.why: 'Shield shaped chest. Widely spaced nipples'.

questions.q: The hearing loss specified is:
questions.why: 'SNHL (Sensorineural hearing loss)'.

questions.q: Which three autoimmune diseases are named?
options: Diabetes, Addison disease and pernicious anaemia
Diabetes, Hashimoto thyroiditis and celiac disease
questions.why: Printed: 'Autoimmune diseases: Diabetes / Hashimoto thyroiditis / Celiac disease'.

questions.q: The elbow deformity named is:
questions.why: 'Cubitus valgus'.

questions.q: Fill up: The cardiac associations are bicuspid aortic valve ____ coarctation of the aorta.
questions.why: 'Cardiac disease: Bicuspid aortic valve > Coarctation of aorta'.

questions.q: Match each Turner feature with its system - 1) Webbing of neck 2) SNHL 3) Cubitus valgus 4) Shield chest ... A) Skeletal B) Neck C) Ear D) Chest
questions.why: Neck, ear, skeletal and chest respectively.

questions.q: Which investigation is listed to rule out the mosaic form?
questions.why: 'Karyotyping: Rule out mosaic'.

questions.q: The renal anomaly specifically sought on renal ultrasound is:
questions.why: 'Renal USG (A/w horse shoe kidney)'.

questions.q: Fill up: ____ is advised for the cardiac associations.
questions.why: 'ECHO (Heart disease)'.

questions.q: Thyroid profile is requested because of which association?
questions.why: The thyroid profile is bracketed '(Hashimoto thyroiditis)'.

questions.q: Which test is listed for the hearing loss?
questions.why: 'Audiometry (SNHL)'.

questions.q: Which two metabolic tests are printed in the management column?
options: Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile
questions.why: Printed: 'Fasting blood glucose, lipid profile (DM)'.

questions.q: Fill up: Hormonal management is estrogen ____ progesterone because the uterus is present.
questions.why: 'E + P : Because uterus (+)'.

questions.q: Why is progesterone added in Turner syndrome?
options: The uterus is present and needs protection from unopposed estrogen
questions.why: The printed reason is simply 'Because uterus (+)'.

questions.q: Scenario: A 15-year-old girl with short stature, webbed neck, shield chest and cubitus valgus has primary amenorrhoea. Which two investigations are prioritised by this page?
questions.why: Karyotyping rules out the mosaic form and ECHO looks for the bicuspid aortic valve and coarctation.

questions.q: True/False: All Turner streak gonads should be removed prophylactically.
options: True - after puberty in every case
questions.why: Non-malignant streak gonads should not be removed; only the streak ovary plus dysgenetic testis combination is removed.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed Turner feature?
questions.why: Horseshoe kidney appears under investigations as an association to seek, not in the features list.

units.title: Swyer Syndrome and the Turner Comparison

questions.q: Fill up: Swyer syndrome presents with primary amenorrhoea, a present uterus and ____ breast development.
questions.why: 'Uterus (+), Breast development (-)'.

questions.q: Which two hormones are raised in Swyer syndrome?
questions.why: 'FSH, LH: ↑'.

questions.q: The gonads in Swyer syndrome are:
questions.why: 'Gonads: Dysgenetic testis'.

questions.q: Height in Swyer syndrome is:
questions.why: 'Height: Normal'.

questions.q: Match each feature with the syndrome - 1) 45XO 2) 46XY 3) Streak ovaries 4) Dysgenetic testis with bilateral inguinal hernia ... A) Swyer syndrome B) Turner syndrome
questions.why: Turner is 45XO with streak ovaries; Swyer is 46XY with dysgenetic testes that present as inguinal hernias.

questions.q: Which syndrome carries the additional dysmorphic features?
questions.why: The comparison table marks additional features as present for Turner's.

questions.q: Scenario: A tall 17-year-old with primary amenorrhoea, absent breasts and a 46XY karyotype. Which diagnosis?
questions.why: Normal height, absent breasts and a 46XY karyotype is the Swyer picture.

questions.q: True/False: Swyer syndrome is associated with short stature.
questions.why: Height is normal in Swyer syndrome; short stature belongs to Turner syndrome.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is a Turner feature rather than a Swyer feature?
questions.why: Webbing of the neck is listed under Turner features.

questions.q: Fill up: The karyotype in Kallmann syndrome is ____.
questions.why: 'Karyotype: 46xx'.

questions.q: The gonads are described as:
questions.why: 'Gonads: Ovary (Normal function)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most commonly affected gene is the ____ gene.
questions.why: 'm/c gene affected: KAL-1 gene'.

questions.q: Breast development in Kallmann syndrome is:
questions.why: 'Breast: Not well developed'.

questions.q: Pubic and axillary hair are:
questions.why: 'Scanty pubic/axillary hair'.

questions.q: Which two hormones are decreased?
questions.why: 'Hormones: FSH, LH ↓'.

questions.q: Stature in Kallmann syndrome is:
questions.why: 'Stature: Normal'.

questions.q: Fill up: The associated sensory finding is ____.
questions.why: 'A/w: Anosmia'.

questions.q: Which three presentations are printed for Kallmann syndrome?
options: Delayed puberty, primary amenorrhoea and infertility
questions.why: The presentation list is delayed puberty, 1° amenorrhoea and infertility.

questions.q: Fill up: The treatment printed is ____ GnRH.
questions.why: 'Management: Pulsatile GnRH'.

questions.q: Why is pulsatile rather than continuous GnRH used?
options: Pulsatile delivery mimics physiological GnRH and drives gonadotrophin release
questions.why: The printed management names pulsatile GnRH to replace the missing hypothalamic signal.

questions.q: Match each Kallmann feature with its descriptor - 1) Karyotype 2) Gonads 3) Hormones 4) Stature ... A) Normal B) FSH and LH low C) Ovary with normal function D) 46XX
questions.why: 46XX karyotype, functional ovaries, low gonadotrophins and normal stature.

questions.q: Scenario: A 19-year-old woman with primary amenorrhoea, absent sense of smell, normal height and low FSH and LH. What treatment is printed?
questions.why: Kallmann syndrome with anosmia is treated with pulsatile GnRH.

questions.q: True/False: Kallmann syndrome is a hypergonadotropic condition.
options: True - FSH and LH are raised
questions.why: FSH and LH are low; it is hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed Kallmann feature?
questions.why: Stature is normal in Kallmann syndrome; short stature belongs to Turner syndrome.

sections.name: Conditions in the Absence of a Uterus

questions.q: Fill up: Mullerian agenesis has a ____ karyotype.
questions.why: The comparison table prints 46XX for Mullerian agenesis and 46XY for AIS.

questions.q: The gonads in Mullerian agenesis are described as normal because they develop from the:
questions.why: 'Ovaries (Normal as they develop from genital ridge)'.

questions.q: The gonads in AIS are:
questions.why: 'Testis (Normal)'.

questions.q: Fill up: Internal genitalia are ____ in both conditions.
questions.why: Both columns print 'Absent' for internal genitalia.

questions.q: Why are the internal genitalia absent in Mullerian agenesis?
options: Both Mullerian ducts are absent, so the fallopian tubes do not form
The ovaries failed to secrete estrogen
The urogenital sinus failed to canalise
questions.why: 'Absent (Both Mullerian ducts (MD) (-) → Fallopian tubes absent)'.

questions.q: External genitalia in both conditions are:
questions.why: Both columns show a female symbol for external genitalia.

questions.q: Breast development in Mullerian agenesis is normal because estrogen is:
questions.why: 'Estrogen: Normal → Breast development: Normal'.

questions.q: Breast development in AIS reaches Tanner stage:
questions.why: The AIS column prints 'Tanner stage 4/5'.

questions.q: Pubic and axillary hair in Mullerian agenesis are:
questions.why: 'Androgens: Normal hair distribution'.

questions.q: Pubic and axillary hair in AIS are:
options: Scanty, because the tissues are unresponsive to testosterone
questions.why: The AIS column prints 'Scanty' and 'Unresponsive to testosterone'.

questions.q: Fill up: Testosterone in Mullerian agenesis is normal and equivalent to ____ levels.
questions.why: 'Normal: Equivalent to female levels'.

questions.q: Testosterone in AIS is:
questions.why: '↑ (Equivalent to male levels)'.

questions.q: LH in Mullerian agenesis versus AIS is:
questions.why: 'LH: Normal | ↑'.

questions.q: FSH in Mullerian agenesis versus AIS is:
questions.why: 'FSH: Normal | Normal'.

questions.q: Fill up: Patients with Mullerian agenesis ____ produce biological children using IVF with oocyte and sperm plus surrogacy.
questions.why: 'Produce biological children: Yes: IVF with oocyte + sperm → Surrogacy'.

questions.q: Can patients with AIS produce biological children?
questions.why: The AIS column marks this as not possible.

questions.q: Match each row with the condition - 1) 46XX 2) Scanty pubic hair 3) Male-level testosterone 4) Raised LH ... A) AIS B) Mullerian agenesis
questions.why: 46XX is Mullerian agenesis; scanty hair, male-level testosterone and raised LH are AIS.

questions.q: Scenario: A 17-year-old with primary amenorrhoea has a 46XY karyotype, Tanner 5 breasts, scanty axillary hair and male-range testosterone. Which diagnosis?
questions.why: 46XY with androgen-unresponsive scanty hair and male testosterone is AIS.

questions.q: True/False: Women with Mullerian agenesis have functional ovaries and can have genetic offspring through surrogacy.
questions.why: The table states biological children are possible with IVF and surrogacy.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is a Mullerian agenesis feature rather than an AIS feature?
questions.why: Normal androgen-dependent hair distribution is the Mullerian agenesis column.

questions.q: Fill up: Mullerian agenesis is also called Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-____ syndrome.
questions.why: The eponym printed is Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome.

questions.q: Which renal anomalies are associated?
questions.why: 'Renal anomalies: Agenesis / Horse shoe kidney'.

questions.q: Fill up: The skeletal anomaly named is ____.
questions.why: 'Skeletal anomalies: Hemivertebra'.

questions.q: How many associated anomaly groups are printed under MRKH?
questions.why: Renal anomalies and skeletal anomalies.

questions.q: Match the anomaly with its system - 1) Horseshoe kidney 2) Hemivertebra ... A) Skeletal B) Renal
questions.why: Horseshoe kidney is renal; hemivertebra is skeletal.

questions.q: True/False: MRKH-associated anomalies include cardiac lesions such as coarctation of the aorta.
options: True - bicuspid aortic valve is listed
questions.why: Cardiac anomalies are listed under Turner syndrome, not MRKH.

questions.q: Which faint note on the final primary amenorrhoea page qualifies the vaginal findings in Mullerian agenesis?
options: The distal end of the vagina is sometimes present
questions.why: Page 177 prints the Mullerian agenesis feature 'sometimes distal end (+)'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT an MRKH association?
questions.why: SNHL belongs to Turner syndrome.

units.title: Investigations and Management with an Absent Uterus

questions.q: Fill up: The first investigation advised in all patients is ____ to look for renal anomalies.
questions.why: 'In all patients: 1. IVP (Intravenous pyelography): Renal anomalies'.

questions.q: The second investigation in all patients is:
questions.why: '2. Skeletal X-ray: Vertebral anomalies'.

questions.q: Fill up: Vaginoplasty is performed for ____ problems.
questions.why: 'Vaginoplasty (For coital problems)'.

questions.q: When is vaginoplasty timed?
questions.why: 'Time: Just before/after marriage'.

questions.q: Which vaginoplasty technique is named first for Mullerian agenesis?
questions.why: 'Technique: McIndoe technique' with 'Vecchietti technique' also listed.

questions.q: Fill up: Management of the AIS side of the table is gonadectomy plus ____ replacement therapy.
questions.why: 'Gonadectomy + Estrogen replacement therapy'.

questions.q: Match each management element with its indication - 1) Vaginoplasty 2) Gonadectomy 3) Estrogen replacement ... A) Mullerian agenesis B) AIS
questions.why: Vaginoplasty addresses coital problems in Mullerian agenesis; gonadectomy and estrogen are the AIS column.

questions.q: Scenario: A 16-year-old with Mullerian agenesis is diagnosed. Which two investigations must be done in all such patients?
questions.why: IVP for renal anomalies and skeletal X-ray for vertebral anomalies are advised for every patient.

questions.q: True/False: Karyotyping is omitted in the investigation list for the absent-uterus group.
options: False - it is the first investigation
questions.why: This page lists only IVP and skeletal X-ray under investigations in all patients.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT part of the printed management block?
questions.why: Pulsatile GnRH is the Kallmann syndrome treatment.

units.title: Summary of Primary Amenorrhoea by Hormone Pattern

questions.q: Fill up: The summary table has ____ hormone-pattern columns.
questions.why: Low gonadotrophins, normal, raised LH with normal FSH, and raised both.

questions.q: Which condition heads the low-LH, low-FSH, low-estrogen column?
questions.why: 'I. Kallmann syndrome'.

questions.q: Which two conditions share the normal hormone column?
questions.why: The normal column lists Mullerian agenesis and cryptomenorrhoea.

questions.q: Which condition alone occupies the raised-LH with normal-FSH column?
questions.why: The third column contains only AIS.

questions.q: How many conditions are listed under the raised LH and FSH with low estrogen column?
questions.why: Turner's syndrome, Swyer's syndrome and pure gonadal dysgenesis.

questions.q: Fill up: The third gonadal dysgenesis in the summary list is ____ gonadal dysgenesis.
questions.why: '3. Pure gonadal dysgenesis'.

questions.q: Match each condition with its summary column - 1) Kallmann 2) Mullerian agenesis 3) Cryptomenorrhoea 4) AIS 5) Turner ... A) LH and FSH normal B) LH up, FSH normal C) LH down, FSH down D) LH up, FSH up
questions.why: Kallmann is hypogonadotropic; Mullerian agenesis and cryptomenorrhoea are normal; AIS has raised LH only; Turner is hypergonadotropic.

questions.q: Scenario: A patient with primary amenorrhoea is found to have raised LH, normal FSH and male-level testosterone. Which column of the summary does she fall into?
options: The raised LH and FSH column
The raised LH with normal FSH column (AIS)
questions.why: That combination is the AIS column.

questions.q: True/False: Cryptomenorrhoea appears in the summary under the low-gonadotrophin column.
options: True - it is grouped with Kallmann syndrome
True - it has its own column
questions.why: Cryptomenorrhoea sits in the normal hormone column.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT in the hypergonadotropic column?
questions.why: Mullerian agenesis has normal hormones.

questions.q: Fill up: Vaginal flora is described as ____.
questions.why: Page 178 opens with 'Vaginal flora: Polymicrobial'.

questions.q: The predominant organism of the vagina is:
questions.why: 'Lactobacilli / Doderlein bacilli (Predominant)'.

questions.q: Doderlein bacilli are described as:
questions.why: '- Gram +ve bacilli'.

questions.q: When do lactobacilli first appear?
questions.why: '- Appears at puberty'.

questions.q: Fill up: Lactobacilli disappear at ____.
questions.why: '- Disappears at menopause'.

questions.q: The substrate converted to lactic acid is:
questions.why: 'Glycogen in stratified epithelium → Lactic acid + H2O2'.

questions.q: Fill up: Glycogen breakdown yields lactic acid and ____.
questions.why: The arrow prints 'Lactic acid + H2O2'.

questions.q: The acidic pH produced by lactobacilli is described as the:
questions.why: '→ Acidic pH → Defense mechanism'.

questions.q: Which hormone is responsible for the presence of glycogen?
questions.why: '- Estrogen: Responsible for presence of glycogen'.

questions.q: Fill up: ____ survives in the acidic pH produced by lactobacilli.
questions.why: '- Candida: Survives in acidic pH'.

questions.q: Which two findings are printed under 'normal pap smear'?
questions.why: The pap smear block lists 'Doderlein bacilli' and 'Superficial cells' under 'Normal pap smear'.

questions.q: What is the stated purpose of the pap smear here?
questions.why: 'Pap smear: Screening for cancer'.

questions.q: Scenario: A postmenopausal woman has recurrent vaginal infections. Which printed fact explains the loss of her defence mechanism?
options: Lactobacilli disappear at menopause, so the acidic protective pH is lost
questions.why: The printed line 'Disappears at menopause' explains the loss of lactobacilli and acidic protection.

questions.q: True/False: Oestrogen protects the vagina by causing glycogen deposition that lactobacilli convert to lactic acid.
options: False - progesterone is responsible for glycogen
False - glycogen is dietary in origin
questions.why: The chain printed is estrogen → glycogen → lactic acid → acidic pH → defence.

questions.q: Odd one out - which organism is NOT described as part of the normal protective flora?
questions.why: Gardnerella is the bacterial vaginosis organism, not normal protective flora.

questions.q: Fill up: Leucorrhoea is described as ____ white discharge.
questions.why: 'Leucorrhoea: Physiological white discharge'.

questions.q: When is physiological discharge increased?
options: In the early follicular phase only
questions.why: 'Increased: During ovulation, Before menstruation'.

questions.q: Fill up: In the first half of the cycle the discharge is thin and watery because of ____.
questions.why: '- 1st half of cycle: Thin watery d/t estrogen'.

questions.q: In the second half of the cycle the discharge becomes thick because of:
questions.why: '- 2nd half of cycle: Thick d/t progesterone'.

questions.q: Which three characteristics define physiological leucorrhoea?
options: Colourless, odourless and without pruritus or dysuria
questions.why: The characteristics block lists colourless, odourless and 'No pruritis/dysuria'.

questions.q: Fill up: The differential listed against leucorrhoea is ____ vaginosis discharge.
questions.why: 'D/d: Bacterial vaginosis discharge'.

questions.q: How does bacterial vaginosis discharge differ from physiological leucorrhoea in the printed comparison?
options: It is curdy white with excoriation
It is colourless but has a pungent fishy odour and no pruritus
questions.why: BV discharge is printed as colourless with a pungent/fishy odour and no pruritus.

questions.q: Match the discharge feature with the diagnosis - 1) Thin watery in the first half of cycle 2) Thick in the second half 3) Pungent fishy odour, colourless 4) Curdy white ... A) Bacterial vaginosis B) Physiological leucorrhoea C) Candidiasis
questions.why: Cycle-related changes are physiological; fishy colourless discharge is BV; curdy white is candidiasis.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman reports increased clear discharge mid-cycle with no smell and no itching. What is the printed interpretation?
options: Physiological leucorrhoea of the ovulatory phase
questions.why: Mid-cycle thin watery discharge without odour or pruritus is physiological.

questions.q: True/False: Physiological leucorrhoea is associated with pruritus and dysuria.
options: True - pruritus is the main complaint
questions.why: The printed characteristics explicitly state no pruritus and no dysuria.

questions.q: Fill up: The organism named for bacterial vaginosis is ____ vaginalis.
questions.why: 'Gardnerella vaginalis' heads the BV organism list.

questions.q: Which two additional organisms are listed with Gardnerella in bacterial vaginosis?
questions.why: The BV organism list is Gardnerella vaginalis, mycoplasma and mobiluncus.

questions.q: Fill up: The candida species named is Candida ____.
questions.why: 'Candida albicans'.

questions.q: Trichomonas vaginalis is described as a:
questions.why: 'Trichomonas vaginalis: Flagellated protozoan'.

questions.q: Fill up: Bacterial vaginosis is described as an alteration of vaginal ____.
questions.why: 'Alteration of vaginal flora'.

questions.q: Which vaginitis is printed as the most common vaginitis in females?
questions.why: 'm/c vaginitis in female' is printed in the BV column.

questions.q: Which vaginitis is the most common in pregnant females?
questions.why: '- m/c vaginitis in pregnant female' appears in the candida column.

questions.q: Which three predisposing factors are listed for candidiasis?
questions.why: The predisposing list is pregnancy, immunocompromised, antibiotics/steroids/OCP consumption.

questions.q: Fill up: Trichomonas is associated with alteration of vaginal pH towards the ____ range.
questions.why: 'Alteration of vaginal pH (Alkaline)'.

questions.q: Trichomonas vaginitis is noted to coexist with:
questions.why: 'Coexist with bacterial vaginosis'.

questions.q: Which discharge colour is printed for trichomonas?
questions.why: 'Frothy / Yellowish green colour'.

questions.q: Fill up: The candida discharge is curdy white, like ____ cheese.
questions.why: 'Curdy white / cottage cheese'.

questions.q: Which pH is printed for candida?
questions.why: The candida column prints pH < 4.5.

questions.q: Which two of the three vaginitides have a pH of 4.5 or above?
questions.why: BV and trichomonas print pH >= 4.5; only candida is below.

questions.q: Fill up: Bacterial vaginosis is marked with a cross against pruritus, meaning ____ inflammation.
questions.why: '× (No inflammation)' is printed for BV.

questions.q: In which vaginitis is excoriation the main complaint?
questions.why: The candida column prints 'Intense pruritis → Excoriation: main complaint'.

questions.q: Fill up: ____ dysuria is listed under trichomonas vaginitis.
questions.why: 'Splash dysuria'.

questions.q: The polymorphonuclear leucocyte to epithelial cell ratio printed for bacterial vaginosis is:
questions.why: 'PMNs / epithelial cells: <1'.

questions.q: Which vaginitis is marked as a sexually transmitted disease in the table?
questions.why: The STD row is marked against trichomonas.

questions.q: Match each finding with the vaginitis - 1) Clue cells 2) Cottage-cheese discharge 3) Strawberry cervix 4) pH below 4.5 ... A) Trichomonas B) Bacterial vaginosis C) Candidiasis
questions.why: Clue cells are BV; cottage cheese and low pH are candida; strawberry cervix is trichomonas.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has profuse frothy yellow-green discharge, an itchy vulva and pain on passing urine. Which vaginitis?
questions.why: Frothy yellowish green discharge with pruritus and splash dysuria is trichomonas.

questions.q: True/False: Bacterial vaginosis shows abundant polymorphonuclear leucocytes on microscopy.
options: True - it is an inflammatory condition
questions.why: BV is marked 'No inflammation' with a PMN/epithelial ratio below 1.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed predisposing factor for candidiasis?
questions.why: Alkaline pH is the trichomonas column, not a candida predisposing factor.

questions.q: Fill up: The investigation of choice for vaginitis is ____ microscopy.
questions.why: 'IOC: Saline microscopy'.

questions.q: A clue cell is defined as:
options: A yeast cell with a bud
An epithelial cell with bacteria adhered to it
A flagellated organism the size of a nucleus
questions.why: 'Epithelial cells with bacteria adhered: Clue cell'.

questions.q: Which gram-stain scoring system is named for bacterial vaginosis?
questions.why: '- Nugent score: Score 7-10'.

questions.q: Fill up: The two candida forms seen on microscopy are pseudohyphae and ____.
questions.why: 'Pseudohyphae' and 'Spores of candida'.

questions.q: Which microscopy appearance is printed for candida spores?
questions.why: 'Tennis racket appearance'.

questions.q: On saline microscopy, trichomonas is identified by:
options: Motility, or a pear-shaped organism the size of a cell nucleus
questions.why: 'motility + (or) Pear shaped organism = Size of nucleus of cells'.

questions.q: Fill up: The gold standard test for candidiasis is culture on ____ media.
questions.why: 'Culture on Sabouraud media' is placed beside 'Gold standard test'.

questions.q: Which per-speculum findings are printed for trichomonas?
options: Strawberry cervix and angry looking vagina
questions.why: 'p/s examination: Strawberry cervix / Angry looking vagina'.

questions.q: Fill up: The named test for bacterial vaginosis is the ____ test.
questions.why: 'Named test' points to the whiff test.

questions.q: What is added to the discharge in the whiff test and what odour results?
options: Acetic acid, producing a yeasty odour
Lugol iodine, producing a metallic odour
Ten percent KOH, producing a fishy amine-like odour
questions.why: 'Add 10% KOH to discharge → fishy / amine like odour'.

questions.q: How many Amsel criteria are listed?
questions.why: Greyish white discharge, pH >= 4.5, clue cells >= 20%, whiff test positive.

questions.q: How many Amsel criteria must be positive to diagnose bacterial vaginosis?
questions.why: '3/4 positive → Diagnostic'.

questions.q: Fill up: Amsel criterion 3 requires clue cells in at least ____ percent of epithelial cells.
questions.why: 'Clue cells >= 20% of epithelial cells'.

questions.q: Which Amsel criterion sets the pH threshold?
questions.why: Criterion 2 is 'pH >= 4.5'.

questions.q: Match each Amsel criterion with its position - 1) Greyish white discharge 2) pH >= 4.5 3) Clue cells >= 20% 4) Whiff test positive ... A) 4 B) 2 C) 1 D) 3
questions.why: The printed order is discharge, pH, clue cells, whiff test.

questions.q: Which of the three vaginitides has a negative whiff test?
questions.why: The candida column prints 'whiff test -ve'; BV and trichomonas are positive.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has a greyish white discharge, vaginal pH 5.2 and clue cells in 30% of epithelial cells, but a negative whiff test. Does she meet Amsel criteria?
options: Yes - three of four criteria are met
No - the whiff test is mandatory
questions.why: Discharge, pH and clue cells give three positive criteria out of four.

questions.q: True/False: The whiff test uses ten percent potassium hydroxide and is positive in both bacterial vaginosis and trichomonas.
options: False - it is positive only in BV
False - it is negative in both
questions.why: BV and trichomonas columns both print whiff test positive, and KOH 10% is the reagent.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed microscopy finding for vaginitis?
questions.why: Intracellular diplococci belong to the gonorrhoea section, not the vaginitis microscopy row.

questions.q: Fill up: The drug of choice for bacterial vaginosis in the non-pregnant woman is oral ____ 500 mg twice daily for 7 days.
questions.why: 'metronidazole: Oral 500 mg BD x 7 days'.

questions.q: Which alternative single-dose regimen is printed for bacterial vaginosis?
questions.why: The bracket reads '(or) 2 gram stat'.

questions.q: Which second drug is listed for bacterial vaginosis?
questions.why: 'Clindamycin' is the alternative named.

questions.q: Fill up: The treatment of candidiasis is oral fluconazole ____ mg stat.
questions.why: 'Oral fluconazole: 150 mg stat'.

questions.q: What is the non-pregnant regimen for trichomonas vaginitis?
options: Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days, or 2 g stat
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days
questions.why: The trichomonas column prints metronidazole 500 mg BD x 7 days or 2 g stat.

questions.q: In the first trimester, how should metronidazole be given?
questions.why: '- 1st trimester: Vaginal metronidazole'.

questions.q: Fill up: From the second trimester onwards, metronidazole is given ____.
questions.why: '- 2nd/3rd trimester: Oral metronidazole'.

questions.q: Which drug is contraindicated in pregnancy for candidiasis?
options: Oral metronidazole in the third trimester
questions.why: 'Oral fluconazole: Contraindicated'.

questions.q: Fill up: The drug of choice for candidiasis in pregnancy is topical ____.
questions.why: 'Topical clotrimazole: DOC'.

questions.q: Partner treatment in bacterial vaginosis is advised:
questions.why: 'Partner Rx: For symptomatic partners only'.

questions.q: Is partner treatment indicated in candidiasis?
questions.why: The candida column marks partner treatment with a cross.

questions.q: Fill up: For trichomonas, the partner receives metronidazole at the ____ dose.
questions.why: '- Dose: Same'.

questions.q: Match each vaginitis with its pregnancy modification - 1) BV in the first trimester 2) BV after the first trimester 3) Candidiasis in pregnancy 4) Trichomonas in the first trimester ... A) Oral metronidazole B) Vaginal metronidazole C) Topical clotrimazole
questions.why: Metronidazole is vaginal in the first trimester and oral later; candida needs topical clotrimazole.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman at 8 weeks of gestation has bacterial vaginosis. What is the printed route of metronidazole?
questions.why: First trimester metronidazole is given vaginally.

questions.q: True/False: Oral fluconazole can be used safely in the first trimester for candidiasis.
options: True - after the first trimester only
questions.why: Oral fluconazole is printed as contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.q: Odd one out - which drug is NOT part of the printed vaginitis treatment set?
questions.why: Cefixime belongs to the cervicitis and PID kits, not vaginitis treatment.

questions.q: Fill up: The ectocervix is lined by stratified ____ epithelium, like the vagina.
questions.why: 'Ectocervix: Stratified squamous epithelium (Like vagina)'.

questions.q: The endocervix is lined by:
questions.why: 'Endocervix: Lined by Columnar epithelium'.

questions.q: Which four infections may involve the ectocervix?
questions.why: The ectocervix list is candida, trichomonas, HSV and HPV.

questions.q: Which two organisms infect the endocervix?
questions.why: The endocervix list is chlamydia and gonorrhoea, with 'Infection of endocervix → Cervicitis'.

questions.q: Fill up: Infection of the ____ is what the page defines as cervicitis.
questions.why: The bracket reads '(Infection of endocervix → Cervicitis)'.

questions.q: Match the epithelium with the infections listed - 1) Ectocervix 2) Endocervix ... A) Chlamydia and gonorrhoea B) Candida, trichomonas, HSV and HPV
questions.why: Squamous ectocervix hosts the vaginal infections; columnar endocervix hosts chlamydia and gonorrhoea.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has a cervical swab growing Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Which part of the cervix is infected?
questions.why: Gonorrhoea is listed as an endocervical infection producing cervicitis.

questions.q: True/False: HPV infection of the cervix is listed under endocervical infections.
questions.why: HPV is listed with the ectocervical (vaginal-type) infections.

questions.q: Odd one out - which infection is NOT listed under the ectocervix?
questions.why: Gonorrhoea is an endocervical infection.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common route of spread is ascending infection along with ____.
questions.why: 'm/c route of spread: Ascending infection along with sperms (STD)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common site of infection is the endocervix rather than the ____.
questions.why: 'm/c site: Endocervix > Urethra'.

questions.q: What proportion of cases are asymptomatic?
questions.why: 'Asymptomatic (50-80%)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common presentation is a ____ discharge.
questions.why: 'Discharge (m/c presentation): mucoid/purulent'.

questions.q: Which two additional symptoms are listed?
questions.why: 'Dyspareunia' and 'Post coital bleeding'.

questions.q: Match each item with its status - 1) Asymptomatic 2) Discharge 3) Dyspareunia 4) Post-coital bleeding ... A) Most common presentation B) 50-80% C) Listed symptom D) Listed symptom
questions.why: Asymptomatic in 50-80%; discharge is the commonest presentation; dyspareunia and post-coital bleeding are additional.

questions.q: Scenario: A 24-year-old has a mucopurulent cervical discharge and bleeding after intercourse but no pain. What is the most likely finding on testing?
questions.why: Mucopurulent discharge with post-coital bleeding in a young woman is the printed cervicitis picture.

questions.q: True/False: The majority of women with chlamydial cervicitis are symptomatic.
questions.why: 50-80% are asymptomatic.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed presentation of cervicitis?
questions.why: Cyclical pain belongs to the cryptomenorrhoea page.

questions.q: Which three per-speculum findings are printed?
options: Unhealthy friable cervix, bleeding on touch, and erosion or ulcer
questions.why: Per speculum: unhealthy friable cervix, bleeds on touch, erosion/ulcer.

questions.q: Fill up: The differential to be excluded when these findings are present is ____.
questions.why: 'D/d: PID' with uterine and adnexal tenderness.

questions.q: Which two findings on per-vaginal examination would shift the diagnosis to PID?
options: Cervical motion tenderness and vaginal discharge
questions.why: The D/d block lists uterine tenderness and adnexal tenderness.

questions.q: In uncomplicated cervicitis, the uterus on per-vaginal examination is:
questions.why: 'Uterus: Normal'.

questions.q: Fill up: In uncomplicated cervicitis the adnexa are ____.
questions.why: 'Adnexa: Normal'.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with a friable cervix that bleeds on touch also has adnexal tenderness. What does the printed page suggest?
options: Consider pelvic inflammatory disease rather than isolated cervicitis
questions.why: Adnexal tenderness is the D/d pointer to PID.

questions.q: True/False: Cervical motion tenderness is listed as a per-speculum finding.
options: True - it is the first per-speculum finding
questions.why: Cervical motion tenderness belongs to the PID criteria; per-speculum findings are appearance-based.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed per-speculum finding in cervicitis?
