questions.why: Adnexal tenderness is a per-vaginal finding pointing to PID.

questions.q: Fill up: Gonorrhoea is described as Gram ____ diplococci.
questions.why: 'Gram -ve diplococci'.

questions.q: Gonococcal diplococci are described as:
questions.why: 'Intra/extracellular'.

questions.q: Fill up: On Gram stain, the criterion printed is more than ____ neutrophils per field.
questions.why: '>10 Neutrophils/field'.

questions.q: Which organism shows no organism on Gram stain?
questions.why: The chlamydia column prints 'No organism'.

questions.q: Fill up: The investigation of choice for both organisms is the nucleic acid ____ test.
questions.why: 'IOC: Nucleic acid amplification test'.

questions.q: Which specimen is advised for gonorrhoea when urethritis is present?
options: Urine, in addition to the endocervical swab
questions.why: 'Specimen: Endocervical swab; Urine if urethritis +ve'.

questions.q: Fill up: The gold standard for gonorrhoea is culture on ____ media.
questions.why: 'Gold standard: Culture on Thayer Martin media'.

questions.q: The gold standard for chlamydia is culture on:
questions.why: 'Gold standard: Culture on McCoy cell lines'.

questions.q: Match each organism with its gold standard - 1) Gonorrhoea 2) Chlamydia ... A) Culture on McCoy cell lines B) Culture on Thayer Martin media
questions.why: Thayer Martin for gonorrhoea; McCoy cell lines for chlamydia.

questions.q: Scenario: A cervical Gram stain shows more than 10 neutrophils per field but no organism. Which diagnosis is favoured?
questions.why: Polymorphs without a visible organism is the chlamydia pattern.

questions.q: True/False: NAAT is listed as the gold standard for chlamydia.
questions.why: NAAT is the investigation of choice; culture on McCoy cell lines is the gold standard.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed specimen or test for cervicitis?
questions.why: Sabouraud media is the candidiasis gold standard.

questions.q: Fill up: In the non-pregnant patient, chlamydia is treated with doxycycline 100 mg ____ for 7 days.
questions.why: Printed: 'Tab. Doxycycline 100mg OD x 7 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: Gonorrhoea is treated with Inj. Ceftriaxone ____ mg IM as a single dose.
questions.why: Printed: 'Inj Ceftriaxone 250mg IM single dose'.

questions.q: Which drug is contraindicated in pregnancy in this treatment block?
questions.why: 'Doxycycline: C/I' under the pregnant row.

questions.q: Fill up: The pregnant patient is treated with tablet azithromycin ____ g orally as a single dose.
questions.why: 'Tab. Azithromycin 1 g oral: Single dose'.

questions.q: Which two complications of cervicitis are printed?
options: PID from ascending infection, and perihepatitis (Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome)
questions.why: 'Complications: PID (d/t ascend of infection), Perihepatitis: Fitz Hugh Curtis syndrome'.

questions.q: Fill up: The perihepatitis of this infection is called Fitz-Hugh-____ syndrome.
questions.why: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is the named perihepatitis.

questions.q: Match each drug with its setting - 1) Doxycycline 100 mg OD x 7 days 2) Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose 3) Azithromycin 1 g single dose 4) Doxycycline in pregnancy ... A) Contraindicated B) Pregnant patient C) Gonorrhoea, non-pregnant D) Chlamydia, non-pregnant
questions.why: Doxycycline for non-pregnant chlamydia, ceftriaxone for gonorrhoea, azithromycin in pregnancy, doxycycline contraindicated in pregnancy.

questions.q: Scenario: A pregnant woman with cervicitis cannot receive doxycycline. What is the printed alternative?
options: Azithromycin 1 g orally as a single dose
questions.why: Azithromycin 1 g single dose is the pregnant patient's regimen.

questions.q: True/False: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is listed as a complication of vaginitis.
questions.why: It is a complication of cervicitis from ascending infection.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT in the printed cervicitis treatment block?
questions.why: Metronidazole 400 mg BD for 14 days belongs to the PID regimen.

questions.q: Fill up: Syndromic management is advised by ____.
questions.why: 'Syndromic management: Advised by NACO'.

questions.q: Colour-coded kits are based on which four inputs?
options: History, per-speculum examination, per-vaginal examination and minimal investigation
Examination, pH, whiff test and microscopy
History, partner history, pap smear and culture
questions.why: 'Colour coded kits: Based on History + P/s examination + P/v examination + minimal investigation'.

questions.q: Fill up: The vaginitis kit is the ____ kit.
questions.why: Green kit is the vaginitis kit.

questions.q: What is in the green kit?
options: Secnidazole 2 g plus fluconazole 150 mg stat
questions.why: 'Green Kit 2: Secnidazole 2 gms + Fluconazole 150 mg stat'.

questions.q: Fill up: The cervicitis kit is the ____ kit, number 1.
questions.why: 'Grey Kit 1' is the cervicitis kit.

questions.q: What two drugs are in the grey kit?
options: Azithromycin 1 g stat and cefixime 400 mg stat
questions.why: 'Grey Kit 1: Tab Azithromycin 1 gm OD stat + Tab Cefixime 400mg OD stat'.

questions.q: Fill up: The PID kit is the ____ kit, number 6.
questions.why: 'Yellow Kit 6' is the PID kit.

questions.q: Which three drugs make up the yellow kit?
options: Azithromycin 1 g, cefixime 400 mg and secnidazole 2 g
Ceftriaxone 250 mg, doxycycline 100 mg and metronidazole 400 mg
Fluconazole 150 mg, secnidazole 2 g and clotrimazole
Cefixime 400 mg stat, metronidazole 400 mg BD for 14 days and doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days
questions.why: The printed yellow kit contains those three drugs.

questions.q: Which extra step is mandated before using the yellow kit?
questions.why: 'R/o: Ectopic pregnancy' is printed in the PID row.

questions.q: Fill up: The partner of a PID patient receives grey kit number ____.
questions.why: The partner treatment for PID is 'No. 1: Grey kit'.

questions.q: Which clinical findings route a patient to the yellow kit?
options: Lower abdominal pain with any one of uterine, cervical movement or adnexal tenderness
Vaginal discharge with a healthy cervix
Post-coital bleeding with a normal cervix
questions.why: The yellow kit row requires lower abdominal pain plus any one tenderness finding.

questions.q: Supportive advice common to the kits includes abstinence for how many days?
questions.why: 'Supportive treatment: Abstinence x 7 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: Partner treatment is indicated in cervicitis and PID but ____ in vaginitis.
questions.why: 'Partner Rx: Cervicitis & PID - Not indicated in vaginitis'.

questions.q: Which three other conditions are listed as uses of kit 1?
options: Vaginal discharge, pelvic pain and dysuria
Cervical erosion, post-coital bleeding and infertility
Anorectal discharge, scrotal pain syndrome and urethritis
questions.why: 'Other uses of Kit 1: Anorectal discharge, Scrotal pain syndrome, Urethritis'.

questions.q: Match the presentation with the kit - 1) Discharge with pruritus, healthy cervix 2) Unhealthy friable cervix 3) Lower abdominal pain with adnexal tenderness ... A) Yellow kit 6 B) Green kit 2 C) Grey kit 1
questions.why: Vaginitis takes green, cervicitis grey, PID yellow.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has vaginal discharge and dysuria; the cervix looks healthy and the per-vaginal examination is normal. Which kit?
options: Grey kit for her and yellow for her partner
questions.why: Discharge with pruritus/dysuria, a healthy cervix and a normal per-vaginal examination is the vaginitis row.

questions.q: True/False: The yellow kit is used for the partner of a woman with PID.
options: True - partners receive the same kit
questions.why: The partner receives grey kit 1 (cefixime and azithromycin).

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a listed use of kit 1?
options: Vaginal discharge with a healthy cervix
questions.why: Vaginal discharge with a healthy cervix routes to the green kit.

questions.q: Fill up: PID is defined as infection of the ____ female genital tract.
questions.why: Page 184: 'Definition: Infection of upper female genital tract'.

questions.q: Which three anatomical sites are listed as being included in PID?
questions.why: 'Includes: Endometritis (uterus), Salpingitis (Fallopian tubes), Oophoritis (Ovaries)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common route of spread is an ascending infection travelling along with ____.
questions.why: 'm/c route of spread: Ascending infection along with sperms (STDs)'.

questions.q: PID is most commonly seen in:
options: Sexually active females aged 15 to 35 years
Pregnant women in the third trimester
questions.why: 'm/c seen in: Sexually active females (15-35 yrs)'.

questions.q: Fill up: PID is described as a ____ infection.
questions.why: 'PID: Polymicrobial infection'.

questions.q: True/False: PID is an infection confined to the lower genital tract.
options: True - it begins in the vagina
True - the cervix is the upper limit
questions.why: It is defined as infection of the upper female genital tract.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT one of the three components printed under 'includes'?
questions.why: Cervicitis has its own chapter; PID includes endometritis, salpingitis and oophoritis.

questions.q: Fill up: Insertion of a copper T within ____ weeks is a risk factor.
questions.why: 'CuT insertion (< 3 weeks)'.

questions.q: Which four obstetric or procedural risk factors are printed?
options: Post abortion, caesarean section, nulliparity and endometriosis
Post abortion, post partum, history of instrumentation and previous history of PID
Post partum, lactation, sterilisation and fibroid
questions.why: The risk factor list prints 'multiple risk factors', post abortion, post partum, H/o instrumentation, previous H/o PID and CuT insertion.

questions.q: Which two protective factors are printed?
options: Oral contraceptive pills and depot medroxyprogesterone
questions.why: 'Protective in PID: Barrier contraceptives (Condoms), MIRENA'.

questions.q: Fill up: Infection can spread to the abdomen causing peritonitis and ____.
questions.why: 'Infection can spread to abdomen: 1. Peritonitis, 2. Perihepatitis'.

questions.q: Which intrauterine device is printed as protective?
questions.why: MIRENA appears under the protective list.

questions.q: Match the factor with its category - 1) Condoms 2) CuT insertion within 3 weeks 3) Post partum state 4) MIRENA ... A) Risk factor B) Protective
questions.why: Condoms and MIRENA protect; recent CuT insertion and the post partum state increase risk.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman had a copper T inserted 10 days ago and now has lower abdominal pain and fever. Which printed risk factor applies?
questions.why: Insertion within 3 weeks is explicitly listed as a risk factor.

questions.q: True/False: The copper T is listed as protective against PID.
options: True - after 3 weeks it becomes protective
True - it is protective in the MIRENA form
questions.why: Recent CuT insertion is a risk factor; MIRENA is the protective device.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed risk factor for PID?
questions.why: Barrier contraceptives are protective, not a risk factor.

questions.q: Fill up: The first step in the printed pathogenesis is ____ of the uterus.
questions.why: 'Pathogenesis: 1. Uterus: Endometritis'.

questions.q: Which three symptoms are printed alongside endometritis?
options: Menstrual abnormalities, dysmenorrhoea and lower abdominal pain
questions.why: The uterus block lists menstrual abnormalities, dysmenorrhoea, lower abdominal pain and endometrial biopsy.

questions.q: Which investigation is printed in the endometritis block?
questions.why: 'Endometrial biopsy' is listed in the uterus block.

questions.q: How are the fallopian tubes described in salpingitis?
questions.why: 'Thick, congested, hyperemic, swollen tubes'.

questions.q: Fill up: Inflammation of the tubal lining is called ____.
questions.why: 'Endosalpingitis'.

questions.q: Which two late tubal outcomes are printed under the tubes heading?
questions.why: 'Pyosalpinx' and 'Hydrosalpinx'.

questions.q: Fill up: The third step in the pathogenesis is ____ of the ovaries.
questions.why: '3. Oophoritis'.

questions.q: The fourth step is:
questions.why: '4. Peritonitis + pelvic abscess'.

questions.q: In women of reproductive age, which two organisms are most commonly implicated and in what order?
questions.why: 'Reproductive age: Chlamydia > Gonorrhea'.

questions.q: Fill up: In virgins, PID is caused by genital ____ spreading by the haematogenous route.
questions.why: 'Virgins: Genital TB (Hematogenous)'.

questions.q: Which organism is named for menopausal females?
questions.why: 'menopausal females: E. coli'.

questions.q: Fill up: In copper IUD users, the organism named is ____.
questions.why: 'Cu-IUD users: Actinomyces'.

questions.q: Match each population with its organism - 1) Reproductive age 2) Virgins 3) Menopausal females 4) Cu-IUD users ... A) Actinomyces B) Chlamydia more than gonorrhoea C) E. coli D) Genital TB
questions.why: Reproductive age is chlamydia then gonorrhoea; virgins have haematogenous TB; menopausal women have E. coli; Cu-IUD users have Actinomyces.

questions.q: Scenario: A 58-year-old woman presents with a tubo-ovarian abscess. Which organism does the printed list favour?
questions.why: Menopausal females are listed with E. coli.

questions.q: True/False: In virgins, PID is most often due to ascending chlamydial infection.
options: True - virgins have the highest chlamydia rate
questions.why: In virgins the printed cause is genital tuberculosis by the haematogenous route.

questions.q: Odd one out - which organism is NOT in the printed 'most common PID' list?
questions.why: Gardnerella causes bacterial vaginosis, not PID.

questions.q: Which symptom is printed as the most common?
questions.why: 'm/c: Lower abdominal pain (B/L)'.

questions.q: Fill up: Pain during ____ is increased.
questions.why: '↑ Pain during coitus'.

questions.q: What does fever lead to in the acute phase?
questions.why: The acute phase arrow reads 'Fever → menorrhagia'.

questions.q: Which two bleeding patterns are printed under AUB?
questions.why: 'AUB: Intermenstrual bleed, Postcoital bleed'.

questions.q: Fill up: ____ is a long-term feature listed among the clinical features.
questions.why: 'Infertility'.

questions.q: Fill up: The perihepatitis of PID is Fitz-Hugh-____ syndrome.
questions.why: 'Complication: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis Syndrome: Perihepatitis'.

questions.q: The adhesions of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome are described as:
options: Violin string adhesions between the liver capsule and anterior abdominal wall
Bands between the uterus and bladder
questions.why: 'Violin string adhesions: Between liver capsule & anterior abdominal wall'.

questions.q: Fill up: The pain of perihepatitis is in the ____ upper quadrant.
questions.why: 'C/o right upper quadrant pain'.

questions.q: Which organism order is given for Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome?
questions.why: 'm/c Chlamydia > Gonorrhea'.

questions.q: How is the diagnosis of PID described?
questions.why: 'PID: Clinical diagnosis'.

questions.q: Match each clinical feature with its descriptor - 1) Lower abdominal pain 2) Fever in the acute phase 3) Intermenstrual bleed 4) Perihepatitis ... A) Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome B) Most common, bilateral C) Menorrhagia D) AUB
questions.why: Bilateral lower abdominal pain is commonest; fever drives menorrhagia; intermenstrual bleeding is AUB; perihepatitis is Fitz-Hugh-Curtis.

questions.q: Scenario: A young woman with PID complains of right upper quadrant pain. What is the printed explanation?
options: Perihepatitis with violin string adhesions - Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome
questions.why: Right upper quadrant pain is the Fitz-Hugh-Curtis presentation.

questions.q: True/False: The violin string adhesions of Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome lie between the liver capsule and the diaphragm.
questions.why: They are printed between the liver capsule and the anterior abdominal wall.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed PID feature?
questions.why: Haemoptysis is not among the printed features.

questions.q: Fill up: On USG, a tubo-ovarian ____ is one of the two findings.
questions.why: '1. USG: Tubo-ovarian mass'.

questions.q: The second USG finding is:
questions.why: 'Swollen tubes'.

questions.q: Which three ultrasound signs are printed?
options: Whirlpool sign, target sign and cogwheel sign
Waist sign, bead on string sign and cogwheel sign
Snowstorm sign, bead on string and waist sign
String of pearls, waist sign and cogwheel sign
questions.why: The signs block lists waist sign, bead on string sign and cogwheel sign.

questions.q: Fill up: The waist sign is associated with ____.
questions.why: The figure caption prints 'Waist sign (Hydrosalpinx)'.

questions.q: The cogwheel sign is produced by:
questions.why: 'Cogwheel sign (Thickened endosalpingeal walls)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The beads-on-string sign is illustrated under the ____ section.
questions.why: The note reads 'USG: PID / Beads on string' and 'HSG: Genital TB'.

questions.q: What does endometrial biopsy demonstrate in PID?
questions.why: '2. Endometrial biopsy: Endometritis'.

questions.q: Fill up: The gold standard investigation is ____.
questions.why: '3. Laparoscopy: Gold standard'.

questions.q: Which three roles are printed for laparoscopy?
options: Direct visualisation of tubes, adnexa and uterus; specimen collection; scoring for conception
Drainage of abscess, fulguration and biopsy
questions.why: 'Visualize tubes, adnexa, uterus directly; Specimen collection; Scoring for conception'.

questions.q: Fill up: The CDC minimum criteria require lower abdominal pain plus any ____ of the three per-vaginal findings.
questions.why: 'Lower abdominal pain with any 1 of the following P/v findings'.

questions.q: Which three per-vaginal findings make up the minimum criteria?
options: Uterine tenderness, adnexal mass and fever
Cervical motion tenderness, discharge and fever
Cervical movement tenderness, adnexal tenderness and uterine tenderness
Adnexal tenderness, cervical erosion and discharge
questions.why: The minimal criteria list cervical movement tenderness, adnexal tenderness and uterine tenderness.

questions.q: Fill up: The temperature threshold in the additional criteria is above ____ degrees Fahrenheit.
Which two laboratory markers are listed in the additional criteria?
questions.why: 'ESR' and 'CRP' are printed in the additional criteria.

questions.q: Which microscopy finding is an additional criterion?
options: Abundant white blood cells on saline microscopy of vaginal discharge
questions.why: 'Saline microscopy of vaginal discharge: Abundant WBCs'.

questions.q: Fill up: The surest sign of PID at laparoscopy is pus trickling from the ____ end.
questions.why: 'Surest sign of PID: Pus trickling from fimbrial end during laparoscopy'.

questions.q: Which scoring system is used in PID and what is excluded from it?
options: Nugent score, which excludes clue cells
Boer-Meisel score, which does not include the type of organism
questions.why: 'Scoring system for conception in PID: Boer-Meisel score (Type of organism not included)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The staging system named for PID is ____ staging.
questions.why: 'Staging of PID: Gainesville staging'.

questions.q: What procedure is named for drainage of a pelvic abscess?
questions.why: 'Culpotomy: Drainage of pelvic abscess'.

questions.q: Which two conditions must be ruled out in the differential?
options: Urinary tract infection and renal colic
questions.why: The D/d block prints ectopic pregnancy and appendicitis.

questions.q: Match each investigation with its role - 1) USG 2) Endometrial biopsy 3) Laparoscopy ... A) Gold standard B) Tubo-ovarian mass and swollen tubes C) Endometritis
questions.why: USG shows the mass and swelling; biopsy shows endometritis; laparoscopy is the gold standard.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has lower abdominal pain and adnexal tenderness but no fever, discharge or raised ESR. Does she meet CDC criteria?
options: Yes - she meets the minimum criteria for PID
No - all three per-vaginal findings are needed
No - a raised CRP is required
questions.why: Lower abdominal pain with any one per-vaginal finding satisfies the minimum criteria.

questions.q: True/False: The beads-on-string sign is described here as an HSG finding of genital tuberculosis.
options: False - it is an ultrasound sign of PID
questions.why: The note prints 'USG: PID / Beads on string' and 'HSG: Genital TB'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed ultrasound sign of PID?
questions.why: Lead pipe appearance is an HSG description from the genital tuberculosis chapter.

questions.q: Fill up: Routine management of PID is on an ____ basis.
questions.why: 'management: OPD basis'.

questions.q: Which three drugs make up the printed broad-spectrum regimen?
questions.why: Inj. Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose + Tab Doxycycline 100 mg BD x 14 days + Tab metronidazole 400 mg BD x 14 days.

questions.q: Fill up: Ceftriaxone is given as ____ mg intramuscularly in a single dose.
questions.why: 'Inj. Ceftriaxone 250mg IM single dose'.

questions.q: For how many days are doxycycline and metronidazole continued?
questions.why: Both are printed as BD for 14 days.

questions.q: Fill up: Doxycycline is given at ____ mg twice daily.
questions.why: 'Tab Doxycycline 100mg BD x 14 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: Metronidazole is given at ____ mg twice daily for 14 days.
questions.why: 'Tab metronidazole 400mg BD x 14 days'.

questions.q: Which of the four admission indications relates to treatment failure?
questions.why: '1. Not responding to oral treatment'.

questions.q: How many indications for admission are printed?
questions.why: Not responding to oral treatment, pelvic abscess, pregnant with severe disease, pregnant and unable to take oral medication.

questions.q: Which two pregnancy-related indications are printed?
options: Clinically severe disease, and inability to take oral medications
questions.why: Both pregnancy indications are severe disease and inability to take oral drugs.

questions.q: Fill up: Intravenous antibiotics are continued for ____ hours after the patient becomes afebrile.
questions.why: 'IV antibiotics continued for 24 hrs after patient becomes afebrile'.

questions.q: After the patient becomes afebrile, oral antibiotics are given for:
questions.why: 'Oral antibiotics x 14 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: The first numbered long-term consequence of PID on this page is ____, described as the most common.
questions.why: '1. Infertility: m/c'.

questions.q: How many numbered consequences are printed in that list?
questions.why: Infertility, ectopic pregnancy, chronic pelvic pain, hydrosalpinx, recurrent PID and Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome.

questions.q: Which consequence is numbered fourth?
questions.why: '4. Hydrosalpinx'.

questions.q: Fill up: The sixth item in the list is Fitz-Hugh-____ syndrome.
questions.why: '6. Fitz-Hugh Curtis syndrome'.

questions.q: Advice on sexual activity after treatment is abstinence for:
questions.why: 'Abstinence x 7-14 days'.

questions.q: Why is alcohol to be avoided?
options: Because metronidazole is part of the regimen
questions.why: The advice prints 'Avoid alcohol (metronidazole)'.

questions.q: Match each management element with its detail - 1) Ceftriaxone 2) Doxycycline 3) Metronidazole 4) IV antibiotics ... A) 400 mg BD x 14 days B) 250 mg IM single dose C) Continued 24 hours after fever settles D) 100 mg BD x 14 days
questions.why: Ceftriaxone single IM dose, doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days, IV therapy until 24 hours afebrile.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with PID is admitted with a pelvic abscess. She defervesces on day 3. When can intravenous antibiotics stop?
options: After a further 24 hours, then switch to oral therapy for 14 days
questions.why: IV antibiotics are continued for 24 hours after the patient becomes afebrile, then oral for 14 days.

questions.q: True/False: Metronidazole is given as a single 2 g dose in the PID regimen.
questions.why: It is 400 mg twice daily for 14 days.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT printed advice after PID treatment?
questions.why: Dairy avoidance is not printed; alcohol avoidance is.

questions.q: Fill up: In the syndromic approach the patient receives yellow kit number ____.
questions.why: 'No. 6: Yellow kit'.

questions.q: Which three drugs are printed for the patient in the syndromic regimen?
options: Cefixime 400 mg stat, azithromycin 1 g and secnidazole 2 g
Cefixime 400 mg stat, metronidazole 400 mg BD for 14 days and doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days
Ceftriaxone 250 mg, doxycycline 100 mg and azithromycin 1 g
Azithromycin 1 g, cefixime 400 mg and metronidazole 400 mg
questions.why: The patient regimen prints those three drugs.

questions.q: Fill up: The partner receives grey kit number ____.
questions.why: 'Partner: No. 1: Grey kit'.

questions.q: What two drugs does the partner receive?
options: Cefixime 400 mg single dose and azithromycin 1 g
questions.why: The partner block prints cefixime single dose and azithromycin.

questions.q: Which mandatory exclusion is printed before starting the syndromic kit?
options: Ensure the urine pregnancy test is negative
questions.why: 'Ensure uPT (-)'.

questions.q: Which three per-vaginal findings trigger the syndromic PID kit?
options: Uterine tenderness, cervical motion tenderness and adnexal tenderness
Uterine enlargement, adnexal mass and cervical erosion
Cervical motion tenderness, discharge and fever
Adnexal tenderness, abdominal rigidity and rebound
questions.why: The indications list any one of uterine, cervical motion or adnexal tenderness.

questions.q: Fill up: The syndromic advice includes abstinence and the use of ____.
questions.why: 'Advice: Abstinence x 7-14 days, Use of condoms'.

questions.q: Match each kit with its recipient - 1) Patient 2) Partner ... A) Grey kit 1 B) Yellow kit 6
questions.why: The patient takes yellow kit 6 and the partner grey kit 1.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with lower abdominal pain and cervical motion tenderness has a positive urine pregnancy test. What is the printed next step?
options: Rule out ectopic pregnancy before using the PID kit
questions.why: 'Ensure uPT (-)' and the standing instruction to rule out ectopic pregnancy precede kit use.

questions.q: True/False: In the syndromic approach, the partner receives the same yellow kit as the patient.
options: True - the partner receives double the dose
questions.why: The partner receives grey kit 1 with cefixime and azithromycin.

questions.q: Odd one out - which drug is NOT in the syndromic PID patient kit?
questions.why: Azithromycin is in the partner's grey kit, not the patient's yellow kit.

questions.q: Fill up: The pathogenesis is numbered through uterus, tubes, ovaries and finally peritonitis with pelvic ____.
questions.why: Step 4 prints 'Peritonitis + pelvic abscess'.

questions.q: Which phrase describes the tubal appearance in salpingitis?
options: Dilated with a lead pipe outline
questions.why: The printed descriptors are thick, congested, hyperemic and swollen.

questions.q: Fill up: In reproductive-age women, chlamydia exceeds ____ as a cause of PID.
questions.why: Printed: 'Reproductive age: Chlamydia > Gonorrhea'.

questions.q: Which organism is specifically linked to copper IUD use in the printed list?
questions.why: 'Cu-IUD users: Actinomyces'.

questions.q: Fill up: The waist sign is captioned as ____ and the cogwheel sign as thickened endosalpingeal walls.
questions.why: The caption prints 'Waist sign (Hydrosalpinx)'.

questions.q: Which investigation pairs with 'beads on string' in the printed note?
questions.why: The note prints 'USG: PID / Beads on string' and 'HSG: Genital TB'.

questions.q: Which statement about HSG in this chapter is correct?
options: HSG is the gold standard for PID
HSG belongs to the genital tuberculosis chapter, not to PID diagnostics here
HSG is the screening test for PID
questions.why: The note assigns HSG to genital TB; PID imaging is by USG.

questions.q: Fill up: The laparoscopy note says the operator can visualise tubes, adnexa and ____ directly.
questions.why: 'Visualize tubes, adnexa, uterus directly'.

questions.q: Which two diagnoses must be excluded before labelling pelvic pain as PID?
questions.why: The D/d block lists ectopic pregnancy and appendicitis.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman has lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness and a temperature of 101.5 degrees Fahrenheit. Which CDC tier is satisfied?
options: Both the minimum criteria and the additional criteria
questions.why: Pain plus cervical motion tenderness meets the minimum criteria, and the temperature above 101 F meets an additional criterion.

questions.q: True/False: A raised ESR and CRP are part of the CDC minimum criteria for PID.
questions.why: They belong to the additional criteria.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT among the three per-vaginal minimum-criteria findings?
questions.why: A mass is not a minimum criterion; tenderness findings are.

questions.q: Fill up: The intramuscular cephalosporin in the OPD regimen is ____, given as a single dose.
questions.why: 'Inj. Ceftriaxone 250mg IM single dose'.

questions.q: Which two oral antibiotics in the OPD regimen share the same 14-day duration?
questions.why: Both are printed as twice daily for 14 days.

questions.q: Fill up: Pelvic ____ is the second indication for admission.
questions.why: '2. Pelvic abscess'.

questions.q: Why is pregnancy singled out among the admission indications?
options: Severe disease or inability to take oral medication in pregnancy warrants admission
questions.why: Both pregnancy indications are clinical severity and inability to take oral drugs.

questions.q: Fill up: The list of six consequences begins with infertility and ends with Fitz-Hugh-Curtis ____.
questions.why: Item 6 is Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome.

questions.q: Which two of the six consequences directly reflect tubal damage?
options: Chronic pelvic pain and recurrent PID
questions.why: Tubal damage produces infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

questions.q: Fill up: Alcohol is to be avoided because of the ____ in the regimen.
questions.why: 'Avoid alcohol (metronidazole)'.

questions.q: What is the printed duration of abstinence after PID treatment?
questions.why: 'Abstinence x 7-14 days'.

questions.q: Fill up: The syndromic patient kit is yellow kit 6; the partner kit is grey kit ____.
questions.why: Partner: No. 1 grey kit.

questions.q: Which drug is common to the OPD regimen and the syndromic patient kit?
questions.why: Metronidazole 400 mg BD appears in both the OPD regimen and yellow kit 6.

questions.q: Which drug appears in the partner kit but not in the patient's yellow kit?
questions.why: The partner receives cefixime plus azithromycin; the patient receives cefixime, metronidazole and doxycycline.

questions.q: Match each PID consequence with its number - 1) Infertility 2) Ectopic pregnancy 3) Chronic pelvic pain 4) Recurrent PID ... A) 5 B) 2 C) 1 (m/c) D) 3
questions.why: Infertility is 1 and most common; ectopic pregnancy 2; chronic pelvic pain 3; recurrent PID 5.

questions.q: Scenario: A patient with PID has completed 24 hours without fever on intravenous antibiotics. What is the printed next step?
options: Switch to oral antibiotics for a total of 14 days
Continue intravenous therapy for another 7 days
questions.why: IV therapy continues 24 hours past defervescence, then oral antibiotics for 14 days.

questions.q: True/False: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome appears both as an acute complication on the features page and as item 6 in the consequence list.
options: False - it appears only on the features page
False - it appears only in the consequences list
questions.why: It is printed under complications on p185 and again as item 6 on p187.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed admission indication?
options: Pregnant patient unable to take oral medication
questions.why: Hydrosalpinx is a numbered consequence, not an admission indication.

questions.q: Fill up: The causative organism printed is ____ tuberculosis.
questions.why: Page 188 names 'Causative organism (mycobacterium tuberculosis)'.

questions.q: The primary source of infection is printed as:
questions.why: '1° source: Lung > LNs'.

questions.q: Fill up: The classic route of spread to the genital tract is ____.
questions.why: 'Hematogenous route' heads the pathogenesis flow.

questions.q: Which second, less common route is printed?
questions.why: 'Transmission: Sexual' appears in the diagram.

questions.q: Fill up: The organism enters and first involves the ____ tube.
questions.why: 'Enters Fallopian Tube (FT)'.

questions.q: How is the tubal lining destroyed?
questions.why: 'Lining destroyed from within → Endosalpingitis'.

questions.q: Fill up: In genital tuberculosis the tubal lining is destroyed from within, producing ____.
questions.why: The chain prints 'Endosalpingitis → Caseous necrosis → Fibrosis/Adhesion'.

questions.q: Which three pathological stages follow endosalpingitis?
questions.why: The printed sequence is caseous necrosis then fibrosis or adhesion.

questions.q: Fill up: The tubal damage culminates in ____ cornual block.
questions.why: 'B/L cornual block'.

questions.q: From the uterus the infection spreads to the:
questions.why: 'From uterus: Spreads to Endometrium'.

questions.q: Fill up: Fimbrial spread causes adhesions and ____.
questions.why: 'Fimbriae spread: Causes adhesions, Causes hydrosalpinx'.

questions.q: Match each step of the tubal pathogenesis with its position - 1) Lining destroyed from within 2) Caseous necrosis 3) Fibrosis or adhesion 4) Bilateral cornual block ... A) 4 B) 1 C) 3 D) 2
questions.why: The flow is endosalpingitis, caseous necrosis, fibrosis or adhesion, then bilateral cornual block.

questions.q: Scenario: A young woman with infertility is found to have bilateral cornual block on HSG. Which organism does the printed pathogenesis point to?
questions.why: Bilateral cornual block is the end point of the genital tuberculosis tubal chain.

questions.q: True/False: The fallopian tube is the first genital structure involved because the organism reaches it by the haematogenous route.
options: False - the ovary is involved first
False - the endometrium is involved first
questions.why: The diagram shows haematogenous seeding entering the fallopian tube first.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed route or source in the pathogenesis diagram?
questions.why: Ascending spread along sperms belongs to PID and cervicitis, not genital tuberculosis.

questions.q: Fill up: Genital tuberculosis of the tube is ____ (bilateral or unilateral).
questions.why: The sites block prints 'B/L'.

questions.q: Which part of the tube is most commonly affected?
questions.why: 'm/c site: Ampulla > Isthmus'.

questions.q: The most common presentation is:
questions.why: 'm/c presentation: Infertility'.

questions.q: Fill up: The investigation of choice for tubal patency is ____.
questions.why: 'IOC for tubal patency: HSG (Hysterosalpingography)'.

questions.q: Why is HSG contraindicated in untreated genital tuberculosis?
questions.why: '- C/I: Can lead to dissemination'.

questions.q: When is HSG performed in genital tuberculosis?
questions.why: '- Done after ATT (Anti-Tuberculosis Treatment)'.

questions.q: How many characteristic appearances on HSG are printed?
questions.why: Beaded, lead pipe, tobacco pouch, golf stick, bilateral cornual block, cotton wool and hydrosalpinx.

questions.q: Which three HSG appearances are illustrated with labelled figures?
options: Beaded appearance, tobacco pouch appearance and lead pipe appearance
Golf stick, cotton wool and hydrosalpinx
Beaded, golf stick and cornual block
Lead pipe, cotton wool and hydrosalpinx
questions.why: The figures are captioned beaded appearance, tobacco pouch appearance and lead pipe appearance.

questions.q: Fill up: The appearance resembling a smoking pipe is called the ____ appearance.
questions.why: 'Tobacco pouch appearance'.

questions.q: Which appearance is described as a golf stick?
questions.why: The printed item is 'Golfstick appearance'.

questions.q: Fill up: A fluffy, ill-defined outline on HSG is the ____ appearance.
questions.why: 'Cotton wool appearance'.

questions.q: The 'lead pipe' appearance describes a tube that is:
questions.why: The lead pipe appearance is the rigid, pipe-like outline of a fibrosed tube.

questions.q: Match each HSG appearance with its descriptor - 1) Beaded 2) Lead pipe 3) Tobacco pouch 4) Cotton wool ... A) Rigid pipe-like tube B) Fluffy ill-defined outline C) Sac-like distal collection D) Alternating constrictions and dilatations
questions.why: Beaded is alternating constrictions; lead pipe is rigid; tobacco pouch is a distal sac; cotton wool is fluffy.

questions.q: Scenario: A patient with suspected genital tuberculosis needs tubal assessment. What is the correct printed sequence?
options: Start anti-tuberculous treatment first, then perform HSG
Perform HSG and then decide on treatment
Perform laparoscopy instead, as HSG is never used
questions.why: HSG is contraindicated before treatment because of dissemination risk and is done after ATT.

questions.q: True/False: HSG is the investigation of choice for tubal patency and is safe at any stage of genital tuberculosis.
options: True - it is safe after the first month
True - dissemination only occurs with laparoscopy
questions.why: It is contraindicated before treatment because it can disseminate infection.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed HSG appearance in genital tuberculosis?
questions.why: Violin string adhesions belong to Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome in the PID chapter.

sections.name: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum

units.title: Genital Tuberculosis of the Uterus, Ovaries and Peritoneum

questions.q: Fill up: In genital tuberculosis of the uterus, the ____ layers of the endometrium are affected.
questions.why: 'Affected: Superficial layers of endometrium'.

questions.q: Which layer is spared?
questions.why: 'Spared: myometrium'.

questions.q: Fill up: Because only the superficial layers are involved, ____ day menstrual blood can be used for investigation.
questions.why: '1st day menstrual blood can be used for Investigation'.

questions.q: Which phase is printed as the best time for endometrial biopsy?
questions.why: 'Best time for endometrial biopsy: premenstrual'.

questions.q: Initially, when the endometrium is still normal, the menstrual pattern is:
questions.why: 'Initially: endometrium normal → No menstrual symptoms'.

questions.q: Fill up: In the acute stage, endometritis causes ____.
questions.why: 'Acute: Endometritis → menorrhagia'.

questions.q: In the chronic stage, adhesions produce:
options: Asherman syndrome with secondary amenorrhoea or oligomenorrhoea
questions.why: 'Chronic: Adhesions (Asherman syndrome) → 2° amenorrhea/oligomenorrhea'.

questions.q: Fill up: Ovarian tuberculosis is limited to the surface of the ovary by the tunica ____.
questions.why: 'TB limited to: Surface of ovary by Tunica albuginea → Prevents spread to stroma'.

questions.q: What keeps ovarian tuberculosis confined to the surface?
options: The tunica albuginea prevents spread to the stroma
The ovary has no lymphatic supply
questions.why: The printed mechanism is the tunica albuginea blocking stromal spread.

questions.q: Fill up: On laparoscopy the ovary shows ____ on its surface.
questions.why: 'Appearance: Tubercles on surface of ovary (on laparoscopy)'.

questions.q: Tubercular peritonitis associated with genital tuberculosis produces:
questions.why: 'Genital TB associated with peritonitis → Ascites'.

questions.q: Match each site with its printed feature - 1) Tube 2) Uterus 3) Ovary 4) Peritoneum ... A) Ascites B) Tubercles on the surface C) Ampulla most common D) Myometrium spared
questions.why: Tube: ampulla; uterus: myometrium spared; ovary: surface tubercles; peritoneum: ascites.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with genital tuberculosis develops secondary amenorrhoea. Which printed mechanism explains it?
options: Chronic endometrial adhesions producing Asherman syndrome
questions.why: The chronic uterine stage produces adhesions (Asherman syndrome) with secondary amenorrhoea.

questions.q: True/False: Genital tuberculosis typically destroys the myometrium.
options: True - the myometrium is the main target
questions.why: Only the superficial endometrium is affected and the myometrium is spared.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed site feature of genital tuberculosis?
options: Cervical ulceration as the commonest finding
questions.why: The common presentations are tubal; cervical ulceration is not printed as the commonest finding.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common age group affected is ____ years.
questions.why: 'm/c age group: 20-30 years'.

questions.q: Genital tuberculosis is the most common cause of PID in:
questions.why: 'm/c cause of PID in virgin females'.

questions.q: Fill up: The fever of genital tuberculosis is described as ____ grade.
questions.why: 'Prodromal Symptoms: Fever (Low grade)'.

questions.q: Which three prodromal symptoms are printed?
options: Low grade fever, malaise and loss of appetite with weight loss
questions.why: The prodromal list is fever, malaise and decreased appetite with weight loss.

questions.q: Fill up: The commonest presentation is infertility due to ____ blockage.
questions.why: 'm/c: Infertility d/t Tubal blockage'.

questions.q: Initially the menstrual abnormality is:
questions.why: 'Initially: menorrhagia d/t endometritis'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common menstrual abnormality is secondary ____ or hypomenorrhoea.
questions.why: 'm/c: 2° amenorrhea / hypomenorrhea d/t Asherman syndrome'.

questions.q: Which pain symptom is marked as variable?
questions.why: '± Chronic pelvic pain' uses the plus-minus sign.

questions.q: Fill up: The rare discharge is described as ____ (blood stained).
questions.why: 'Rare: Serosanguinous (Blood stained) discharge'.

questions.q: Which future risk is flagged?
questions.why: 'Future risk of: ectopic pregnancy'.

questions.q: Match each clinical item with its descriptor - 1) Infertility 2) Menorrhagia 3) Secondary amenorrhoea 4) Serosanguinous discharge ... A) Most common menstrual abnormality B) Rare C) Initial menstrual abnormality D) Most common presentation
questions.why: Infertility is the commonest presentation; menorrhagia is initial; secondary amenorrhoea becomes commonest; the discharge is rare.

questions.q: Scenario: An 18-year-old virgin presents with pelvic inflammatory disease that has not responded to broad-spectrum antibiotics. Which diagnosis should be considered?
questions.why: Genital TB is the commonest cause of PID in virgins and is flagged in the diagnostic history list.

questions.q: True/False: Genital tuberculosis most commonly presents with menorrhagia.
options: True - bleeding is the cardinal symptom
questions.why: Infertility is the commonest presentation; menorrhagia is only the initial menstrual change.
