questions.q: The three malignancies with increased risk listed under Klinefelter syndrome are ____, ____ and ____.
options: Prostate adenocarcinoma; seminoma only; renal cell carcinoma
Thyroid medullary cancer; chronic myeloid leukaemia; choriocarcinoma
Breast cancer; Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma; extragonadal germ cell tumour
Hepatocellular carcinoma; Hodgkin lymphoma; Wilms tumour
questions.why: Source (scan 205): '• ↑ Risk of Breast cancer, Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, Extragonadal germ cell tumour'.

questions.q: Which is NOT in the source's increased-tumour-risk list for Klinefelter syndrome?
questions.why: Source (scan 205): breast cancer, Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, and extragonadal germ cell tumour are the three listed tumours.

questions.q: The final bullet under Klinefelter characteristics prints ____ lifespan and ____ IQ.
questions.why: Source (scan 205): '• ↓ Life span, ↓ IQ.' Clarification: clinically, cognitive and survival outcomes in 47,XXY vary widely (many individuals have normal general intelligence with selective verbal/executive differences).

questions.q: The string of numbered ellipsoid beads (`1` to `25`) illustrated beside Klinefelter syndrome is the ____, which ____.
options: Leech Wilkinson cannula; injects HSG dye
questions.why: Source (scan 205): figure caption 'Prader orchidometer (measures testis size)'.

questions.q: Under `Spermatogenesis & Sperm pathway`, male infertility is bracketed as arising from two broad mechanisms: ____ and ____.
options: Defect in spermatogenesis; obstruction in sperm passage
Failure of capacitation; failure of acrosome loss
Absent seminal fructose; excess prostatic zinc
questions.why: Source (scan 205): '{ • Defect in spermatogenesis. • Obstruction in sperm passage. } → Infertility in males.'

questions.q: In the HPG diagram on scan 205, spermatogenesis begins at ____ and takes place in the ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 205): 'Spermatogenesis : Begins at puberty' and bottom label 'Spermatogenesis in Seminiferous tubule'.

questions.q: Tracing the top of the HPG diagram: the hypothalamus secretes ____ to stimulate the ____ to release FSH and LH, with positive (`⊕`) arrows from FSH, LH and testosterone toward ____.
options: Dopamine; median eminence; fructose synthesis in Leydig cells
TRH; posterior pituitary; spermiation in the vas deferens
Inhibin B; adrenal zona reticularis; epididymal capacitation
GnRH; anterior pituitary; spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubule
questions.why: Source (scan 205): 'Hypothalamus → GnRH → Anterior pituitary → FSH & LH', with ⊕ arrows leading down to 'Spermatogenesis in Seminiferous tubule'.

questions.q: Match anterior-pituitary gonadotropins with their testicular target cells in the diagram: 1) FSH 2) LH — A) Leydig cells B) Sertoli cells.
questions.why: Source (scan 205): 'FSH → Sertoli cells' and 'LH → Leydig cells'.

questions.q: In the testicular endocrine diagram, Sertoli cells secrete ____ while Leydig cells secrete ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 205): 'Sertoli cells → Inhibin B' and 'Leydig cells → Testosterone'.

questions.q: Evaluate the dashed negative-feedback (`⊖`) arrows in the scan 205 HPG diagram: I) Inhibin B sends a negative-feedback arrow to FSH. II) Testosterone sends a negative-feedback arrow to hypothalamic GnRH while stimulating spermatogenesis (`⊕`).
questions.why: Source (scan 205): dashed ⊖ arrows run from Inhibin B to FSH and from Testosterone back to GnRH.

questions.q: Order the four transport structures numbered along the `Sperm pathway` diagram: A) `3. Vas deferens` B) `1. Testis` C) `2. Epididymis (motile + mature)` D) `7. Ejaculatory duct`.
questions.why: Source (scan 205): traces 1. Testis → 2. Epididymis : motile + mature → 3. Vas deferens → 7. Ejaculatory duct (note: the stylized pointer line for 7 sits distally on the sketch, whereas anatomically the ejaculatory duct traverses the prostate to enter the prostatic urethra).

questions.q: In the `Sperm pathway` diagram, `4. Seminal vesicle` pours secretions that are rich in ____ and form a ____ component of semen.
questions.why: Source (scan 205): '4. Seminal vesicle : Pours secretions • Rich in fructose • Major component of semen.'

questions.q: Alongside `4. Seminal vesicle` and `5. Prostate`, structure `6.` pouring secretions into the pathway is the ____, also called ____ gland.
questions.why: Source (scan 205): '5. Prostate : Pours secretions. 6. Bulbourethral/Cowper's gland : Pours secretions.'

questions.q: Among the seven numbered labels in the `Sperm pathway` diagram, which structure produces spermatozoa rather than transporting them or pouring accessory secretions?
questions.why: Source (scan 205): spermatogenesis occurs in the seminiferous tubules of 1. Testis; epididymis/vas/ejaculatory duct transport sperm and vesicles/prostate/Cowper's gland pour secretions.

sections.name: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm

units.title: Levels of dysfunction and azoospermia algorithm

questions.q: Match `Levels of organs involved in spermatogenesis` at the top of scan 206: 1) Pre-testicular organs 2) Testicular organs 3) Post-testicular organs — A) Testis B) Hypothalamus and pituitary C) Seminal vesicles, epididymis, ejaculatory duct, vas deferens.
questions.why: Source (scan 206 / printed 198): reproduces all three organ levels and all four named post-testicular structures verbatim.

questions.q: Evaluate the two functional bullets under `Post-testicular organs`: I) They are necessary for sperm passage. II) They are necessary for spermatogenesis itself.
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '• Not necessary for spermatogenesis. • Necessary for sperm passage.'

questions.q: Under `Semen` (listing seminal vesicle, prostate gland, and bulbourethral gland), `Prostatic enzymes` cause ____ of semen.
questions.why: Source (scan 206): 'Semen : • Seminal vesicle. • Prostate gland : Prostatic enzymes → Liquefaction of semen.'

questions.q: Under `Semen`, the `Bulbourethral gland` adds its secretion at the time of ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '• Bulbourethral gland : Adds secretion at the time of intercourse.'

questions.q: [Scenario] A patient has `Azoospermia in 1st semen analysis`. What is the immediate next step in the `AZOOSPERMIA ON SEMEN ANALYSIS` flowchart before endocrine testing?
options: Measure serum FSH, LH and testosterone immediately without repeating semen
questions.why: Source (scan 206): 'Azoospermia in 1st semen analysis → Repeat semen analysis → Azoospermia → FSH, LH, Testosterone levels.'

questions.q: In the box beside `Repeat semen analysis`, the `Ideal` interval is after ____ and the `Min` interval is after ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 206): boxed note '• Ideal : After 1 month. • Min : After 7 days.'

questions.q: Once repeat semen analysis confirms azoospermia, the next investigation line measures ____ levels.
options: Seminal zinc, citric acid and PSA
questions.why: Source (scan 206): 'Azoospermia → FSH, LH, Testosterone levels.'

questions.q: [Scenario] Confirmed azoospermia with `↓ FSH & ↓ Testosterone` maps to which endocrine state and anatomical level in the left branch?
options: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism due to hypothalamus/pituitary causes
Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism due to testicular causes
Obstructive azoospermia due to post-testicular block
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '↓ FSH & ↓ Testosterone → Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism → Hypothalamus/pituitary causes'.

questions.q: The three numbered `Hypothalamus/pituitary causes` of azoospermia listed in the left branch are ____, ____ and ____.
options: Klinefelter syndrome; testicular tumour; mumps orchitis
Young's syndrome; Kartagener syndrome; genital TB
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '1. Kallman syndrome. 2. Hyperprolactinemia d/t -ve feedback on GnRH. 3. Chronic hypothyroidism : ↓ T3 → ↑ TRH → ↑ TSH, ↑ Prolactin.'

questions.q: Which is NOT in the left-branch list of hypothalamic/pituitary hypogonadotropic causes?
questions.why: Source (scan 206): mumps orchitis sits in the middle (testicular) branch.

questions.q: In item `2.` of the hypogonadotropic branch, hyperprolactinaemia causes azoospermia via negative feedback on ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '2. Hyperprolactinemia d/t -ve feedback on GnRH.'

questions.q: Arrange the endocrine chain written for `3. Chronic hypothyroidism` in the azoospermia diagram: A) `↑ TRH` B) `↓ T3` C) `↑ TSH, ↑ Prolactin`.
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '3. Chronic hypothyroidism : ↓ T3 → ↑ TRH → ↑ TSH, ↑ Prolactin.'

questions.q: [Scenario] Confirmed azoospermia with `↑ FSH & ↓ Testosterone` maps to which diagnosis and frequency label in the middle branch?
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '↑ FSH & ↓ Testosterone → Hypergonadotropic hypogonadism → Testicular cause : m/c'.

questions.q: The four numbered `Testicular cause` examples under hypergonadotropic hypogonadism are ____, ____, ____ and ____.
options: Klinefelter syndrome; testicular tumour; mumps orchitis; increased heat exposure (miners)
Varicocele; cystic fibrosis; vasectomy; genital TB
Hypospadias; premature ejaculation; erectile dysfunction; retrograde ejaculation
Kallmann syndrome; hyperprolactinaemia; chronic hypothyroidism; pituitary adenoma
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '1. Klinefelter syndrome. 2. Testicular tumor 3. Mumps orchitis. 4. ↑ Heat exposure (miners).'

questions.q: Which is outside the middle-branch testicular-cause list on scan 206?
questions.why: Source (scan 206): vasectomy is in the right-hand obstructive branch.

questions.q: For testicular cause `4. ↑ Heat exposure`, the parenthetical occupation named in the notes is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 206): '4. ↑ Heat exposure (miners).'

questions.q: [Scenario] Confirmed azoospermia with `Normal FSH & Normal Testosterone` enters which right-hand branch of the scan 206 algorithm?
questions.why: Source (scan 206): 'Normal FSH & Normal Testosterone → Obstructive azoospermia → Obstruction in sperm pathway'. Clarification: clinically, maturation arrest can also present with normal FSH and testosterone, so normal hormones favour—rather than prove—obstruction.

questions.q: Alongside `1. Varicocele` (flagged separately), items `2` to `5` printed under `Obstruction in sperm pathway` are ____, ____, ____ and ____.
options: Cystic fibrosis; vasectomy; retrograde ejaculation; genital TB
Klinefelter syndrome; mumps orchitis; miners; testicular tumour
Hypospadias; vaginismus; erectile dysfunction; premature ejaculation
Kallmann syndrome; hyperprolactinaemia; hypothyroidism; Kartagener syndrome
questions.why: Source (scan 206): lists '1. Varicocele. 2. Cystic fibrosis. 3. Vasectomy 4. Retrograde ejaculation. 5. Genital TB'. (Note: retrograde ejaculation is a functional antegrade-emission disorder rather than an anatomical lumen block, though grouped here under post-testicular pathway causes.)

questions.q: Which is NOT among the five items printed under `Obstruction in sperm pathway` on scan 206?
questions.why: Source (scan 206): Kallmann syndrome is in the pretesticular hypothalamic/pituitary branch.

questions.q: Source-check: `1. Varicocele` is printed as the first item under `Obstructive azoospermia / Obstruction in sperm pathway` on scan 206. What medical clarification is essential?
options: Varicocele causes congenital bilateral agenesis of both seminal vesicles
Varicocele impairs testicular spermatogenesis (heat/stasis), not ductal passage
Varicocele mechanically obliterates the distal ejaculatory duct on TRUS
Varicocele is a central hypothalamic GnRH-deficiency endocrine syndrome
questions.why: Source (scan 206): keep awareness that the notes list '1. Varicocele' under the right-hand branch, but clinically varicocele is a non-obstructive testicular cause (thermoregulatory/oxidative dysfunction), not a ductal obstruction.

questions.q: [Scenario] In the `Obstructive azoospermia` flowchart at the top of scan 207, semen shows `Low semen volume, ↓ Fructose`. Loss of contribution from which structure is inferred?
questions.why: Source (scan 207 / printed 199): 'Low semen volume, ↓ Fructose → No contribution from seminal vesicle.'

questions.q: When low semen volume and low fructose indicate no seminal-vesicle contribution, the next imaging test in the algorithm is ____ to assess the ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'No contribution from seminal vesicle → Trans rectal ultrasound → Seminal vesicles'.

questions.q: [Scenario] On transrectal ultrasound for low-volume, low-fructose azoospermia, the seminal vesicles are `Not seen`. What condition, anatomical defect, and confirmatory test follow this branch?
options: Ejaculatory duct obstruction with mega-vesicles; confirmed by Endtz test
Cystic fibrosis with absence of vas deferens and seminal vesicle; confirmed by CFTR gene mutation
Retrograde ejaculation with normal vasa; confirmed by scrotal USG
Klinefelter syndrome with streak vasa; confirmed by 47,XXY karyotype
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Seminal vesicles → Not seen → Cystic fibrosis : Absence of vas deferens & seminal vesicle → Confirmation : CFTR gene mutation.'

questions.q: [Scenario] On transrectal ultrasound in the low-volume, low-fructose branch, seminal vesicles are `Seen` and `Dilated`. Which diagnosis is shown?
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Seminal vesicles → Seen → Dilated → Ejaculatory duct obstruction.'

questions.q: [Scenario] On transrectal ultrasound in the low-volume, low-fructose branch, seminal vesicles are `Seen` and `Normal`. Which diagnosis does the diagram assign?
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Seminal vesicles → Seen → Normal → Retrograde ejaculation.' (Clinically confirmed by finding sperm in post-ejaculatory urine.)

questions.q: [Scenario] In the right-hand branch of `Obstructive azoospermia`, semen has `Normal semen volume, Fructose +`. What inference and block site follow?
options: Seminal-vesicle agenesis confirmed → block at prostatic urethral crest
Hostile cervical mucus barrier → mechanical block at external os
Pituitary gonadotropin deficiency → isolated block inside rete testis
Seminal-vesicle contribution intact → block above it (vas or epididymis)
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Normal semen volume, Fructose + → Contribution of seminal vesicle to semen → Block above seminal vesicle • Vas deferens • Epididymus.'

questions.q: When obstruction is localised above the seminal vesicle (`Vas deferens` / `Epididymus`), the imaging step below it is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Block above seminal vesicle (• Vas deferens • Epididymus) → Scrotal USG'.

questions.q: Under `Treatment Procedures`, `INTRAUTERINE INSEMINATION` is defined in the opening line as ____.
options: Injecting a single sperm into oocyte cytoplasm
Co-incubating gametes in a pyruvate Petri dish
Placing gametes laparoscopically into the ampulla
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'INTRAUTERINE INSEMINATION : Injecting sperm into uterus.'

questions.q: The two `Prerequisite` thresholds printed for IUI on scan 207 are sperm concentration ____ and sperm morphology ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Prerequisite : • Sperm concentration : 10 million/ml. • Sperm morphology : 14%.' Clarification: 14% reflects older pre-2010 WHO morphology criteria rather than the 4% Strict Tygerberg WHO 2022 limit on scan 204; modern IUI eligibility commonly relies on post-wash total motile sperm count.

questions.q: Match `Obtaining semen` labels for IUI: 1) From husband 2) From donor — A) `IUI-D` B) `IUI-H`.
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Obtaining semen : • From husband : IUI-H. • From donor : IUI-D.'

questions.q: The four `Processing of semen` techniques listed before IUI (producing `Sperm in sterile medium`) are ____, ____, ____ and ____.
options: Formalin fixation; saline wash; lignocaine gel; pyruvate freezing
Swim-up; swim-down; density centrifugation; glass-wool filtration
Eosin staining; trypan blue; hypo-osmotic swelling; Endtz assay
questions.why: Source (scan 207): lists all four techniques under 'Processing of semen', alongside the vial captioned 'Sperm in sterile medium'.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four semen-processing techniques listed for IUI on scan 207?
questions.why: Source (scan 207): swim-up, swim-down, density centrifugation, and glass-wool filtration are the four listed methods.

questions.q: Among the four listed semen-processing methods, the one explicitly labelled `Best` in the notes is the ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 207): '• Glasswool filtration technique : Best.' (source-specific teaching superlative; density-gradient and swim-up are widely used in contemporary andrology labs).

questions.q: In the IUI `Procedure` flowchart, ____ of concentrated processed sperm is injected into the uterus using an ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Procedure : 0.5 mL of conc. processed sperm → Injected into uterus with IUI catheter, bypassing cervix → Sperm travel to fallopian tube.'

questions.q: [Scenario] According to the IUI `Procedure` arrows and pelvic illustration (`Sperm injected into uterus`), why can IUI overcome a cervical factor yet still require tubal patency?
options: Catheter bypasses the cervix, after which sperm still travel to the tube
Catheter mechanically dilates bilateral fimbrial hydrosalpinx ostia
Catheter injects capacitated sperm directly into the ovarian follicle
Catheter deposits day-5 blastocysts 2 cm below the uterine fundus
questions.why: Source (scan 207): 'Injected into uterus with IUI catheter, bypassing cervix → Sperm travel to fallopian tube.'

sections.name: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline

units.title: IUI indications, ART grouping and IVF outline

questions.q: At the top of scan 208, IUI is broadly summarised as `Done in` ____ and ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 208 / printed 200): 'Done in : • Cervix abnormalities. • Ejaculatory abnormalities.'

questions.q: [Scenario] Immediately below `Done in`, the line `Not done : In females with ____` excludes IUI in which setting?
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'Not done : In females with tubal blockage.' (Compare scan 200, where unilateral tubal block can still use CC + IUI, whereas bilateral tubal blockage precludes IUI.)

questions.q: Under `Note : Assisted Reproductive Techniques`, ART `Includes` the four procedures ____, ____, ____ and ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'Note : Assisted Reproductive Techniques • Includes : - IVF - ICSI - GIFT - ZIFT • Does not include IUI.'

questions.q: Which procedure is explicitly excluded (`Does not include`) from the `Assisted Reproductive Techniques` group on scan 208?
questions.why: Source (scan 208): '• Does not include IUI.'

questions.q: Alongside IVF, ICSI and GIFT, the fourth procedure in the ART list is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 208): '- ZIFT' (zygote intrafallopian transfer) completes the four-item ART list.

questions.q: Under IUI `Indications` on scan 208, the sperm-count range written beside `Oligospermia` is ____ (whereas the summary table on scan 210 writes `10–15 million/mL`).
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'Indications : • Oligospermia : 10–16 million/mL.' (reflecting <16 million/mL WHO oligospermia down to the 10 million/mL IUI prerequisite).

questions.q: Match three IUI indications on scan 208 with their descriptions/categories: 1) Hypospadias 2) Antisperm antibodies in cervix 3) Vaginismus — A) Cervical immunological factor B) Ejaculatory cause C) Involuntary contraction of vaginal muscles.
questions.why: Source (scan 208): '• Ejaculatory causes : Hypospadias', '• Vaginismus : Involuntary contraction of vaginal muscles', and '• Anti sperm antibodies in cervix'.

questions.q: Completing the eight-bullet IUI `Indications` list on scan 208 alongside oligospermia, hypospadias, vaginismus and cervical antisperm antibodies are ____, ____, ____ and ____.
options: Retrograde ejaculation; discordant HIV status in the partners; mild endometriosis; unexplained infertility
Severe endometriosis; bilateral hydrosalpinx; azoospermia; premature ovarian insufficiency
Mullerian agenesis; Kartagener asthenospermia <5%; Klinefelter syndrome; PGT
Pituitary ablation; Kallmann syndrome; cervical cancer; Asherman syndrome
questions.why: Source (scan 208): directly tests the remaining four bullets in the two-column IUI Indications list. (Clarification: in HIV-discordant couples, modern care relies on antiretroviral viral suppression ± sperm washing per current guidelines.)

questions.q: Which is NOT among the eight listed indications for IUI on scan 208?
options: Discordant HIV status in the partners
questions.why: Source (scan 208): tubal blockage precludes IUI; severe hydrosalpinx requires proximal clipping/salpingectomy + IVF.

questions.q: The first bullet in the `Note` above IVF states: `IUI done at the time of` ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'Note : • IUI done at the time of ovulation.'

questions.q: Source-check: the second bullet in that `Note` reads `HCG is done before IUI to rule out tubal blockage`. What error in the handwritten note must be recognised?
options: `HSG` is an intramuscular gonadotropin injected 36 hours prior to IUI
`HSG` (hysterosalpingography), not `HCG`, tests tubal patency; hCG triggers ovulation
Neither tubal-patency imaging nor ovulation timing is needed before IUI
Injection `hCG` is instilled transcervically to opacify fallopian spill on X-ray
questions.why: Source (scan 208): the note miswrites 'HCG' where 'HSG' (hysterosalpingography) is meant for ruling out tubal blockage.

questions.q: Under `IN VITRO FERTILISATION`, the stated `Pre-requisite` is `Sperm count` : ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'IN VITRO FERTILISATION Pre-requisite : Sperm count : 5 million/mL.' (5–10 million/mL is directed to conventional IVF, <5 million/mL to ICSI in this chapter).

questions.q: Order the female steps in the IVF `Procedure` overview on scan 208: A) Trigger ovulation B) Stimulate ovary C) Follicular monitoring in TVS (`Follicle > 17mm`) D) `2° Oocyte` picked up under US guidance.
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'Females : Stimulate ovary → Follicular monitoring in TVS → Follicle > 17mm → Trigger ovulation → Ovulation occurs → Same day 2° Oocyte picked up under US guidance.'

questions.q: In the scan 208 IVF overview flowchart, the follicle threshold written above `Trigger ovulation` is ____ (refined on scan 209 to `≥2 follicles with ≥17 mm`).
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'Follicular monitoring in TVS → Follicle > 17mm → Trigger ovulation.'

questions.q: In the `Males` arm of the IVF flowchart, the semen sample is collected on ____ and then ____.
options: Three days after embryo transfer; stained with eosin
The day of oocyte pick-up; processed
The day of HSG; left unwashed
Day 2 of the female cycle; frozen in formalin
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'Males : Semen sample collected on the day of oocyte pick up → Semen processed.'

questions.q: In the female IVF arm, the gamete retrieved is a ____ oocyte, picked up under ____ guidance.
questions.why: Source (scan 208): '2° Oocyte picked up under US guidance.'

questions.q: [Scenario] After `2° Oocyte` pick-up and `Semen processed` join in the IVF flowchart, what happens next to achieve fertilisation?
options: A single immobilized sperm is microinjected into cytoplasm
Unwashed semen is instilled into the fallopian ampulla
Gametes are transferred immediately into the cervix
They are incubated together → fertilisation occurs in vitro
questions.why: Source (scan 208): joined arrow reads 'Incubated together → Fertilization → Embryo transfer on day 3 or 5.'

questions.q: The final line of the scan 208 IVF overview states `Embryo transfer on` ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 208): 'Embryo transfer on day 3 or 5'.

sections.name: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications

units.title: IVF stimulation, laboratory stages and indications

questions.q: Scan 209 begins under `Female ovarian stimulation` → `Controlled ovarian hyperstimulation`, where hyperstimulation yields multiple ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 209 / printed 201): 'Hyperstimulation → multiple 2° oocytes → 2–3 embryo implantation.'

questions.q: Source-check: the opening sub-bullets under `Controlled ovarian hyperstimulation` write `Success rate of IVF : 20–30%` and `multiple 2° oocytes → 2–3 embryo implantation`. What clinical caution applies to transferring 2–3 embryos?
options: Multi-embryo transfer raises twin/preterm risks; guidelines favour single-embryo transfer
Transferring three embryos eliminates dizygotic twin and triplet gestations
Routine transfer of ≥4 embryos is mandatory across all IVF age groups
Embryo transfer number has no influence on maternal or neonatal morbidity
questions.why: Source (scan 209): records the exact printed '2–3 embryo implantation' shorthand while separating it from modern single-embryo transfer safety standards.

questions.q: Under `Female ovarian stimulation`, `Drug used` is written as ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): '• Drug used : HMG/GnRH analogue.'

questions.q: Match the two `Monitoring` modalities during IVF ovarian stimulation: 1) `Follicles (on TVS)` 2) Biochemical blood monitoring — A) Serum estradiol levels B) Numbers and size.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Monitoring : • Follicles (on TVS) : Numbers, size. • Serum estradiol levels.'

questions.q: Under `Ovulation trigger`, triggering is done when there are ____ follicles measuring ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Ovulation trigger : • Done when ≥ 2 follicles with ≥ 17mm.'

questions.q: For the IVF ovulation trigger, `Drug used` is ____, and the right-hand bullet notes `Ovulation occurs ____ after Inj. hCG`.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): '• Drug used : Inj. hCG.' and '• Ovulation occurs 32–36 hrs after Inj. hCG.'

questions.q: Source-check: scan 208 wrote `Ovulation occurs → Same day 2° Oocyte picked up` and scan 209 notes `Ovulation occurs 32–36 hrs after Inj. hCG`. How is oocyte retrieval actually timed clinically?
options: Performed prior to giving the hCG trigger
Performed 48 hours after spontaneous follicular rupture into the peritoneal cavity
Scheduled ~34–36 hours after hCG trigger, just BEFORE spontaneous follicular rupture disperses the oocytes
Delayed until oocytes reach the uterine cavity on day 5
questions.why: Source (scans 208–209): clarifies the compressed note wording—retrieval captures mature 2° oocytes from intact preovulatory follicles right before rupture would occur.

questions.q: `Oocyte retrieval` is done under ____ guidance in the ____, under ____.
options: Laparotomic; labour room; spinal block obligatorily
Hysteroscopic; ward procedure room; paracervical spray only
Fluoroscopic; outpatient X-ray room; no analgesia
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Oocyte retrieval : Done under US guidance in OT, under anaesthesia.'

questions.q: `Fertilisation` in IVF is performed on ____ as oocyte retrieval.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Fertilisation : On the same day as retrieval.'

questions.q: Under `Culture media : Semen + oocyte added`, the medium is rich in ____, and ____ sperms per oocyte are added.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Culture media : Semen + oocyte added. • Rich in pyruvate. • 50,000 – 1,00,000 sperms per oocyte.'

questions.q: On the right of `Culture media`, conventional IVF fertilisation occurs in an ____, in a ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): '• Fertilisation occurs in incubator, in petri dish.'

questions.q: Match `Embryo transfer` days with their developmental stages: 1) Day 3 2) Day 5 — A) Blastocyst stage B) Cleavage stage.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Embryo transfer : • On → Day 3 : Cleavage stage ; Day 5 : Blastocyst stage (Better).'

questions.q: Between day-3 cleavage-stage and day-5 blastocyst-stage transfer, scan 209 explicitly labels ____ as `(Better)`.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Day 5 : Blastocyst stage (Better).'

questions.q: For `Embryo transfer`, the target `Site` is ____ below the uterine fundus, and the `Instrument` is ____.
options: At the internal os; Karman cannula
questions.why: Source (scan 209): '• Site : 2 cm below uterine fundus. • Instrument : Cooks catheter.'

questions.q: Which hormone is `given prior to embryo transfer`, and what is its stated role?
options: hCG alone; induces cervical mucus ferning
Clomiphene citrate; thins endometrium to <2 mm
questions.why: Source (scan 209): '• Progesterone given prior to embryo transfer → prepares endometrium for implantation.'

questions.q: `Pre-implant genetic testing` is done on a ____ embryo, and if `No abnormality` is found, the embryo is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Pre-implant genetic testing : Done on day 3/day 5 embryo. → No abnormality → Implanted'. (Clarification: clinically, trophectoderm biopsy at the day-5/6 blastocyst stage is now preferred over day-3 cleavage biopsy, and 'implanted' here means transferred into the uterus.)

questions.q: The `Cryopreservation` line states that it can be done for the ____ oocyte.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Cryopreservation : Can be done for secondary oocyte.'

questions.q: The standalone `Success rate` line repeats ____, adding that it is `↑ed by` ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Success rate : 20–30% → ↑ed by multiple embryo transfer.'

questions.q: [Scenario] While scan 209 notes `Success rate : 20–30% → ↑ed by multiple embryo transfer`, why is routine multiple-embryo transfer restricted in clinical practice?
options: Multiple transferred embryos neutralise each other's trophoblastic hCG output
Transferring >1 blastocyst causes acute bilateral tubal hydrosalpinx
Elective single-embryo transfer has a 0% clinical implantation rate
Multifetal pregnancy raises maternal-perinatal risk, so transfer count is individualised
questions.why: Source (scan 209): distinguishes the source's raw implantation-rate observation from safe clinical transfer policy.

questions.q: Match specific IVF `Indications` at the bottom of scan 209: 1) Premature ovarian insufficiency 2) Mullerian agenesis — A) IVF with donor eggs B) IVF with surrogacy.
questions.why: Source (scan 209): '• IVF with donor eggs in premature ovarian insufficiency. • IVF with surrogacy in mullerian agenesis.' (Gestational surrogacy is subject to statutory legal criteria.)

questions.q: Alongside donor-egg POI, surrogacy in Mullerian agenesis, and pre-implantation genetic testing, the other three conventional-IVF `Indications` listed on scan 209 are ____, ____ and ____.
options: Oligospermia (5–10 million/mL); tubal cause of infertility; severe endometriosis
questions.why: Source (scan 209): completes the six-bullet IVF Indications list ('Oligospermia : 5–10 million/mL', 'Tubal cause of infertility', 'Severe endometriosis').

questions.q: Which condition sits under `Not used in` rather than `Indications` for conventional IVF on scan 209?
questions.why: Source (scan 209): 'Not used in : • Severe oligospermia. • Azoospermia. • Asthenopermia.'

questions.q: Including the sixth indication bullet (`Pre-implantation genetic testing`), conventional IVF is explicitly `Not used in` which three male-factor conditions on scan 209?
options: Tubal block, severe endometriosis, and Mullerian agenesis
Premature ejaculation, varicocele with normal count, and discordant HIV
Mild oligospermia (12 million/mL), hypospadias, and erectile dysfunction
questions.why: Source (scan 209): directly tests all three bullets under 'Not used in' (which instead move to ICSI on scan 210).

sections.name: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests

units.title: ICSI, sperm retrieval, treatment table and viability tests

questions.q: Evaluate the `Procedure` bullets under `INTRACYTOPLASMIC SPERM INJECTION` (ICSI): I) Collection of the `2° oocyte` and semen is the same as in IVF. II) Multiple sperms (50,000–100,000) are injected into the cytoplasm of each oocyte.
questions.why: Source (scan 210 / printed 202): 'Procedure : • Collection of 2° oocyte & semen same as IVF. • Single sperm injected into cytoplasm of oocyte → 1 sperm/oocyte.'

questions.q: In ICSI, a ____ is injected directly into the ____ of the oocyte (`1 sperm/oocyte`).
questions.why: Source (scan 210): '• Single sperm injected into cytoplasm of oocyte → 1 sperm/oocyte.'

questions.q: The three `Indications` listed for ICSI at the top right of scan 210 are ____, ____ and ____.
options: Oligospermia (5–10 million/mL); bilateral tubal block; Mullerian agenesis
Oligospermia (10–16 million/mL); mild endometriosis; unexplained infertility
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Indications : • Severe oligospermia : < 5 million/ml. • Azoospermia. • Asthenopermia : motility < 5%.'

questions.q: Which is outside the three-item ICSI `Indications` list on scan 210?
options: Oligospermia at 12 million/mL with normal motility
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 10–15 (or 10–16) million/mL with adequate parameters is managed with IUI, not ICSI.

questions.q: Under ICSI `Indications`, the motility cut-off written beside `Asthenopermia` [asthenospermia] is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): '• Asthenopermia : motility < 5%.'

questions.q: In the `Testicular azoospermia` pathway on scan 210, the hormone profile written at the start of the arrow is ____, ____ and ____.
options: Normal FSH; Normal LH; Normal Testosterone
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Testicular azoospermia : ↑FSH, ↑LH, Testosterone↓ → Testicular biopsy'.

questions.q: [Scenario] In `Testicular azoospermia` (`↑FSH, ↑LH, Testosterone↓`), why is `Testicular biopsy` performed, and what follows if `Sperm+`?
options: To identify presence of sperms in the testis; if sperm+, they are surgically extracted for ICSI
To diagnose Kallmann syndrome; if sperm+, start sildenafil alone
To measure seminal fructose in Leydig tissue; if positive, proceed to IUI
To recanalise the ejaculatory duct; if patent, use timed intercourse
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Testicular biopsy : To identify presence of sperms in testis → Sperm+ → Surgically extracted → ICSI'.

questions.q: Match testicular retrieval abbreviations under `Surgical methods to retrieve sperms`: 1) `TESA` 2) `TESE` — A) Testicular Sperm Extraction B) Testicular Sperm Aspiration.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'TESA : Testicular Sperm Aspiration. TESE : Testicular Sperm Extraction.'

questions.q: Match epididymal retrieval abbreviations under `Surgical methods to retrieve sperms`: 1) `PESA` 2) `MESA` — A) Microsurgical Epididymal Sperm Aspiration B) Percutaneous Epididymal Sperm Aspiration.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'PESA : Percutaneous Epididymal Sperm Aspiration. MESA : Microsurgical Epididymal Sperm Aspiration.'

questions.q: [Scenario] Using the `Mx OF SPECIFIC CAUSES OF MALE INFERTILITY` table on scan 210, a man has oligospermia of 12 million/mL. Which treatment row applies?
questions.why: Source (scan 210): row 1 under Oligospermia prints '10–15 million/mL → IUI' (note the slight variation from '10–16 million/mL' on scan 208).

questions.q: [Scenario] Using the same management table, sperm concentration is 7 million/mL. Which treatment is listed?
questions.why: Source (scan 210): row 2 under Oligospermia prints '5–10 million/mL → IVF'.

questions.q: [Scenario] Using the management table, sperm concentration is 3 million/mL. Which treatment is listed?
questions.why: Source (scan 210): row 3 under Oligospermia prints '< 5 million/mL → ICSI'.

questions.q: Match the exact `Oligospermia` concentration brackets in the scan 210 management table: 1) `10–15 million/mL` 2) `5–10 million/mL` 3) `<5 million/mL` — A) IVF B) ICSI C) IUI.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): directly tests all three exact numeric brackets in the Oligospermia sub-rows.

questions.q: In row 4 of the management table, `Non obstructive azoospermia` is treated with ____ followed by ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Non obstructive azoospermia → Surgical extraction of sperms → ICSI'.

questions.q: Match sexual-dysfunction rows in the management table: 1) `Erectile dysfunction` 2) `Premature ejaculation` — A) SSRI B) Sildenafil.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Erectile dysfunction → Sildenafil' and 'Premature ejaculation → SSRI'.

questions.q: [Scenario] In the management table, `Ejaculatory dysfunction (Hypospadias)` is managed with ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Ejaculatory dysfunction (Hypospadias) → IUI'.

questions.q: In the final row of the management table, `Retrograde ejaculation` is managed by ____ followed by ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Retrograde ejaculation → Sperms taken from urine → IUI'.

questions.q: Under `Note : Difference between dead sperm & live sperm`, test `1.` is `Supravital stain` using ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): '1. Supravital stain (Eosin/Trypan blue)'.

questions.q: Match `Supravital stain (Eosin/Trypan blue)` results: 1) `Stained` 2) `Not stained` — A) Live sperm B) Dead sperm.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Stained : Dead sperm' (disrupted plasma membrane admits dye) and 'Not stained : Live sperm'.

questions.q: Test `2.` for distinguishing dead from live immobile sperm is the ____ test.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): '2. Hypotonic osmotic sperm swelling test'.

questions.q: [Scenario] In the `Hypotonic osmotic sperm swelling test`, an immobile sperm `Swells`. What interpretation is printed?
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Swells : Live, immobile.' (Note: unlike supravital staining—which kills/fixes cells—HOS identifies live immobile sperm usable for ICSI.)

questions.q: In the `Hypotonic osmotic sperm swelling test`, `No swelling` indicates ____ sperm.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'No swelling : Dead.'

questions.q: To evaluate `Round cells on semen analysis`, the `Myeloperoxidase test` is also called the ____ test.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): 'Round cells on semen analysis : Myeloperoxidase test (Endtz test)'.

questions.q: Match `Myeloperoxidase test (Endtz test)` results as printed at the bottom of scan 210: 1) `+ve` 2) `-ve` — A) `Round sperm without an acrosomal cap` B) `WBC`.
questions.why: Source (scan 210): '+ve : WBC' and '-ve : Round sperm without an acrosomal cap.' Clarification: clinically, peroxidase-negative round cells in semen are typically immature germ cells (spermatids/spermatocytes) or round-headed/globozoospermic sperm lacking an acrosome; peroxidase negativity excludes granulocytic WBCs rather than proving a single cell subtype alone.

questions.q: In row 1 of the opening `Mechanism` table, combined `OCPs (E + P)` have main mechanism ____ with suppression of ____ much greater (`>>>`) than ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 211 / printed 203): row 1 prints '1. OCPs (E + P) → Main mechanism : Anovulation (↓ FSH >>> ↓ LH)'. (Clarification: clinically estrogen primarily suppresses FSH while progestin suppresses the LH surge.)

questions.q: Under `Other mechanism` in row 1 for combined `OCPs (E + P)`, the three bullets listed are ____, ____ and ____.
options: Endometrial decidualisation; fimbrial agglutination; FSH stimulation
Copper-induced leukocytosis; myometrial contraction; acrosome blockade
Thicker cervical mucus; thinning of endometrium; decreased tubal motility
Permanent cornual occlusion; luteolysis; spermicidal vaginal pH
questions.why: Source (scan 211): row 1 Other mechanism lists '• Thicker cervical mucus • Thinning of endometrium • ↓ Tubal motility'.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the `Other mechanism` bullets listed for combined OCPs on scan 211?
questions.why: Source (scan 211): combined OCP effects are reversible, not permanent tubal scarring.

questions.q: In row 2, traditional `POP (contains ____)` acts mainly to ____.
options: Ethinyl estradiol; stimulate the LH surge
questions.why: Source (scan 211): row 2 reads '2. POP (contains LNG) → Main mechanism : Make cervical mucus thick'.

questions.q: Match rows 3 and 4 of the `Mechanism` table with their `Main mechanism`: 1) `Progesterone implant / Injection / Cerazette (Contains Desogestrel)` 2) `Cu IUCD` — A) Prevents fertilisation (Cu induces inflammatory reaction) B) Anovulation.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): row 3 main mechanism is 'Anovulation'; row 4 main mechanism is 'Prevents fertilization (Cu : induces inflammatory reaction)'.

questions.q: In row 5, the table prints the `Main mechanism` of `MIRENA` as `Prevents ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): row 5 prints '5. MIRENA → Prevents implantation'. Clarification: clinically, 52-mg LNG-IUS acts predominantly BEFORE fertilisation by thickening cervical mucus and inhibiting sperm transport/survival in addition to endometrial suppression; it is not an abortifacient.

questions.q: In row 6, `Centchroman` (programme brand `____`) inhibits implantation by making the ____ out of phase.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): row 6 reads '6. Centchroman (Chaya) → Inhibit implantation by making endometrium out of phase'.

questions.q: In the `Other mechanism` column, `Inhibits implantation` is additionally written for row 3 (`____`) and row 4 (`____`).
questions.why: Source (scan 211): rows 3 and 4 both print 'Inhibits implantation' in the third column (secondary to their primary ovulation/fertilisation blockade).

questions.q: Under `CONTRACEPTIVES – GENERAL`, the three numbered items listed under `Long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARC)` are `1.` ____, `2.` ____ and `3.` ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'Long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARC) : 1. Injection : DMPA 2. Implants 3. IUCD'. Clarification: NICE includes DMPA in LARC, whereas ACOG/CDC often reserve LARC for IUDs and subdermal implants that do not require 3-monthly redosing.

questions.q: Which sits under `Permanent methods` rather than `Long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARC)` on scan 211?
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'Permanent methods : 1. Tubal ligation 2. Vasectomy'.

questions.q: Alongside `2. Vasectomy`, item `1.` under `Permanent methods` is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'Permanent methods : 1. Tubal ligation 2. Vasectomy'.

questions.q: `DMPA` stands for `Depot ____`, and is included in the national family planning programme (`NFP`) under the name ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'DMPA Injection (Depot Medroxy Progesterone Acetate) : Included in NFP : Antara'.

questions.q: In the DMPA box, `Dose` is ____ repeated every ____, and `Route` is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'Dose : 150 mg, repeated every 3 months. Route : Intramuscular.' (Subcutaneous DMPA-SC 104 mg also exists clinically, though not listed here.)

questions.q: Under DMPA `Missed dose`, for `<4 wks of due date` the injection can be given up to ____ before or ____ after the due date.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): '• <4 wks of due date : Can be given upto 2 wks before/4 wks after due date.'

questions.q: [Scenario] A patient presents `>4 wks after due date` for her repeat DMPA injection. What two-step management is listed in the box?
options: Rule out pregnancy (UPT), then give DMPA + backup × 7 days
Defer DMPA for 12–18 months until bone density normalises
Switch permanently to combined OCPs without pregnancy testing
Give double-dose DMPA immediately without UPT or any backup
questions.why: Source (scan 211): '• >4 wks after due date : 1. Rule out pregnancy (UPT). 2. Injection given + advise backup contraceptive × 7 days.'

questions.q: Inside the dedicated DMPA box, `Mechanism of action` is stated as ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'Mechanism of action : Anovulation.'

questions.q: Match the two non-contraceptive clinical `Advantages` listed in the DMPA box: 1) Epileptics 2) Sickle cell anaemia — A) `↓ sickling` B) `↓ seizure frequency`.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'Advantages : → ↓ seizure frequency in epileptics ; ↓ sickling in sickle cell anemia.'

questions.q: Under DMPA `Disadvantage`, delayed return of fertility (`____`) is paired with ____ and irregular bleeding.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'Disadvantage : • Delayed return of fertility (12–18 months) • ↓ bone mineral density • Irregular bleeding : m/c reason for discontinuation'. (Clinically, median fertility return is ~9–10 months after the last injection, and BMD loss is largely reversible after stopping.)

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three DMPA disadvantages listed on scan 211?
questions.why: Source (scan 211): DMPA delays ovulation return temporarily without destroying follicular reserve.

questions.q: In the DMPA box, the `m/c reason for discontinuation` is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): '• Irregular bleeding : m/c reason for discontinuation'.

questions.q: [Scenario] In the `Epilepsy & contraception` box, a woman with epilepsy is `Not on any antiepileptic`. Which contraceptive rule is stated?
options: Any contraceptive can be used (`OCPs also`)
Combined OCPs are strictly contraindicated by epilepsy itself
questions.why: Source (scan 211): '1. Not on any antiepileptic : Any contraceptive can be used (OCPs also)'.

questions.q: For `2. Patient on antiepileptic` in the scan 211 box, ____ contraceptive is used, and OCPs are marked `C/I` due to ____.
options: No hormonal or intrauterine; ovarian hyperstimulation
Combined high-dose estrogen; increased (`↑`) efficacy of OCPs
questions.why: Source (scan 211): '2. Patient on antiepileptic • Progesterone only contraceptive used • OCPs C/I (↓ efficacy of OCP's)'. (Qualified in the next question!)

questions.q: Source-check: the epilepsy box broadly states `Progesterone only contraceptive used` and `OCPs C/I (↓ efficacy of OCP's)` for patients on antiepileptics. What clinical qualification is required?
options: Every antiepileptic induces CYP3A4 identically, and every oral progestin pill is immune
Oral minipills and implants remain completely unaffected by phenytoin or carbamazepine
Enzyme-inducing AEDs reduce COCs, POPs and implants, whereas DMPA and IUDs stay effective
Antiepileptic drugs interact exclusively with copper IUDs and never with oral steroids
questions.why: Source (scan 211): separates the simplified note shorthand from drug- and formulation-specific MEC rules (hepatic enzyme inducers reduce COC, POP and implant efficacy; non-enzyme-inducing AEDs other than lamotrigine do not reduce COC efficacy).

questions.q: The closing `Note` in the epilepsy box warns that OCPs decrease the efficacy of ____, leading to an increased chance of seizures.
questions.why: Source (scan 211): 'Note : OCPs ↓ efficacy of lamotrigine (↑ chance of seizures)' (ethinyl estradiol induces lamotrigine glucuronidation).

questions.q: Match `Classification based on estrogen dose` (`Ethinyl estradiol`, `EE`) on scan 212: 1) High dose 2) Low dose 3) Very low dose — A) `EE < 20 mcg` B) `EE ≥ 50 mcg` C) `EE < 50 mcg (30 mcg)`.
questions.why: Source (scan 212 / printed 204): 'High dose : (Ethinyl estradial) EE ≥ 50 mcg; Low dose : EE < 50 mcg (30 mcg); Very low dose : EE < 20 mcg'.

questions.q: Source-check: under `Minimum possible dose : 10 mcg`, an arrow on scan 212 points to the printed text `α oesthin pill`. What does the scan show and what is the clinical clarification?
options: Minimum EE is `10 mcg`; `α oesthin pill` is a garbled print of *Lo Loestrin*
Minimum EE is `35 mcg`; `α oesthin pill` is India's national *Mala-N* regimen
Minimum EE is `10 mg`; `α oesthin pill` is a high-dose vaginal estriol tablet
Minimum EE is `50 mcg`; `α oesthin pill` is an alpha-adrenergic antihypertensive
questions.why: Source (scan 212): magnified crop confirms 'Minimum possible dose : 10 mcg → α oesthin pill' (typesetter misread handwritten 'Lo oestrin / Lo Loestrin' as 'α oesthin').

questions.q: Match progestin generations in `Classification based on progesterone`: 1) `1st generation` 2) `2nd generation` 3) `4th generation` — A) Drospirenone B) Norethindrone C) LNG (levonorgestrel).
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '1st generation : Norethindrone; 2nd generation : LNG; 4th generation : Drospirenone'.

questions.q: The three `3rd generation` progestins listed on scan 212 are ____, ____ and ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): under '3rd generation : Least androgenic side effects', the bullets are '• Desogestrel • Norgestimate • Gestodene'.

questions.q: Which progestin belongs to the `4th generation` rather than the `3rd generation` list on scan 212?
questions.why: Source (scan 212): drospirenone is 4th generation; desogestrel, norgestimate and gestodene are 3rd generation.

questions.q: On scan 212, `3rd generation` progestins are characterised as having the `Least ____ side effects`.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '3rd generation : Least androgenic side effects' (note clinically 3rd-generation COCs carry slightly higher VTE risk than 2nd-generation LNG).

questions.q: Under `4th generation : Drospirenone`, its two pharmacological properties are ____ and ____, with the latter linked on the page to `____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '4th generation : Drospirenone • Antiandrogenic • Antimineralocorticoid → weight loss • ↑ K+'. (Clarification: clinically, antimineralocorticoid natriuresis reduces fluid retention/bloating rather than causing true fat loss.)

questions.q: [Scenario] Because drospirenone has antimineralocorticoid (spironolactone-like) activity, which serum electrolyte change is listed as its third bullet on scan 212?
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• ↑ K+' under 4th generation : Drospirenone.

questions.q: Under `Absolute C/I of OCP's`, the printed `Mnemonic` sentence reads: `____ have various schemes to provide home loans during may.`
questions.why: Source (scan 212): reproduces the opening mnemonic line verbatim.

questions.q: [Scenario] A patient has a `H/o Breast cancer`. How is this placed in the `Absolute C/I of OCP's` box on scan 212?
options: Listed as the first absolute contraindication bullet
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• H/o Breast cancer.' (Under WHO/CDC MEC, current breast cancer is Category 4 and past breast cancer with no evidence of disease for 5 years is Category 3.)

questions.q: Under `Severe uncontrolled hypertension`, the arrows print `WHO` : ____ and `CDC` : ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): 'Severe uncontrolled hypertension → { WHO : ≥160/100 mmHg ; CDC : ≥140/90 mmHg }'. Clarification: both WHO and CDC US MEC actually classify systolic 140–159 or diastolic 90–99 mmHg as Category 3 (risks generally outweigh advantages) and ≥160/100 mmHg as Category 4 (unacceptable risk).

questions.q: The third contraindication bullet groups history of venous or arterial thrombosis with ____, ____, ____ and ____ positivity.
options: Haemorrhoids; Raynaud phenomenon; syncope; antisperm antibody
Superficial phlebitis; anaemia; asthma; rubella IgG
Varicose veins; mitral prolapse; sinus arrhythmia; Rh antibody
MI; CAD; stroke; lupus anticoagulant antibody
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• H/o Venous/Arterial thrombosis/MI/CAD/stroke/lupus anticoagulant antibody (+).'

questions.q: Which is NOT part of the thrombotic/cardiovascular contraindication bullet on scan 212?
questions.why: Source (scan 212): dysmenorrhoea is a non-contraceptive indication on scan 214, not a contraindication.

questions.q: Smoking is listed in the `Absolute C/I of OCP's` box for `Smokers` aged ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• Smokers ≥ 35yrs of age.' (Under MEC, ≥15 cigarettes/day at age ≥35 is Category 4 and <15/day at ≥35 is Category 3.)

questions.q: Match the three reproductive/cardiac states combined in bullet 5 of `Absolute C/I of OCP's`: 1) Current gestation 2) Cardiomyopathy history 3) Puerperal window — A) `<21 days postpartum` B) `Pregnant` C) `h/o peripartum cardiomyopathy`.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• Pregnant / h/o peripartum cardiomyopathy/< 21 days postpartum.'

questions.q: Bullet 6 of the OCP contraindication box lists the lipid disorder ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• Hypertrigliceridemia.' (Severe hypertriglyceridaemia increases pancreatitis/vascular risk with oral estrogen.)

questions.q: Bullet 7 of `Absolute C/I of OCP's` groups `Abnormal liver function`, `Hepatic adenoma`, `Liver cancer`, and ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• Abnormal liver function/Hepatic adenoma/Liver cancer / h/o cholestasis during pregnancy.' Clarification: in WHO/CDC MEC, pregnancy-related cholestasis is Category 2 whereas past COC-related cholestasis is Category 3, and severe cirrhosis/acute viral hepatitis/adenoma/hepatoma are Category 4.

questions.q: Which is NOT in the hepatic contraindication bullet on scan 212?
questions.why: Source (scan 212): functional ovarian cysts are in the reduced-risk/use boxes on scan 214, not hepatic contraindications.

questions.q: Bullet 8 lists `Diabetes with ____` as an OCP contraindication.
options: Family history in a second-degree relative
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• Diabetes with vasculopathy.' (Nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy or vascular disease = MEC 3/4.)

questions.q: [Scenario] Bullet 9 closes the `Absolute C/I of OCP's` box with which headache diagnosis?
options: Menstrual migraine without aura in a 24-year-old nonsmoker
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '• Migraine with aura' (MEC Category 4 due to ischaemic stroke risk; contrast 'Menstrual migraine' without aura listed under uses on scan 214).

questions.q: In the bottom `Note`, `1. m/c side effect of OCPs` is ____, noted to be `m/c with ____ pills d/t less 'E'`.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '1. m/c side effect of OCPs : Irregular/Breakthrough Bleeding (m/c with low dose pills d/t less 'E').'

questions.q: Item `2.` of the bottom `Note` states that before `Elective surgery with anticipated immobilization`, OCPs are stopped ____ prior.
questions.why: Source (scan 212): '2. Elective surgery with anticipated immobilization : OCPs stopped 4 wks prior.'

sections.name: OCP consumption, regimens and missed-pill source algorithm

units.title: OCP consumption, regimens and missed-pill source algorithm

questions.q: Under `Method of consumption`, OCPs ____ (`Can be started at any time`), while the `Ideal` start window without backup is ____ of the cycle.
options: Can be started at any time; D1–D5
questions.why: Source (scan 213 / printed 205): 'Method of consumption : • Can be started at any time. • Ideal : D1 – D5 of cycle.' (Clinically, 'quick start' outside D1–D5 requires reasonable certainty the woman is not pregnant.)

questions.q: When OCPs are started `>D5` of the cycle, a `Backup method` is advised for ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): '• >D5 : Backup method × 7 days.' (Contrast 48 hours for POPs on scan 217.)

questions.q: Routine OCP dosing is `1 pill ____, at ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): '• 1 pill everyday, at same time.'

questions.q: In the `28 Tab pack` example on scan 213, the pack contains ____ hormonal tablets + ____ tablets.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): '28 Tab pack : • 21 Hormonal tablets. + 7 Ferrous fumarate tablets.' (Corresponds to standard Government of India Mala-N/Mala-D 21+7 packs.)

questions.q: [Scenario] Under `28 Tab pack`, the second bullet writes `Menstruation (+) : Fresh pack started`. How is a 21+7 pack taken continuously in practice?
options: Continue taking extra iron tablets daily until a mid-cycle LH surge appears
Finish the 7 iron tablets and start the next pack immediately with no gap
Wait until withdrawal bleeding stops for 7 full days before opening a pack
Discard remaining iron pills on day 1 of bleeding and wait 7 pill-free days
questions.why: Source (scan 213): clarifies 'Menstruation (+) : Fresh pack started'—withdrawal bleeding occurs during the 7 iron-tablet days, and the next pack starts right on schedule without extending the hormone-free interval.

questions.q: Under `21 Tab pack`, the dosing pattern is `1 pill daily × ____ & ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): '21 Tab pack : • 1 pill daily × 3 weeks & 1 week off'.

questions.q: Source-check: the second bullet under `21 Tab pack` writes `1 day of menstruation : Fresh pack started`. What safety clarification prevents contraception failure?
options: Never extend the break past 7 days waiting for menses; restart right after 7 days
Always wait until bleeding starts, even if that requires 3 weeks off active pills
Any withdrawal bleeding during the 7-day pill-free interval proves method failure
Open a brand-new 21-tablet hormonal pack on every single day of withdrawal bleeding
questions.why: Source (scan 213): flags the ambiguous bullet ('1 day of menstruation : Fresh pack started', conflating first-ever Day-1 start with repeat-pack transition) so the 7-day maximum hormone-free interval is never exceeded.

questions.q: Match `Regimens` in the top-right box on scan 213: 1) `21/7` 2) `24/4` — A) 24 days hormonal pills + 4 days off B) 21 days pills + 7 days off.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): 'Regimens : 21/7 : 21 days pills + 7 days off. 24/4 : 24 days hormonal pills + 4 days off.'

questions.q: The two `Advantages` listed under the `24/4` regimen are ____ efficacy and ____ side effects.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): '24/4 ... • Advantages → { Better efficacy. ; Lesser side effects. }' (shorter hormone-free interval reduces follicular escape and hormone-withdrawal symptoms).

questions.q: `Multiphasic pills` are defined as `Pills with ____ in the same pack` and are parenthetically labelled `(____)`.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): 'Multiphasic pills : Pills with different doses in the same pack (obsolete).' Clarification: multiphasic COC brands remain commercially marketed in some regions, though monophasic regimens are simpler and preferred.

questions.q: In the middle-right box, `Return of menses` notes `____ +/–` due to thinning of the endometrium by ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): 'Return of menses : Post pill amenorrhea +/– → D/t thinning of endometrium by progesterone.'

questions.q: Directly below post-pill amenorrhoea, `Return of fertility` after OCPs is described as `Rapid, ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): 'Return of fertility : Rapid, ≤ 3 months' (contrasting with 12–18 months in the DMPA box on scan 211).

questions.q: [Scenario] Under `Government of India guideline for missed pills`, what two bullets appear under `Missed 1 or 2 pills`?
options: Discard the current pill pack immediately; use barrier backup for 4 weeks
Skip the missed tablets completely; omit active hormonal pills for 7 days
Swallow 4 hormonal pills immediately; insert copper IUCD within 24 hours
Take 1 pill ASAP or 2 pills at scheduled time; no backup method required
questions.why: Source (scan 213): 'Government of India guideline for missed pills : Missed 1 or 2 pills : • One pill to be taken ASAP or 2 pills at scheduled time. • Backup contraceptive method not required.'

questions.q: Source-check: immediately below `Missed 1 or 2 pills` (no backup), the next heading reads `Missed ≥ 2 pills` (backup × 7 days). What internal inconsistency must be flagged?
options: Exact `2 missed pills` appears in both headings with opposite backup instructions
Both headings apply exclusively to 3-year subdermal etonogestrel rods, not OCPs
Missing 2 active pills mandates discontinuing all contraception for 3 full months
Both headings give identical 7-day barrier-backup advice for 1 or 2 missed pills
questions.why: Source (scan 213): explicitly flags the boundary overlap at '2 pills' between 'Missed 1 or 2 pills' and 'Missed ≥ 2 pills' (clinically, WHO/GOI rules require 7-day backup after ≥3 missed 30–35 mcg EE pills or ≥2 missed ≤20 mcg EE pills).

questions.q: Under the `Missed ≥ 2 pills` heading on scan 213, a `Backup method` is advised for ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): 'Missed ≥ 2 pills : • Backup method × 7 days.'

questions.q: Under `Missed ≥ 2 pills`, an `Emergency contraceptive pill` is advised if unprotected intercourse occurred in the previous ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): '• Unprotected intercourse in previous 72 hrs : Emergency contraceptive pill.' (Clinically, ulipristal/Cu-IUD EC windows extend up to 120 hours.)

questions.q: [Scenario] In the `1st/2nd week` sub-branch under `Missed ≥ 2 pills`, what three actions are listed?
options: Discard the entire pill pack immediately and wait for next spontaneous menses
Take 1 pill immediately + finish pack, backup × 7 days, and ECP if sex ≤72 h
Swallow 3 hormonal pills daily for 7 days without barrier backup or any ECP
Omit remaining hormonal tablets, start iron tablets early, and avoid backup
questions.why: Source (scan 213): reproduces all three bullets under '1st/2nd week'.

questions.q: [Scenario] In the `3rd week` sub-branch under `Missed ≥ 2 pills`, how does pack management differ from weeks 1–2?

Take 1 pill now + finish active pack + start new pack (`non-hormonal pills omitted`)
Observe a 14-day hormone-free interval before opening the next active pill pack
Discontinue combined OCPs until a day-26 endometrial biopsy confirms ovulation

questions.q: Evaluate the `Government of India guideline for missed pills` box on scan 213: I) Management of `Missed ≥ 2 pills` separates `1st/2nd week` from `3rd week`. II) In the `3rd week`, the 7 non-hormonal pills are taken before starting a new pack.
questions.why: Source (scan 213): in week 3, non-hormonal pills are explicitly omitted so the new active pack starts immediately.

questions.why: Source (scan 216): 'H/o Thrombosis : CuIUCD/Mirena' (Cu-IUD is MEC 1 and LNG-IUS is MEC 2 in past VTE).

questions.why: Source (scan 216): 'PID : • 1st three weeks : ↑ risk of PID' (related to insertion instrumentation).

questions.why: Source (scan 216): '• m/c PID : Actinomyces'. Clarification: microbiologically, polymicrobial STI/endogenous flora (Chlamydia, Gonorrhoea, anaerobes) cause most PID overall, whereas *Actinomyces israelii* is the classic organism uniquely associated with prolonged IUCD use.

questions.q: [Scenario] In the scan 216 flowchart, clinically symptomatic `Actinomyces` PID in an IUCD user is `managed by` ____.

Leaving the IUCD permanently without antibiotics
questions.why: Source (scan 216): 'm/c PID : Actinomyces → managed by → IUCD removal + antibiotics'. Clarification: if *Actinomyces*-like organisms are found incidentally on a Pap smear in a completely asymptomatic woman without pelvic infection, guidelines advise leaving the IUCD in situ without antibiotics.

questions.q: [Scenario] An IUCD user with `Other PID` is `not responding` after 48–72 hours of oral antibiotics. What escalation is written on scan 216?
options: Remove IUCD immediately before giving any antibiotic
Switch to IV antibiotics + IUCD removal after 24 hours
Continue unchanged oral antibiotics for 6 weeks
questions.why: Source (scan 216): 'Oral antibiotics × 48 – 72 hrs → not responding → switch to iv + IUCD removal after 24 hrs' (establishing IV antibiotic cover prior to removal).

Implanon stops releasing etonogestrel after month 1 and acts purely as an inert foreign body

questions.why: Source (scan 218): '• Married women only. • At least 1 child, ≥ 1yr of age.' (Indian MoHFW administrative programme criteria unless medically indicated; autonomous informed consent and local law govern care.)

questions.q: [Scenario] Under `Pre-requisite` on scan 218, whose consent is explicitly required for female tubal ligation?

Written consent of the husband in place of hers

questions.q: Immediately below `Consent of female`, the second `Pre-requisite` bullet specifies a `____ individual`.

Capacity review and statutory safeguards apply; disability never permits coercion
Any psychiatric diagnosis automatically removes all reproductive bodily autonomy
A family guardian can legally override any competent adult's informed refusal

questions.q: The fourth `Pre-requisite` bullet states: `Husband : No h/o ____ (Except in case of ____)`.
questions.why: Source (scan 218): '• Husband : No h/o vasectomy (Except in case of failure).' (Indian public-programme double-sterilisation check.)

questions.q: Match `Eligibility criteria to perform tubal ligation` on scan 218: 1) Specialist OBG qualification (`1.`) 2) `2. MBBS` / `3. MS` training requirement — A) `Assisted in 5 & performed 5 as a primary surgeon` B) `MD/DNB/DGO in OBG`.

questions.q: Items `3.`–`6.` of `Preliminary investigations before tubal ligation` are ____, ____, ____, and `UPT : ____`.

Serum AMH; karyotype; day-21 progesterone; never
Lipid panel; HbA1c; thyroid profile; mandatory twice
Blood group; haemoglobin; urine routine/microscopy; if required

No condition bans ligation permanently, though Category `D`/`S` states require deferral or care
Confirmed intrauterine pregnancy never requires postponing elective tubal sterilisation
Critically ill patients with acute myocardial infarction or sepsis undergo immediate surgery

questions.q: Item `4.` delays postpartum sterilisation during `Post partum period : ____ days` (`____`).
questions.why: Source (scan 218): '4. Post partum period : 8–41 days (1–6 wks).'

questions.q: Which is NOT among the obstetric/infectious `Indications for delayed procedure` on scan 218?

questions.q: [Scenario] Item `6.` (`Current PID`) is diagnosed at a woman's planned interval tubal-ligation visit. What action matches the scan 218 classification?
options: Ignore PID if haemoglobin exceeds 7 g/dL
Proceed immediately because ligation cures acute PID
Delay the procedure until pelvic infection is treated and resolved
Impose a permanent lifetime ban even after cure
questions.why: Source (scan 218): '6. Current PID' is in 'Indications for delayed procedure' (risk of pelvic abscess/adhesions if operated acutely).

questions.q: Item `7.` delays postpartum tubal ligation for `H/o premature rupture of membrane > ____` or `h/o ____`.

questions.q: Item `10.` of `Indications for delayed procedure` lists `Cancer : Endometrium / Cervix / ____`.

questions.q: [Scenario] The bottom-left box `Tubal ligation safe in :` begins with `• BP ≥ 160/100`. What clinical qualification is required?
options: Preoperative blood-pressure measurement is omitted before elective tubal sterilisation
Severe uncontrolled hypertension is best treated with 50-mcg combined oral pills
Blood pressure of 180/110 mmHg carries zero anaesthetic risk and needs no monitoring
Unlike estrogen OCPs it is not banned, but BP ≥160/100 needs control and Category `S` care
questions.why: Source (scan 218): reconciles 'Tubal ligation safe in : • BP ≥ 160/100' with safe perioperative care (WHO MEC places BP ≥160/100 in Category S = Special arrangements).

HIV-positive patients; diabetics; breast cancer; smokers
Current MI; acute DVT; pulmonary embolism; APH/PPH
questions.why: Source (scan 218): 'Tubal ligation safe in : • BP ≥ 160/100. • HIV positive patients. • Diabetics. • Breast cancer. • Smokers.'

questions.why: Source (scan 218): directly links the 8–41 day deferral window with the ≥6-week interval start.

units.title: Emergency contraception: mechanisms, timing and regimens

questions.q: At the top of scan 220, `Emergency contraceptives` are given the synonym `AKA ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220 / printed 212): 'Emergency contraceptives / AKA Interceptives.'

questions.q: The three bullets under `Indications :` on scan 220 are ____, ____ and ____.
options: Confirmed intrauterine pregnancy; planned conception; HSG
After unprotected intercourse; rape victim; condom rupture
Postmenopausal HRT; luteal support; Asherman syndrome
Heavy menstrual bleeding; hirsutism; Turner syndrome
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Indications : • After unprotected intercourse. • Rape victim. • Condom rupture.'

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the `Indications :` for emergency contraception on scan 220?
questions.why: Source (scan 220): EC prevents pregnancy prior to implantation and cannot terminate an established pregnancy.

questions.q: Under `Timing :` on scan 220, emergency contraception is `Ideal : Within ____` and `Can be given : upto ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Timing : • Ideal : Within 72 hrs. • Can be given : upto 120 hrs.'

questions.q: Directly below `Timing` on scan 220, the quoted `Failure rate` is `____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Failure rate : 1.1%' (approximate oral LNG EC failure figure; Cu-IUCD is <0.1% and ulipristal ~0.9–1.4%).

questions.q: [Scenario] Beside `Failure rate : 1.1%`, an arrow reads `In accidental pregnancy : No risk of • Teratogenicity • Ectopic pregnancy`. How should this be applied clinically if pregnancy occurs despite EC?
options: Reassure against teratogenic or added ectopic risk, while still confirming intrauterine site
Omit early pelvic ultrasound because ectopic gestation is biologically impossible
Administer empirical systemic methotrexate before checking beta-hCG or ultrasound
Recommend immediate medical termination because oral LNG causes major limb defects
questions.why: Source (scan 220): captures both bullets ('No risk of • Teratogenicity • Ectopic pregnancy') with safe clinical follow-up context.

questions.q: The `m/c used` emergency pill on scan 220 is `____ (i-pill)`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Levonorgestrel (i-pill) : • m/c used.'

questions.q: Under `Levonorgestrel (i-pill)`, scan 220 writes `Only used upto ____` hours.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '• Only used upto 72 hrs.' (Clarification: efficacy is highest ≤72 h; if ulipristal/Cu-IUD are unavailable between 72 and 120 h, some guidelines still permit LNG with counselled lower efficacy.)

questions.q: Order the primary `Levonorgestrel (i-pill)` mechanism arrow (`1.`) on scan 220: A) `Delays ovulation` B) `Delays LH surge`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '1. Delays LH surge → Delays ovulation.'

questions.q: Alongside `1. Delays LH surge → Delays ovulation`, item `2.` under `Levonorgestrel (i-pill) → Mechanism of action` states `Delays ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '2. Delays fertilization.'

questions.q: Evaluate `Note : LNG` on scan 220: I) LNG has `No effect on implantation`. II) LNG acts as an `abortifacient`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Note : LNG → { No effect on implantation. ; Not an abortifacient. }'

questions.q: On scan 220, `Most effective : ____` is contrasted with `Hormonal : ____` (most effective oral/hormonal EC).
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Most effective : Cu-IUCD ... Hormonal : Ulipristal'.

questions.q: The two bullets directly under `Most effective : Cu-IUCD` state that it `Acts ____` and `Prevents ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Most effective : Cu-IUCD • Acts immediately • Prevents implantation.' (Clarification: copper ions also exert a potent pre-fertilisation gamete-toxic effect in addition to preventing implantation.)

questions.q: Source-check: on scan 220, a right-hand bracket spanning `Cu-IUCD` and `Hormonal : Ulipristal` points to `• Prescription : Not required • Can be used multiple times • No teratogenicity`. What clarification is needed?
options: Those points describe oral ECPs (OTC LNG); Cu-IUCD needs clinician insertion and Rx rules vary
Patients routinely self-insert copper T 380A devices over the counter several times monthly
Repeated postcoital ECP dosing in every cycle is more effective than subdermal implants
Single-dose ulipristal acetate causes severe congenital heart defects in accidental pregnancy
questions.why: Source (scan 220): explicitly audits the mis-attached bracket while recording all three printed bullets (Cu-IUCD requires trained provider insertion, and ulipristal requires a prescription in many countries).

questions.q: Scan 220 states: `Patient vomits ≤ ____ of taking pill : Repeat course`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Patient vomits ≤ 1 hr of taking pill : Repeat course.' (WHO/CDC/FSRH product guidance generally repeats oral EC if vomiting occurs within 2–3 hours.)

questions.q: Under `Drugs used : 1. Levonorgestrel (LNG) – Plan B method`, the single-dose regimen is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '• Dose : 1.5 mg single dose or 0.75 mg → 12hrs later → 0.75 mg.'

questions.q: In the split-dose `Plan B` regimen on scan 220, `____` is followed `____ later` by `0.75 mg`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'or 0.75 mg → 12hrs later → 0.75 mg.'

questions.q: Both the right-hand EC bracket and `1. Levonorgestrel (LNG) – Plan B method` state that ____ is required, and oral EC can be used ____.
options: Inpatient admission; once in a lifetime
Baseline HSG; daily as routine contraception
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '• No prescription required' and '• Can be used multiple times' (though ongoing regular contraception is far more effective than repeated ECP use).

questions.q: Item `2.` under `Drugs used` names the combined-OCP emergency regimen: `OCPs – ____ method`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '2. OCPs – Yuzpe method'.

questions.q: Source-check: the `Yuzpe method` bullet writes `100 mcg EE + 0.5mg Progesterone`. What hormonal clarification is needed?
options: Standard Yuzpe uses `100 mcg EE + 0.5 mg levonorgestrel`, not natural progesterone
Standard Yuzpe dosing is injected intramuscularly rather than taken as oral pills
Oral ethinyl estradiol alone without any progestin constitutes the Yuzpe regimen
Any 0.5-mg micronised natural progesterone capsule provides identical EC efficacy
questions.why: Source (scan 220): separates the shorthand '0.5mg Progesterone' from standard EE + levonorgestrel (or 1.0 mg dl-norgestrel) Yuzpe composition.

questions.q: In `2. OCPs – Yuzpe method`, the `Repeat dose` interval printed across all three arrows is ____ later.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '12hrs later → Repeat dose'.

questions.q: Source-check: under Yuzpe `↓ Dosing`, scan 220 prints `High dose : 4 pills → 12hrs later → 4 pills` and `Low dose : 2 pills → 12hrs later → 2 pills`. Why must this be flagged?
options: Counts are inverted: 100 mcg EE needs `2 + 2` high-dose (50-mcg) vs `4 + 4` low-dose pills
Low-dose pills contain double the ethinyl estradiol of high-dose 50-mcg tablets
Standard Yuzpe dosing omits the 12-hour repeat dose when low-dose pills are used
Four high-dose 50-mcg ethinyl estradiol tablets contain only 25 mcg EE in total
questions.why: Source (scan 220): flags the reversed 4+4 vs 2+2 tablet numbers so reversed dosing is never applied clinically.

questions.q: Under `3. Ulipristal acetate`, the emergency `Dose` is `____, OD` (single oral dose).
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '3. Ulipristal acetate : • Dose : 30 mg, OD.'

questions.q: Compared with `LNG`, `3. Ulipristal acetate` is stated to be `____ effective`.
questions.why: Source (scan 220): '• More effective than LNG.'

questions.q: The three sub-bullets (`i`, `ii`, `iii`) under `3. Ulipristal acetate → Indications` on scan 220 are ____, ____ and ____.
options: Day 1 of menses; <12 hrs only; underweight adolescents
Confirmed pregnancy; missing IUD thread; septic abortion
Near mid-cycle; ≥72 hrs after unprotected intercourse; obese patients
Within 10 mins of placenta; lactation day 1; Wilson's disease
questions.why: Source (scan 220): 'Indications : i. Near mid-cycle. ii. ≥72 hrs after unprotected intercourse. iii. Obese patients.'

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three settings (`i`–`iii`) listed under `Ulipristal acetate → Indications` on scan 220?
questions.why: Source (scan 220): ulipristal is an emergency contraceptive (up to 120 h), not an abortifacient for established pregnancy (and Cu-IUD remains unaffected by high BMI when acceptable).
