options: Combined patch; vaginal ring; danazol; mifepristone
Combined OCPs; laparoscopic ligation; diaphragm; sponge
Ethinyl estradiol; Yuzpe pills; Essure; Filshie clip
questions.why: Source (scan 221): 'Day-1 after delivery : • Condoms • Centchroman • POPs • Progesterone implants'.

questions.q: Which is NOT among the four methods in `Day-1 after delivery :` on scan 221?
questions.why: Source (scan 221): combined OCPs are deferred postpartum (see 'Other contraceptives : 1. OCPs' below).

questions.q: The non-barrier, non-steroidal Indian family-planning pill included in `Day-1 after delivery :` on scan 221 is ____.
questions.why: Source (scan 221): '• Centchroman' (Chaya/Saheli).

questions.q: Under `Other contraceptives : 1. OCPs`, the two adverse bullets state `↓ ____ in breastfeeding females` and `↑ Risk of ____ in breastfeeding & non-breastfeeding females`.
questions.why: Source (scan 221): '1. OCPs : • ↓Breast milk in breastfeeding females. • ↑Risk of thrombosis in breastfeeding & non-breastfeeding females.'

questions.q: Under `1. OCPs → Nonbreastfeeding`, combined pills `Can start : ____` and `Ideally : ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 221): 'Nonbreastfeeding : • Can start : ≥ 3 weeks. • Ideally : ≥ 6 weeks.' (WHO/CDC MEC: <21 days = Category 4; 21–42 days = Category 2 without other VTE risk factors or Category 3 with VTE risk factors; >42 days = Category 1.)

questions.q: Under `1. OCPs → Exclusively breastfeeding`, combined pills `Can start : ____` and `Ideally : ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 221): 'Exclusively breastfeeding : • Can start : ≥ 6 weeks • Ideally : ≥ 6 months.' (WHO MEC: <6 weeks = Category 4; 6 weeks to <6 months = Category 3; ≥6 months = Category 2.)

questions.q: Source-check: at bottom-left of scan 221, `2. DMPA` literally prints `Leads to osteoporosis if given ≥ 4wks`. What must a learner conclude?
options: Single-dose DMPA given at 4 weeks postpartum causes acute irreversible vertebral fractures
Postpartum DMPA is permitted only during weeks 1–3 and permanently banned after week 4
Depot medroxyprogesterone has zero effect on bone mineral density at any duration of use
Garbled rule: WHO MEC delays DMPA to ≥6 wks in lactation; BMD loss is chronic and reversible
questions.why: Source (scan 221): magnified crop confirms the literal print '2. DMPA : Leads to osteoporosis if given ≥ 4wks.' and clearly separates it from WHO/GOI postpartum MEC rules (<6 weeks breastfeeding = MEC 3 for neonatal steroid exposure).

questions.q: Match `3. IUCD` postpartum insertion windows on scan 221: 1) `Postplacental` 2) `Postpartum` 3) `Interval` — A) `After 6 weeks` B) `Within 10 mins of delivery` C) `Till 48 hours of delivery`.
questions.why: Source (scan 221): '3. IUCD : • Postplacental : Within 10 mins of delivery. • Postpartum : Till 48 hours of delivery. • Interval : After 6 weeks.'

questions.q: [Scenario] A woman requests PPIUCD insertion 24 hours after vaginal delivery (and has no chorioamnionitis/PPH). Which `3. IUCD` window on scan 221 applies, and when would insertion be deferred?
options: Delayed `Interval : After 6 weeks` window; insertion at 24 hours is prohibited
Permitted continuously from 10 minutes through day 28 without any deferral gap
Early `Postpartum : Till 48 hours` window; after 48 hours defer to `After 6 weeks`
Immediate `Postplacental : Within 10 mins` window; after 10 mins defer to 6 months
questions.why: Source (scan 221): applies both the 'Till 48 hours' early postpartum window and the 48-hour to 6-week deferral gap.

questions.q: Item `4.` in the bottom box on scan 221 states: `Emergency contraception : After ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 221): '4. Emergency contraception : After 4 weeks.' (Ovulation rarely occurs before day 25–28 postpartum; clinically LAM criteria can extend natural protection in exclusive breastfeeding.)

questions.q: [Scenario] Under `5. Tubectomy` on scan 221, which surgical route is marked `C/I in postpartum period`?
questions.why: Source (scan 221): '• Laparoscopic tubal ligation : C/I in postpartum period.'

questions.q: Under `5. Tubectomy`, postpartum `Minilaparotomy` names the `(____ technique)`.
questions.why: Source (scan 221): '• Minilaparotomy (modified Pomeroy technique)'.

questions.q: The two timing sub-bullets under `Minilaparotomy (modified Pomeroy technique)` on scan 221 are `Postpartum : ____` and `Interval : ____`.
questions.why: Source (scan 221): '- Postpartum : Till 1 week. - Interval : After 6 weeks.'

questions.q: Evaluate `Post-partum contraception` on scan 221: I) The `Rule of 3` (`3 weeks` / `3 months`) means no contraceptive method can ever be initiated on `Day-1 after delivery`. II) Scan 221 explicitly lists `Condoms`, `Centchroman`, `POPs` and `Progesterone implants` in `Day-1 after delivery` (plus `Postplacental` IUCD within 10 mins).
questions.why: Source (scan 221): reconciles the ovulation-based 'Rule of 3' box with immediate Day-1 and postplacental options on the same page.

questions.q: In the Contraception: Images condom table, the male condom has ____ ring and the female condom has ____.
questions.why: The Ring row contrasts one rolled rim on the male condom with the two rings sketched on the female condom.

questions.q: The Appearance row gives the male condom ____.
options: a short, broad shape with no pointed end
a dome with a flexible rim

questions.q: The female condom is described in the Appearance row as ____.
options: short, broad and with no pointed end
questions.why: Short/broad/no-pointed-end is printed opposite the male condom's pointed end.

questions.q: Which is NOT a printed difference between the male and female condom columns?
questions.why: The tablet count belongs to the Mala N/D pill packet on the next sheet, not to the condom comparison.

questions.q: Male condoms are ____ because they are used on an erect penis.
questions.why: Coitus dependent / used on erect penis is the male entry; the female condom is coitus independent.

questions.q: The female condom is labelled ____ in the Coitus row.
questions.why: The table contrasts coitus-independent female condoms with coitus-dependent male condoms.

questions.q: The Failure rate row prints ____ per HWY for male condoms.
questions.why: 2-15/HWY is the male figure; 5-20/HWY is the female figure in the neighbouring cell.

questions.q: The Failure rate row prints ____ per HWY for female condoms.
questions.why: The female-condom cell reads 5-20/HWY, higher than the male 2-15/HWY.

questions.why: HWY = Hundred women years, the exposure denominator for the Pearl-style failure rates.

questions.q: Under Programme, the male condom is included in the National Family Planning Programme as ____.
questions.why: Nirodh is the free male-condom brand named in the programme row; Mala D is an oral pill on the next sheet.

questions.q: Female condoms are described as distributed ____ to female sex workers.

questions.q: The usage row calls the male condom ____ use.
questions.why: Single use sits beside the female-condom annotation that it can be used twice.

questions.q: Source-check: the table says a female condom 'can be used twice'. What is the safest reading?
options: A female condom is designed for 30 hours of repeated intercourse
Washing and reusing female condoms is standard WHO advice
It is an edition-specific annotation; current guidance treats condoms as single-use, so re-use must not be taught as practice

questions.q: The Advantage line ranks HIV protection as male condom ____ female condom.
questions.why: It reads protects against HIV (male condom > Female condom), then lists PID, STD, cervical dysplasia and pregnancy.

questions.q: Which is NOT among the conditions the condom Advantage line says condoms protect against?
questions.why: HIV, PID, STD, cervical dysplasia and pregnancy are listed; bone loss is not.

questions.q: I) Male condoms are termed coitus dependent. II) Female condoms are termed coitus independent.
questions.why: The Coitus row assigns dependence to the male condom and independence to the female condom.

questions.q: Match the Ring row: 1) Male condom 2) Female condom with A) Two rings B) A single ring.
questions.why: The figure shows one rolled ring on the male condom and two rings on the female condom.

questions.q: Source-check: the male-condom 'made of' cell reads 'Polyurethane condom'. What caution applies?
options: The material row refers only to the female condom
It is the source wording; most male condoms are latex and the actual product material must be checked
All male condoms are polyurethane by regulation
questions.why: The printed material is study text, not a universal product description or a rule about STI protection.

questions.q: A programme worker needs the free-of-cost condom supplied to female sex workers. Which source row is being described?
options: Male condoms as Nirodh under the National Family Planning Programme
Implanon, not free of cost by GoI
questions.why: NACO / free of cost / female sex workers is the female-condom programme cell.

questions.q: The Today Sponge is described as a ____ shaped device.
questions.why: Mushroom shaped is the sponge; dome shaped with a flexible rim is the diaphragm below it.

questions.q: The Today Sponge contains ____ of nonoxynol-9, a spermicide.
questions.why: 1 g of nonoxynol-9 is the sponge dose; the other figures are Mala N, Mirena and Implanon hormone amounts from this chapter.

questions.q: After insertion the Today Sponge is used multiple times for ____.
questions.why: 24 hrs is the multiple-use window; 30 hrs is the separate maximum permitted duration.

questions.q: The maximum permitted duration printed for the Today Sponge is ____.
questions.why: 30 hrs is the maximum permitted duration, printed below the 24-hour multiple-use line.

questions.q: Source-check: the sponge bullet reads 'Chances of toxic shock syndrome: Nil'. What should a learner conclude?
options: The sponge eliminates all menstrual toxic-shock risk
Toxic shock syndrome is caused only by nonoxynol-9
It is an overconfident source claim; barrier/device use can carry toxic-shock risk and current product guidance governs
Nil means a 30-hour insertion is always safe
questions.why: 'Nil' is printed as an absolute; it should be read as source shorthand rather than a clinical guarantee.

questions.q: The Diaphragm is a ____ shaped device with a flexible rim.
questions.why: Dome shaped with flexible rim is the diaphragm description.

questions.q: The diaphragm is washed and reused for up to ____.
questions.why: Upto 1 year of reuse is printed for the diaphragm; the 24/30-hour figures belong to the sponge.

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as a diaphragm material?
questions.why: Made of rubber/latex/silicone is the diaphragm; nylon thread is the multiload-375 and Gynefix component.

questions.q: The diaphragm is described as not ____.
questions.why: 'Not sperm-proof' is why a spermicidal agent is added.

questions.q: Because it is not sperm-proof, a ____ is added to the diaphragm.
questions.why: Spermicidal agent is added; the other options are IUCD and implant components elsewhere in the chapter.

questions.q: I) The Today Sponge is a single-use device. II) The diaphragm can be reused for up to one year.
questions.why: The sponge is used multiple times over 24 hours, while the diaphragm is washed and reused up to a year.

questions.q: A learner confuses the sponge's 24-hour and 30-hour numbers. Which mapping is correct in the source?
options: 30 hours of repeated use; 24 hours maximum duration
24 hours of repeated use; 30 hours maximum permitted duration
questions.why: The two lines are separate: a 24-hour multiple-use window and a 30-hour maximum permitted duration.

questions.q: Match the barrier device to its shape: 1) Today Sponge 2) Diaphragm with A) Mushroom B) Dome with flexible rim.
questions.why: Mushroom shaped is the sponge; dome shaped with a flexible rim is the diaphragm.

sections.name: Mala N/D, IUCD generations and Copper T 380A

units.title: Mala N/D, IUCD generations and Copper T 380A

questions.q: Mala N and Mala D contain ethinylestradiol ____ plus levonorgestrel ____.
questions.why: Composition = Ethinylestradiol 30 mcg + Levonorgestrel (LNG) 150 mcg.

questions.q: A Mala packet contains ____ hormonal pills and ____ ferrous fumarate tablets.
questions.why: 21 hormonal pills + 7 ferrous fumarate tablets is the printed 28-day packet.

questions.q: Mala N is distributed by the Government of India ____.
questions.why: Mala N is free of cost; Mala D is the subsidised version.

questions.q: Mala D is distributed ____.
questions.why: The two lines separate free Mala N from subsidised Mala D.

questions.q: Match the brand to distribution: 1) Mala N 2) Mala D with A) Free of cost B) Subsidised rates.
questions.why: Mala N is the free government supply; Mala D is sold at subsidised rates.

questions.q: The source lists the ____ loop as the first-generation IUCD.
questions.why: 1st gen = Lippes loop; 2nd gen = Copper IUCD.

questions.q: The third-generation IUCD named in the list is ____.
questions.why: 3rd gen = Hormonal IUCD (mirena); 4th gen = Frameless IUCD.

questions.q: The fourth-generation IUCD in the list is ____.
questions.why: 4th gen = Frameless IUCD, later named Gynefix on the next sheet.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four IUCD generations listed?
questions.why: Essure is a hysteroscopic tubal-occlusion coil, not an intrauterine device generation.

questions.q: Copper T 380A, also called ____, is a T-shaped device.
questions.why: Copper T 380 A (Paraguard) is the printed name.

questions.q: In 'Copper T 380A', 380 mm2 refers to the ____.
options: surface area of the copper wire
questions.why: 380 mm2 = surface area of copper wire; A = copper on the arms of the T.

questions.q: The 'A' in Copper T 380A denotes copper present on the ____.
questions.why: A = copper present on the arms of the T tube.

questions.q: Copper T 380A releases about ____ of copper per day in the source.
questions.why: 50 mcg/day is the source figure; 20 mcg/day is Mirena's LNG release.

questions.q: The lifespan printed for Copper T 380A is ____.

questions.q: The rounded end of the Copper T is annotated to prevent ____.
questions.why: A diagram arrow labels the tip as preventing perforation, a device-safety annotation rather than a contraceptive mechanism.

questions.q: A student reads '380' as a hormone dose and 'A' as a drug name. Which correction fits the source?
options: 380 is days of use and A is a sterilisation route
380 is 380 mg of LNG and A is the manufacturer
380 is the thread length and A is the applicator
380 is copper-wire surface area in mm2 and A marks copper on the arms
questions.why: The numeric and letter describe copper geometry, not a hormonal dose or product code.

questions.q: In the multiload 375, copper is present on the ____.
questions.why: Multiload 375 has copper on the vertical stems, contrasted with copper on the arms in CuT 380A.

questions.q: The bent arms of the multiload 375 carry spurs whose stated role is to ____.
questions.why: Bent arms with spurs -> spurs lessen expulsion.

questions.q: The multiload 375 thread is made of ____.

questions.q: The lifespan of the multiload 375 is ____.
questions.why: Life span: 5 years, shorter than CuT 380A's 10 years.

questions.q: Match the device to its lifespan: 1) Copper T 380A 2) Multiload 375 with A) 5 years B) 10 years.
questions.why: CuT 380A is 10 years; multiload 375 is 5 years.

questions.q: Mirena is a ____ IUCD (LNG 20).
questions.why: Mirena is the 3rd-generation hormonal IUCD containing LNG.

questions.q: Mirena releases ____ of levonorgestrel per day.
questions.why: Releases 20 mcg/day; 50 mcg/day is the copper figure for CuT 380A.

questions.q: Mirena's lifespan in the source is ____.
questions.why: Life span: 5 yrs, matching multiload 375 rather than CuT 380A.

questions.q: Mirena is used in AUB and ____.
questions.why: Used in AUB and endometrial hyperplasia without atypia.

questions.q: Source-check: the Mirena bullet says 'Not used as emergency contraception'. What is the best reading?
options: LNG-IUDs are abortifacients at any dose
It reflects this edition; evidence and guidance for 52-mg LNG-IUD emergency use have since evolved
Copper IUCDs also cannot be used for emergency contraception
Mirena is the only emergency method available
questions.why: The 2024 note is edition-specific and should not be generalised into a permanent rule.

questions.q: Mirena's stated mechanism is to prevent ____.
questions.why: moa: prevents implantation (does not cause anovulation).

questions.q: I) Mirena is described as containing LNG. II) It is described as working mainly by causing anovulation.
questions.why: Contains LNG is printed, but the mechanism is prevention of implantation, explicitly not anovulation.

questions.q: Which is NOT a Mirena statement on this sheet?
options: It is a frameless IUCD sutured to the myometrium
questions.why: The frameless/sutured description belongs to Gynefix on the next page.

sections.name: Mirena effects, Gynefix, implants, LARC and Essure

units.title: Mirena effects, Gynefix, implants, LARC and Essure

questions.q: The two side effects continued under the hormonal IUCD are irregular bleeding and ____.
options: endometrial atrophy with amenorrhoea on continuous use
questions.why: Irregular bleeding and endometrial atrophy on continuous use -> amenorrhoea are the two bullets.

questions.q: The Gynefix is a ____ IUCD and the fourth-generation device.
questions.why: Frameless IUCD: 4th gen IUCD, aka Copper fix IUCD/Flexiguard.

questions.why: Aka Copper fix IUCD/Flexiguard; Paraguard is CuT 380A.

questions.q: Gynefix is said to be used in ____ females.
questions.why: Used in nulliparous females; the copper cylinders are held by a nylon thread.

questions.q: The two Gynefix advantages printed are less pain and ____.
questions.why: Advantages: less pain, less expulsion rate.

questions.why: Single rod implant is the printed description.

questions.q: Implanon contains ____ of etonogestrel, released at ____ per day.
questions.why: Contains etonogestrel 68 mg -> released at 60 mcg/day.

questions.why: Inserted on non-dominant arm (medial side) on D1-D7 menstrual cycle.

questions.q: If inserted after day 7, the source requires added contraception for ____.
questions.why: If inserted after D7: added contraception required x 3 days.

questions.q: Implanon is classified as a ____ (LARC).
questions.why: Long acting reversible contraceptive (LARC).

questions.q: The source notes Implanon is ____ by the Government of India.
questions.why: Not provided free of cost by GoI, unlike the free Mala N.

questions.q: The source's LARC group consists of implants, IUCD and ____.
questions.why: Note: LARC: Implants, IUCD, Injectables.

questions.q: Source-check: Nexplanon is listed with both 'Barium sulfate in stem' and 'Not radiopaque'. What is the safest interpretation?
options: The two bullets conflict; barium sulfate is a radiopaque marker and product details must be checked
Radiopacity is unrelated to implant imaging
Barium sulfate makes every implant invisible on X-ray
Implanon and Nexplanon are identical in all respects
questions.why: The source lines are internally inconsistent; barium sulfate is added precisely to make the rod radiopaque, so the note is not a reliable product statement.

questions.q: Essure is a ____ device with an outer and an inner cylinder.
questions.why: Coiled device with outer & inner cylinder; inserted hysteroscopically.

questions.q: The Essure outer cylinder is made of ____ and the inner of stainless steel.
questions.why: Outer cylinder: Nickel + Titanium; inner cylinder: Stainless steel.

questions.q: Essure is inserted into the ____ part of the fallopian tube via hysteroscopy.
questions.why: Inserted into Intramural/Interstitial part of fallopian tube via hysteroscopy.

questions.q: Essure produces tubal occlusion by ____, complete by about ____.
questions.why: Tubal occlusion by inflammation; occlusion by 3 months.

questions.q: The Essure pathway requires confirmation of occlusion by HSG after 3 months. What else does the source advise during that interval?
options: Use other contraceptives until occlusion is confirmed
questions.why: Female advised for other contraceptives until 3 months; HSG confirms occlusion after 3 months.

questions.q: The success rate printed for Essure is ____.
questions.why: Success rate: 99% is the source figure for the historical device.

questions.q: Source-check: a learner wants to recommend Essure today. What is the appropriate response?
options: Essure is a historical/withdrawn device; study the mechanism but do not present it as an available option
Essure is the current first-line LARC in India
questions.why: The 2024 note describes a device no longer marketed in many settings; it is covered as printed history, not a current method.

sections.name: Laparoscopic ligation, mini lap, Pomeroy and Parkland

units.title: Laparoscopic ligation, mini lap, Pomeroy and Parkland

questions.q: Laparoscopic tubal ligation is described as the ____ method of ligation.

questions.why: Lap. tubal ring applicator with extended tip and one/two silastic rings.

questions.q: The MINI LAP TECHNIQUE begins by making a ____ in the isthmus of the fallopian tube.

questions.q: In mini lap the loop is occluded with a ____ ligature before it is cut.
questions.why: Step 2: loop occluded with single/double ligature; step 3: loop is cut.

questions.q: The two 'm/c techniques' of mini lap named are Pomeroy and ____.
questions.why: Pomeroy and modified pomeroy are bracketed as the m/c techniques.

questions.q: Pomeroy uses ____ catgut, which is absorbable but takes time to dissolve.
questions.why: Pomeroy: Chromic catgut, absorbable, takes time to dissolve.

questions.q: Modified Pomeroy uses ____ catgut, which dissolves quickly.

questions.q: The stated advantage of the Parkland technique is ____ of the two ends of the tube.

questions.q: Babcock's forceps and a window made in the mesentery are figure labels for the ____ technique.

questions.q: I) Pomeroy uses chromic catgut. II) Modified Pomeroy uses plain catgut and dissolves quickly.

sections.name: Irving, Uchida, Madlener, Kroener and outcome rankings

questions.why: Distal end is ligated and sutured along mesentery.

Pomeroy is highest for failure but only mid-ranked for recanalization, where clips and Fallope rings lead
Pomeroy is lowest on both lists

questions.q: I) Cautery is at the least-failure end. II) Cautery is at the least-recanalization end.

options: Treat them as the source's qualitative orderings, not absolute failure probabilities
Assume clips are a surgical ligation technique
Convert each position into an exact percentage

questions.q: After ruling out pregnancy, the first investigation listed for EH is ____.
questions.why: 1st Ix (after r/o pregnancy): TVS up-ET -> suspect EH -> take EB.

questions.q: The investigation of choice (IOC) for endometrial pathology named here is ____.
questions.why: IOC for endometrial pathology: Endometrial biopsy (EB).

questions.q: The gold standard listed in the EH overview is ____.
questions.why: Gold standard: Fractional curettage + Hysteroscopy.

questions.q: In the investigations line, ET stands for ____ and TVS for ____.
questions.why: The margin defines ET = endometrial thickness and TVS = trans-vaginal sonography.

questions.q: Match the EH investigation role: 1) First investigation 2) IOC 3) Gold standard with A) Fractional curettage plus hysteroscopy B) TVS C) Endometrial biopsy.
questions.why: The overview assigns TVS, EB and FC+hysteroscopy to first, IOC and gold-standard roles.

questions.q: A perimenopausal woman has AUB and a thick endometrium on TVS; pregnancy is excluded. Which sequence follows the source overview?
options: TVS first, then endometrial biopsy, with FC plus hysteroscopy as gold standard
questions.why: TVS is the first test, EB the IOC, and FC+hysteroscopy the gold standard.

questions.q: I) The source calls TVS the first investigation after pregnancy is ruled out. II) It calls endometrial biopsy the gold standard.
questions.why: TVS is first, but the gold standard is FC + hysteroscopy, not EB.

questions.q: A student reads 'Suspect EH, take EB' and concludes EB is the definitive gold-standard test. What is the source's actual hierarchy?
options: EB is both IOC and gold standard
None of the three is preferred
EB is the IOC; the gold standard is FC + hysteroscopy
questions.why: The arrows give TVS first, EB as IOC, and FC+hysteroscopy as gold standard; the roles are distinct.

sections.name: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications

units.title: Endometrial sampling and its age-based indications

questions.q: Endometrial sampling is also called ____ or endometrial aspiration cytology.
questions.why: Endometrial biopsy/endometrial aspiration cytology head the sampling block at 00:04:35.

questions.q: Endometrial sampling is done in the ____ setting.
questions.why: Done in: OPD; anaesthesia: Not required.

questions.q: The source states anaesthesia ____ for endometrial sampling.
questions.why: Anaesthesia: Not required is the printed line.

questions.q: In India the named sampling instrument is ____.
questions.why: Instrument used -> India: Karman's cannula; Pipelle and Vabra aspirator are the alternatives.

questions.q: Besides Karman's cannula, the sampling instruments listed are ____.
questions.why: Pipelle and Vabra aspirator are the two other devices in the sampling list.

questions.q: Which is NOT a device in the endometrial-sampling list?
questions.why: The ring applicator is a sterilisation instrument from the previous chapter.

questions.q: Match the age group to the endometrial-sampling trigger: 1) Reproductive age (<40 y) 2) Perimenopausal (FOGSI >=40 y / ACOG >=45 y) 3) Menopausal with A) EB irrespective of USG findings B) AUB plus risk factors or ET >=12 mm C) ET >=4 mm on TVS or AGCUS on Pap smear.
questions.why: Each age column has its own printed indication set; do not swap their thresholds.

questions.q: In reproductive-age women (<40 y), sampling is indicated for AUB with risk factors of Ca endometrium such as ____.
questions.why: C/o AUB + risk factors of Ca endometrium: PCOS, DM, HTN, Tamoxifen.

questions.q: The endometrial thickness threshold in the reproductive-age column is ET >= ____.
questions.why: ET >= 12 mm is the reproductive-age trigger; 4 mm belongs to the menopausal column.

questions.q: AUB unresponsive to medical management with tranexamic acid, OCP or ____ is a reproductive-age sampling indication.
questions.why: AUB unresponsive to medical mx (Tranexamic acid, OCP, progesterone).

questions.q: In the perimenopausal column the source recommends EB ____.
options: only if the Pap smear is normal
questions.why: EB irrespective of USG findings is the FOGSI/ACOG perimenopausal instruction.

questions.q: The perimenopausal age cut-off is >=40 years for FOGSI and >=____ for ACOG.
questions.why: Perimenopausal (>=40 yrs: FOGSI / >=45 yrs: ACOG).

questions.q: In the menopausal column, the TVS trigger is ET >= ____.
questions.why: Menopausal: ET >= 4 mm on TVS.

questions.q: The menopausal Pap-smear finding that triggers sampling is ____.
questions.why: Pap smear: AGCUS (Atypical glandular cells of undetermined significance).

questions.q: I) The reproductive-age ET threshold is 12 mm. II) The menopausal ET threshold is 4 mm.
questions.why: The two columns use 12 mm and 4 mm respectively; swapping them would misclassify patients.

questions.q: A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman has ET 6 mm on TVS. Which source indication applies?
options: Menopausal ET >=4 mm on TVS triggers endometrial biopsy
No indication until ET reaches 12 mm
questions.why: At 6 mm she exceeds the menopausal 4 mm threshold, so biopsy is indicated.

questions.q: Source-check: a 42-year-old with AUB and a normal USG is in the perimenopausal column. What does the source advise?
options: Start tranexamic acid and never sample
Reassure because the scan is normal
Perform EB irrespective of the USG findings
Wait for ET to reach 12 mm
questions.why: The perimenopausal instruction is EB regardless of ultrasound findings; thresholds are edition-specific study values.

sections.name: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways

units.title: Fractional curettage, hysteroscopy and EB report pathways

questions.q: Hysteroscopy is annotated here as being used for ____ pathology.
questions.why: Hysteroscopy: used for localised pathology, in contrast to fractional curettage.

questions.q: Fractional curettage (FC) is done in the ____.
questions.why: Done in: OT; anaesthesia: GA (under general anaesthesia).

questions.q: The anaesthesia line for fractional curettage is ____.
questions.why: Anaesthesia: GA (under general anaesthesia).

questions.q: The FC procedure begins with ____ curettage, then endometrial curettage.
questions.why: Procedure: Endocervical curettage (1st) -> endometrial curettage.

questions.q: The stated advantage of FC is diagnosis of ____ endometrial pathology.
questions.why: Advantage: Diagnosis generalised endometrial pathology.

questions.q: The stated disadvantage of FC is that it is ____ for localised pathology.
questions.why: Disadvantage: Not good for localised pathology; hysteroscopy covers the focal lesions.

questions.q: The margin note names ____ as the single best investigation.
questions.why: Note: Single best Ix -> Fractional curettage.

questions.q: Match the modality to its strength: 1) Hysteroscopy 2) Fractional curettage with A) Localised pathology B) Generalised endometrial pathology.
questions.why: Hysteroscopy targets focal disease; FC samples the generalised endometrium.

questions.q: A focal endometrial polyp is suspected. Which source statement explains why FC alone may miss it?
options: FC is the only test for focal lesions
FC is not good for localised pathology; hysteroscopy is used for focal lesions
TVS is the gold standard for polyps
questions.why: FC samples generalised tissue and is poor for localised pathology; hysteroscopy is the focal tool.

questions.q: The 'EB Report Interpretation & Management' heading lists ____ EB outcomes.
questions.why: EB outcomes: 1. Normal, 2. Metropathia hemorrhagica, 3. Endometrial hyperplasia +/- Atypia.

questions.q: Match each EB outcome to its next step: 1) Normal 2) Metropathia hemorrhagica 3) Endometrial hyperplasia +/- atypia with A) Progesterone (TOC) B) First-line AUB drugs, then FC+hysteroscopy if unresponsive C) Detailed hyperplasia management on the next sheet.
questions.why: The flow chart routes normal, metropathia and hyperplasia to different next steps.

questions.q: For a NORMAL EB report, first-line AUB drugs are tranexamic acid, OCP and ____.
questions.why: Use 1st line drugs to mx AUB: Tranexamic acid, OCP, Progesterone -> Oral / mirena.

questions.q: If a normal-EB patient is unresponsive to first-line drugs, the next step is ____.
questions.why: Unresponsive -> FC + Hysteroscopy.

questions.q: Which is NOT a first-line drug in the normal-EB pathway?
questions.why: Carboplatin is a chemotherapy drug from the endometrial-cancer chapter.

questions.q: Metropathia hemorrhagica is most common in a ____ female.
questions.why: m/c: Perimenopausal female.

questions.q: The underlying pathology of metropathia hemorrhagica is ____ cycles.
questions.why: Pathology: Anovulatory cycles.

questions.q: The bleeding pattern is amenorrhoea for 2-3 months followed by ____.
questions.why: Amenorrhea x 2-3 months -> HMB (Heavy menstrual bleeding).

questions.q: The HPE of metropathia hemorrhagica shows a ____ pattern.
questions.why: HPE: Swiss cheese pattern, proliferative endometrium, equivalent to cystic glandular hyperplasia.

questions.q: Metropathia hemorrhagica is described as equivalent to ____ hyperplasia.
questions.why: Equivalent to cystic glandular hyperplasia.

questions.q: The risk of malignancy printed for metropathia hemorrhagica is ____.
questions.why: Risk of malignancy: 1%; higher figures belong to EH with atypia.

questions.q: The treatment of choice (TOC) for metropathia hemorrhagica is ____.
questions.why: mx: TOC: Progesterone -> Oral / mirena.

questions.q: I) Metropathia hemorrhagica follows anovulatory cycles. II) Its HPE shows a Swiss cheese pattern.
questions.why: The pathology and HPE bullets are printed together.

questions.q: A perimenopausal woman has 2-3 months of amenorrhoea then heavy bleeding; biopsy shows a Swiss-cheese proliferative endometrium. Which source diagnosis and treatment fit?
options: EH with atypia treated by TAH
Normal endometrium treated with tranexamic acid
questions.why: The presentation, HPE and 1% risk define metropathia hemorrhagica; progesterone is the TOC.

questions.q: Which is NOT a metropathia hemorrhagica feature in the source?
questions.why: Atypia is not listed; it belongs to the EH-with-atypia branch on the next sheet.

sections.name: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance

units.title: EH without atypia: progesterone and surveillance

questions.q: Endometrial hyperplasia without atypia carries a malignancy risk of ____.
questions.why: Risk of malignancy: 1-3% for EH without atypia; 8-30% with atypia.

questions.q: The next step after EH without atypia is ____.
questions.why: Next step: Progesterone.

questions.q: Progesterone acts by downregulation of estrogen receptors, producing ____.
questions.why: Downregulation of estrogen receptors -> Endometrial atrophy.

questions.q: The source prefers ____ over oral medroxy progesterone acetate for EH without atypia.
questions.why: Mirena > Oral: medroxy progesterone acetate.

questions.q: For EH without atypia, ____ progesterone is preferred over cyclical.
questions.why: Continuous > Cyclical is printed under the progesterone branch.

questions.q: Cyclical progesterone needs at least ____ days for a protective effect.
questions.why: >= 12 days for a protective effect.

questions.q: The cyclical progesterone bullet notes ____ contraceptive benefit.
questions.why: No contraceptive benefit is listed for cyclical progesterone.

questions.q: After treatment for EH without atypia, a repeat biopsy is done at ____.
questions.why: Repeat biopsy at 3-6 months.

questions.q: If hyperplasia or bleeding persists at review, the next step is ____.
questions.why: Hyperplasia (+)/bleeding (+) -> FC + Hysteroscopy.

questions.q: I) Continuous progesterone is preferred to cyclical. II) Cyclical progesterone has no contraceptive benefit.
questions.why: The continuous-over-cyclical arrow and the no-contraceptive-benefit bullet are both on this sheet.

questions.q: A woman with EH without atypia is managed with oral cyclical progestogen. Which source caveat should be highlighted?
options: A >=12-day course is needed for a protective effect and it gives no contraceptive benefit
questions.why: The 12-day and no-contraception notes are edition-specific study points; Mirena and continuous therapy are preferred.

questions.q: Match the EH-without-atypia values: 1) Malignancy risk 2) Repeat biopsy 3) Minimum cyclical days with A) 12 days B) 1-3% C) 3-6 months.
questions.why: Risk, surveillance interval and cyclical duration are three distinct printed numbers.

sections.name: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy

units.title: EH with atypia and indications for FC plus hysteroscopy

questions.q: Endometrial hyperplasia with atypia carries a malignancy risk of ____.
questions.why: Risk of malignancy: 8-30% (up-up chance), far above the without-atypia figure.

questions.q: The next step for EH with atypia is ____.
questions.why: Next step: FC + hysteroscopy.

questions.q: The best management for EH with atypia is ____.
options: TAH (total abdominal hysterectomy, uterus plus cervix)
questions.why: Best: TAH (Total abdominal hysterectomy -> Uterus + cervix).

questions.q: If a patient refuses TAH, the source offers ____.
questions.why: Patient refuses TAH: Progesterone (megestrol).

questions.q: Failure or continued bleeding on megestrol leads to ____.
questions.why: Failure/continued bleeding -> Hysterectomy.

questions.q: Match the EH branch to its risk and management: 1) Without atypia 2) With atypia with A) 8-30% risk, TAH best B) 1-3% risk, progesterone and repeat biopsy.
questions.why: The two branches carry distinct malignancy risks and very different definitive management.

questions.q: Which is NOT an indication for FC plus hysteroscopy in the source note?
options: Routine TVS screening at 3 weeks postpartum
questions.why: Postpartum IUCD timing is a contraception topic, not an FC+hysteroscopy indication.

questions.q: An EB report of an ____ sample is one indication for FC plus hysteroscopy.
questions.why: EB report: Insufficient sample is listed among the indications.

questions.q: ____ is another listed indication for FC plus hysteroscopy because it limits blind sampling.
questions.why: In case of cervical stenosis appears in the indication list.

questions.q: EH without atypia plus ____ of medical management is the fourth indication.
questions.why: EB: EH w/o atypia + Failure of medical mx.

questions.q: I) EH with atypia has a higher malignancy risk than EH without atypia. II) TAH is the best management for EH with atypia.
questions.why: 8-30% exceeds 1-3%, and TAH is named the best treatment in the with-atypia branch.

questions.q: A biopsy shows EH with atypia; the patient declines hysterectomy and is started on megestrol, but bleeding continues. What does the source algorithm advise?
questions.why: Failure/continued bleeding on progesterone is followed by hysterectomy.

questions.q: Source-check: a learner reads 'TAH -> uterus + cervix' and concludes removing the cervix is always optional. What is the source's definition?
options: TAH removes the ovaries and tubes only
TAH here explicitly includes uterus plus cervix as the specimen
questions.why: The printed expansion defines the operation; the surrounding atypia pathway treats it as definitive management, with the usual counselling caveats for any surgery.

sections.name: Associated factors, protective factors and familial syndromes

units.title: Associated factors, protective factors and familial syndromes

questions.q: Endometrial cancer is said to be seen in ____ states.
questions.why: Seen in hyperestrogenic states opens the Associated Factors & Screening section at 00:01:03.

questions.q: The risk-factor mnemonic printed is ____.
questions.why: Mnemonic: Family has old aunt; the risk list follows.

questions.q: Among the risk factors, ____ is marked m/c (most common).
questions.why: Obesity: m/c is printed in the risk list.

questions.q: Which is NOT in the source's endometrial-cancer risk list?
options: Early menarche protection from early coitarche
questions.why: Early coitarche is a cervix-cancer risk factor in a later chapter, not an endometrial-cancer risk here.

questions.q: Unopposed estrogen risk is exemplified by PCOS, estrogen-only HRT and ____.
questions.why: Unopposed estrogen -> PCOS, estrogen only HRT, estrogen secreting hormones (Granulosa cell tumours).

questions.q: Nulliparity and ____ are both listed as risk factors.
questions.why: Nulliparity and Tamoxifen (2nd m/c) are risk entries; multiparity, pregnancy and OCP are protective.

questions.q: Tamoxifen is annotated as the ____ most common drug-related risk in this list.
questions.why: Tamoxifen: 2nd m/c; the annotation is source shorthand about ranking, not a quantified incidence.

questions.q: Source-check: the tamoxifen bullet adds a 'time between tamoxifen and pregnancy' of min 2 months, ideal 3 months. What is the safest reading?
options: The interval is a WHO legal requirement
It is an edition-specific spacing annotation; individual oncology and reproductive counselling governs care
Pregnancy must always occur exactly 3 months after tamoxifen
questions.why: The min/ideal line is study shorthand about a washout interval, not a universal rule; tamoxifen is not a drug to be used in pregnancy.

questions.q: OCPs protect because progesterone ____ estrogen receptors on the endometrium.
questions.why: OCP: Progesterone downregulates estrogen receptors -> decreased proliferation -> endometrial atrophy.

questions.q: The proposed (weaker) protective factors listed are ____.
questions.why: Proposed protective factors: Physical exercise and green tea; multiparity, pregnancy and OCP are the main ones.

questions.q: Match the factor: 1) Obesity 2) OCP 3) Green tea with A) Protective, proposed B) Risk, most common C) Protective, hormonal.
questions.why: The three columns separate the leading risk, a hormonal protective factor and a merely proposed protective factor.

questions.q: Corpus cancer syndrome is the triad of hypertension, obesity and ____.
questions.why: Hypertension, Obesity, Diabetes -> increased risk of endometrial Ca.

questions.q: Lynch II syndrome is also called ____ syndrome.
questions.why: Aka HNPCC syndrome: Hereditary non polyposis colorectal carcinoma.

questions.q: The most common cancer associated with Lynch II in the source is ____ cancer.
questions.why: Cancers associated with Lynch II -> m/c: Colon cancer.

questions.q: I) Obesity is labelled the most common risk factor. II) Multiparity is listed as protective.
questions.why: Obesity: m/c is in the risk column; multiparity is in the protective column.

questions.q: A student claims OCPs increase endometrial cancer risk because they contain estrogen. Which correction fits the source?
options: OCPs are the most common risk factor
OCPs have no effect on the endometrium
OCPs are protective because progestin downregulates endometrial estrogen receptors
questions.why: The source's protective mechanism is progestin-driven receptor downregulation and endometrial atrophy.

sections.name: Familial syndromes, screening and histopathologic types

units.title: Familial syndromes, screening and histopathologic types

questions.q: In Lynch syndrome the second most common cancer after colon is ____ cancer, exceeding ovarian.
questions.why: 2nd m/c: Endometrial Ca > Ovarian Ca.

questions.q: The mismatch-repair genes named for Lynch syndrome are ____.
questions.why: Genes involved: MLH1, MSH2, MSH6.

questions.q: The source quotes a ____ chance of endometrial cancer in Lynch syndrome.
questions.why: 60% chance of endometrial ca. in Lynch syndrome is the printed figure; it is a source statistic, not a personal-risk calculator.

questions.q: Cowden syndrome is linked to a mutation in the ____ gene on chromosome 10.
questions.why: Cowden syndrome: mutation in PTEN gene on chromosome 10.

questions.q: BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations are associated mainly with ____ cancer exceeding endometrial.
questions.why: 3) BRCA 1 & 2 mutation: Associated cancers: Ovarian ca > Endometrial ca.

questions.q: Which is NOT a familial syndrome in this screening list?
questions.why: The list names Lynch II, Cowden and BRCA1/2; Gardner is not printed here.

questions.q: Universal screening for endometrial cancer ____ according to the source.
questions.why: Universal screening not done; indication: Hereditary cancer.

questions.q: For hereditary-cancer families the source advises an annual ____.
options: endometrial biopsy from 35 years of age
questions.why: Annual endometrial biopsy: From 35 years of age; mx: OCPs if needed.

questions.q: The best method of prevention in familial syndromes is ____.
questions.why: Best method of prevention in familial syndromes: TAH + BSO.

questions.q: In that prophylactic surgery, TAH prevents ____ cancer and BSO prevents ____ cancer.
questions.why: TAH: Prevents endometrial ca.; BSO: Prevents ovarian ca.

questions.q: The indication for prophylactic TAH+BSO in the source is a completed family by ____.
questions.why: Indication: Completed family by 40 years of age; these are historical programme-style criteria, not a rule overriding individual choice.

questions.q: Source-check: the sheet offers risk-reducing TAH+BSO at 'completed family by 40 years'. What is the appropriate caution?
options: It is a source criterion; contemporary care requires genetic counselling, individual risk and autonomous informed consent
Surgery must be performed on every BRCA carrier at 40
questions.why: The printed age/parity criterion is not a universal or compulsory rule.

questions.q: The most common histopathologic type of endometrial cancer is ____.
questions.why: Adenocarcinoma: m/c type.

questions.q: The endometrioid adenocarcinoma is described as a tumour of a uterus lined by ____ epithelium.
questions.why: Uterus lined by columnar epithelium; a.k.a endometrioid tumour.

questions.q: Adenocarcinoma of the endometrium is also called a(n) ____ tumour.
questions.why: A.k.a endometrioid tumour.

questions.q: The most malignant histologic type in the source is ____.
questions.why: Clear cell: most malignant (Clear cell > Papillary serous).

questions.q: Which is NOT among the histopathologic types listed?
questions.why: Serous, Mucinous and Carcinosarcoma are listed; liposarcoma is not.

questions.q: Grading of adenocarcinoma is based on the ____ component.
questions.why: Based on undifferentiated solid component.

questions.q: Grade 1 (well differentiated) has a solid component of ____.
questions.why: Grade 1: <5% solid, well differentiated.

questions.q: Grade 2 (moderately differentiated) corresponds to a solid component of ____.
questions.why: Grade 2: 6-50% solid, moderately differentiated.

questions.q: Grade 3 (poorly differentiated) has a solid component of ____.
questions.why: Grade 3: >=50% solid, poorly differentiated.

questions.q: Match the adenocarcinoma grade: 1) Grade 1 2) Grade 2 3) Grade 3 with A) >=50% solid B) <5% solid C) 6-50% solid.
questions.why: The three solid-component bands ascend with worsening differentiation.

questions.q: A tumour shows 60% undifferentiated solid growth. Which source grade applies?
questions.why: >=50% solid maps to Grade 3, poorly differentiated.

questions.q: I) Higher grade corresponds to a larger solid component. II) Grade 1 is poorly differentiated.
questions.why: Solid percentage rises with grade number, but Grade 1 is well differentiated.

sections.name: Type 1 versus type 2 carcinoma, presentation and spread

units.title: Type 1 versus type 2 carcinoma, presentation and spread

questions.q: Type 1 endometrial carcinoma, the most common, comprises adenocarcinoma grades ____.
questions.why: Type 1: (m/c) Adenocarcinoma grade 1, 2.

questions.q: Type 2 carcinoma comprises grade 3 adenocarcinoma, clear cell and ____.
questions.why: Type 2: Adenocarcinoma grade 3, Clear cell, Papillary serous.

questions.q: Prognosis is ____ for type 1 and ____ for type 2.
questions.why: Prognosis: Good (type 1), Bad (type 2).

questions.q: Type 1 is associated with ____ estrogen and type 2 with decreased estrogen.
questions.why: Associated features: up-estrogen (type 1) versus down-estrogen (type 2).

questions.q: The predisposing factor for type 1 is ____ and for type 2 it is endometrial atrophy.
questions.why: Predisposing factors: Endometrial hyperplasia (type 1), Endometrial atrophy (type 2).

questions.q: Type 1 is described in a ____ woman aged 50-60; type 2 in a thin woman aged 60-70.
questions.why: Age & features: type 1 = 50-60 years, Obese; type 2 = 60-70 years, Thin.

questions.q: Gene mutations for type 1 are ____ and for type 2 it is p53.
questions.why: Gene mutation: PTEN, KRAS (type 1); p53 gene (type 2).

questions.q: Match the type: 1) Type 1 2) Type 2 with A) p53 mutation, thin, 60-70 y, bad prognosis B) PTEN/KRAS, obese, 50-60 y, good prognosis.
questions.why: Each column of the comparison table is internally consistent; the two must not be mixed.

questions.q: The most common age group for endometrial cancer is 50-70 years with a median of ____.
questions.why: m/c: 50-70 years; median: 60 years.

questions.q: The most common presenting complaint is ____.
questions.why: Irregular vaginal bleeding/AUB: m/c complaint.

questions.q: The most specific presentation is ____.
questions.why: Post menopausal bleeding (PMB): most specific.

questions.q: About ____ of postmenopausal bleeding is due to endometrial cancer in the source.
questions.why: 10% of PMB -> Endometrial ca.

questions.q: The most common cause of PMB in the source is ____ (37%), exceeding endometrial atrophy (30%).
questions.why: m/c cause of PMB: Polyp (37%) > Endometrial atrophy (30%).

questions.q: Pain referred to the right hypochondrium is termed ____ pain in the source.
questions.why: Pain referred to right hypochondrium: Simpson pain.

questions.q: The most common route of spread named is ____.
questions.why: Spread: Direct: m/c route.

questions.q: The note names ____ as the gatekeeper gene.
questions.why: Note: GateKeeper gene: PTEN.

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as a presentation of endometrial cancer?
questions.why: Jaundice is not in the presentation list.

questions.q: I) Type 2 has a worse prognosis than type 1. II) Type 2 arises on a background of endometrial hyperplasia.
questions.why: Type 2 is bad-prognosis but is linked to atrophy, not hyperplasia.

questions.q: An obese 55-year-old has a grade 1 endometrioid tumour. Which type and gene profile does the source predict?
questions.why: Age, obesity, low grade and good-prognosis type 1 align with PTEN/KRAS.

questions.q: In the diagnostic algorithm, ____ is the first investigation.
questions.why: TVS: First investigation -> Endometrial thickness.

questions.q: The TVS threshold that leads on to biopsy is endometrial thickness >= ____.
questions.why: Endometrial thickness >=4 mm -> Endometrial biopsy: IOC.

questions.q: The investigation of choice in the algorithm is ____.
questions.why: Endometrial biopsy: IOC; malignancy +ve proceeds to further staging.

questions.q: Fractional curettage plus hysteroscopy is described as the ____.
questions.why: Fractional curettage + Hysteroscopy -> Gold standard: Assesses type, grade & histology.

questions.q: The gold-standard step assesses ____.
questions.why: Assesses type, grade & histology.

questions.q: Match the step to the modality: 1) First investigation 2) IOC 3) Gold standard with A) Fractional curettage + hysteroscopy B) TVS C) Endometrial biopsy.
questions.why: This repeats the EH-chapter hierarchy inside the cancer diagnostic algorithm.

questions.q: A postmenopausal woman has ET 8 mm on TVS. Which source step follows?
questions.why: ET >=4 mm leads to endometrial biopsy, the investigation of choice.

questions.q: I) TVS is the first investigation in the algorithm. II) Endometrial biopsy is the gold standard.
questions.why: TVS is first; the gold standard is FC + hysteroscopy.

questions.q: Source-check: the EH overview also said FC+hysteroscopy is gold standard, but called TVS first and EB the IOC. What consistent reading emerges?
options: TVS is first, EB the IOC, and FC+hysteroscopy the gold standard across both sheets
The two sheets contradict every role
EB is the gold standard and FC+hysteroscopy the first test
questions.why: The roles are consistent between the EH overview and the cancer algorithm.

questions.q: If required, ____ is named the best investigation for involvement of myometrium and parametrium.
questions.why: MRI (Best investigation): Involvement of myometrium & parametrium.

questions.q: CT is named the best investigation for ____ metastases.
questions.why: CT (Best investigation for omental mets).

questions.q: ____ is named the best investigation for lymph node status.
questions.why: PET-CT: Best investigation for lymph node status.

questions.q: Match the imaging question: 1) Myometrial/parametrial involvement 2) Omental metastases 3) Nodal status with A) PET-CT B) MRI C) CT.
questions.why: The three 'best investigation' arrows map to three different modalities.

questions.q: The staging sequence runs from surgical staging through histopathological examination and tumour staging to ____.
questions.why: Surgical staging -> Histopathological examination -> Staging of tumour -> Post-op mx.

questions.q: The treatment of choice printed beside the staging sequence is ____.
questions.why: mx of choice: Radiotherapy is the note beside the staging flow.

questions.q: Staging of endometrial cancer uses FIGO ____ in the source.
questions.why: STAGING: FIGO 2009: is the printed table heading; FIGO 2023 is noted separately at the bottom.

questions.q: In FIGO 2009, stage IA means myometrial involvement of ____.
questions.why: IA: <50% of myometrium involvement; IB: >50%.

questions.q: Stage II involves the ____.
questions.why: Involvement of cervical stroma and glands defines stage 2.

questions.q: Stage IIIA involves ____.
options: serosa and adnexa (fallopian tube and ovaries)
questions.why: 3A: Serosa & adnexa (Fallopian tube & ovaries) involvement.

questions.q: Stage IIIB is involvement of the ____.
questions.why: 3B: Vagina/parametrium involvement.

questions.q: Stage IIIC1 denotes ____ nodes and IIIC2 denotes para-aortic nodes.
questions.why: 3C: Lymph node involvement -> 3C1 Pelvic nodes, 3C2 Para-aortic nodes.

questions.q: Stage IVA is regional metastasis to ____.
questions.why: 4A: Regional metastasis to bladder/bowel.

questions.q: Stage IVB is distant metastasis or ____ lymph node involvement.
questions.why: 4B: Distant metastasis or superficial lymph node involvement.

questions.q: The source notes that superficial lymph node involvement (stage 4B) applies to endometrial, ovarian and ____ cancer.
questions.why: Superficial lymph nodes involvement - Stage 4B: endometrial ca, ovarian ca and cervical ca.

questions.q: A tumour extends to the cervical stroma but not beyond the cervix. Which FIGO 2009 stage does the source assign?
questions.why: Cervical stromal/glandular involvement is stage 2.

Endometrial Ca spread to cervix moves stage I to II; cervical Ca spread to uterus does not change stage

questions.q: FIGO 2023 staging is noted to combine surgical staging, histopathological staging and ____.
questions.why: FIGO 2023 Staging: Surgical + Histopathological + molecular classification.

sections.name: Molecular classification, prognosis and surgical staging

questions.q: The molecular subtype with a good prognosis is ____ mutation.

questions.q: Intermediate prognosis is linked to mismatch repair defect (MMRD) and ____.
questions.why: Intermediate prognosis: MMRD, microsatellite instability (MSI).

questions.q: Match the molecular group: 1) Good 2) Intermediate 3) Bad with A) p53 abnormality B) POLE mutation C) MMRD/MSI.
questions.why: The three prognosis groups map to distinct molecular alterations.

questions.q: In the prognosis table, the good-prognosis column is ER/PR ____.

questions.q: The good-prognosis column is type ____ with grades 1 and 2.
questions.why: Good prognosis: Type 1, Grade 1,2; bad: Type 2, Grade 3.

questions.q: The bad-prognosis spread criterion includes myometrial involvement of ____.
questions.why: To cervix or structures beyond / myometrium involvement >=50% is the bad-prognosis spread cell.

questions.why: Spread of uterine tumour to ovary: Stage 3A, distinct from synchronous independent primaries.

questions.q: Two patients have a uterine endometrioid tumour plus ovarian involvement. What distinguishes IA3 from 3A in the source?
options: Simultaneous independent tumours are IA3; metastatic spread of the uterine tumour to ovary is 3A

questions.q: For stage I disease the surgical staging lists ____.
questions.why: Stage 1: TAH + BSO (Type 1 Hysterectomy).

questions.q: For stages 2 and 3 the operation named is ____.

questions.q: Stage 4 is managed by ____ surgery.
questions.why: Stage 4: Debulking Sx.

questions.q: For papillary serous tumour or carcinosarcoma the source adds ____.
questions.why: TAH + BSO + Infracolic omentectomy, due to increased chances of omental micrometastasis.

questions.q: For mucinous tumour the source adds ____ because of association with appendix cancer.

questions.q: In stage IA, a tumour smaller than ____ receives no nodal dissection.

questions.q: All stages other than stage IA receive ____ node dissection.

questions.q: Match the stage to surgery: 1) Stage 1 2) Stages 2 & 3 3) Stage 4 with A) Wertheim's hysterectomy B) TAH + BSO C) Debulking surgery.

questions.q: I) Wertheim's hysterectomy is listed for stage 1. II) Debulking surgery is listed for stage 4.
questions.why: Stage 1 uses TAH+BSO; Wertheim's is for stages 2/3 and debulking for stage 4.

questions.q: Low-risk post-op disease (adenocarcinoma grade 1/2 + stage IA) receives ____.
questions.why: Low: No mx.

questions.q: High-risk disease (stage 3/4 or papillary serous/clear cell tumour) receives ____.
questions.why: Chemotherapy + Radiotherapy: Carboplatin + Paclitaxel.

questions.q: The chemotherapy regimen named for high-risk disease is ____.
questions.why: Carboplatin + Paclitaxel.

questions.q: The intermediate-risk group (all others) receives ____.
questions.why: Intermediate: Radiotherapy.

questions.q: Match the risk group to post-op care: 1) Low 2) Intermediate 3) High with A) Radiotherapy B) No treatment C) Chemotherapy + radiotherapy.
questions.why: The three-tier table assigns distinct post-op management.

questions.q: A woman has stage 3B papillary serous carcinoma after surgery. Which post-op plan does the source assign?
questions.why: High risk (stage 3/4 or papillary serous/clear cell) gets chemoradiotherapy.

questions.q: In the postmenopausal-bleeding algorithm, the first test is ____.
questions.why: Post-menopausal bleeding -> Transvaginal sonography (TVS) for endometrial thickness.

questions.q: In the PMB algorithm, a 4 mm endometrium is managed with tranexamic acid, but bleeding continues. What does the source advise next?
options: Suspect type 2 endometrial cancer and do fractional curettage + hysteroscopy
questions.why: 4 mm -> Tranexamic acid -> Bleeding + -> Suspect type 2 endometrial cancer -> FC + Hysteroscopy.

questions.q: In the PMB algorithm, an endometrial thickness >4 mm proceeds to ____.
questions.why: >4 mm -> Endometrial biopsy.

questions.q: The most common cause of PMB in the causes list is ____.
questions.why: Causes: Polyp (m/c), Endometrial atrophy (2nd m/c), HRT, Endometrial Ca (10%).

questions.q: The second most common cause of PMB listed is ____.
questions.why: Endometrial atrophy (2nd m/c).

questions.q: Endometrial cancer accounts for about ____ of PMB in the causes list.
questions.why: Endometrial Ca (10%).

questions.q: Source-check: the causes list says polyp is m/c but also adds 'Cancer cervix: m/c cause of PMB in India'. What is the best reading?
options: It is a setting-specific annotation; the two 'm/c' claims are not universally interchangeable
Polyp causes no PMB in India
Cancer cervix is always the global m/c cause
questions.why: The India note is a local epidemiological claim and should not silently override the general list.

questions.q: The section's postmenopausal-bleeding heading carries the printed timestamp ____.
questions.why: 00:49:08 is on the PMB heading; the other times belong to earlier sections.

questions.q: I) PMB with ET >4 mm proceeds to endometrial biopsy. II) Persistent bleeding with a 4 mm endometrium prompts suspicion of type 2 disease.
questions.why: Both branches of the printed PMB algorithm lead to further evaluation.

questions.q: Which is NOT in the source's list of PMB causes?
questions.why: Cervical stenosis is an FC+hysteroscopy indication in the EH chapter, not a PMB cause here.

sections.name: Anatomy of the cervix and pubertal vaginal acidity

questions.why: Red on P/S exam for endocervix; pink for exocervix.

questions.why: Acts on glycogen -> Lactic acid -> Acidic pH of vagina.

questions.q: The end result of the Doderlein pathway is a(n) ____ vaginal pH.
questions.why: Lactic acid -> Acidic pH of vagina.

questions.q: The circular figure labels the squamocolumnar epithelium as the ____ zone.

questions.q: The opening at the centre of the diagram is the ____.
questions.why: External os is labelled with the transformation zone figure.

questions.q: I) The endocervix is lined by columnar epithelium. II) Doderlein bacilli produce lactic acid from glycogen.

options: It is lactic acid, not acetic acid

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the labels on the cervical anatomy diagram?
questions.why: Nabothian follicles are introduced on the next sheet, not on the anatomy figure.

questions.q: The 'Anatomy & Histopathology of Cervix' section opens at the printed timestamp ____.

sections.name: Transformation zone, metaplasia, Nabothian cysts and applied anatomy

questions.q: Squamous metaplasia is when ____ epithelium grows over columnar epithelium.
questions.why: Squamous epithelium grows over Columnar epithelium.

questions.q: The transformation zone is a dynamic area between the ____ and ____ squamocolumnar junctions.
questions.why: Dynamic area between old & new squamocolumnar junction.

questions.q: The position of the transformation zone changes with hormonal status, OCPs, pregnancy and ____.
questions.why: Position changes d/t Hormonal status, OCPs, Pregnancy, menopause.

questions.q: The original squamocolumnar junction is described as located near the ____.
questions.why: Original position: Located near external OS.

questions.q: Which is NOT listed as a factor shifting the transformation zone?
questions.why: The four listed factors are hormonal status, OCPs, pregnancy and menopause.

questions.q: Blockage of columnar epithelial glands gives rise to ____ cysts/follicles.
questions.why: Blockage of columnar epithelial glands -> Nabothian cysts/Follicles.

questions.q: Nabothian cysts are described as ____ and needing no biopsy.
questions.why: Physiological; Biopsy not required; they indicate the original SC junction.

questions.q: Nabothian cysts indicate the ____ squamocolumnar junction.
questions.why: Indicates the original SC junction.

questions.q: For cancer cervix, the most common histologic variety is ____ carcinoma.
questions.why: Squamous cell carcinoma: most common variety.

questions.q: The transformation zone is the ____ site for cervical cancer.
questions.why: Transformation zone (TZ): m/c site.

questions.q: The endocervix is named as the most common site for ____.
questions.why: Endocervix: m/c site for adenocarcinoma.

questions.q: A Pap smear samples ____ sites: the transition zone near the external os and the endocervix.
questions.why: 2 Samples: Transition zone near external OS; Endocervix.

questions.q: Match the cervical cancer fact: 1) Squamous cell carcinoma 2) Most common site 3) Adenocarcinoma site with A) Transformation zone B) Endocervix C) Most common variety.
questions.why: Histology, site and glandular origin are three separate applied-aspect lines.

questions.q: A clinician sees a smooth cyst on the ectocervix and wants to biopsy it. Which source statement is relevant?
options: Nabothian cysts are physiological and do not require biopsy
All cervical cysts need cone biopsy
questions.why: The source explicitly marks them physiological with no biopsy required.

questions.q: I) The transformation zone position can change in pregnancy. II) Nabothian cysts are premalignant.
questions.why: Pregnancy is a listed shifting factor, but Nabothian cysts are physiological, not premalignant.

questions.q: Dysplasia is described as ____ metaplasia.
questions.why: Dysplasia (Unorganized metaplasia).

questions.q: Metaplasia is ____ while dysplasia is pathological.
questions.why: Metaplasia: Physiological; Dysplasia: Pathological.

questions.q: Metaplasia is ____ but dysplasia is premalignant.
questions.why: Not premalignant (metaplasia) versus Premalignant (dysplasia).

questions.q: Metaplasia is seen in ____ females.
questions.why: Seen in all females.

questions.q: Dysplasia occurs in the presence of ____ for cancer cervix.
questions.why: Occurs in presence of risk factors by ca cervix.

questions.q: Dysplastic cells show an increased ____ ratio.
questions.why: Increased Nucleus: Cytoplasmic ratio.

questions.q: Dysplastic cells also show increased nuclear ____.
questions.why: Increased Nuclear pyknosis is the second characteristic.

questions.q: Match the feature: 1) Metaplasia 2) Dysplasia with A) Premalignant, risk-factor associated B) Physiological, seen in all females.
questions.why: The histopathology table contrasts the two processes on every row.

questions.q: A biopsy is reported as unorganised metaplasia with an increased nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio. Which source category fits?
questions.why: Unorganised metaplasia with nuclear changes is the dysplasia column.

questions.q: Which is NOT a characteristic of dysplastic cells in this table?
questions.why: The source lists increased, not decreased, nuclear pyknosis.

questions.q: I) Metaplasia is seen in all females. II) Dysplasia is not premalignant.
questions.why: Metaplasia is universal and physiological; dysplasia is explicitly premalignant.

sections.name: CIN grading and the role of Pap smear

units.title: CIN grading and the role of Pap smear

questions.q: CIN I involves the ____ of the cervical epithelial thickness.
questions.why: Cervical epithelial thickness <1/3rd -> CIN I.

questions.q: CIN 2 involves ____ of the epithelial thickness.
CIN 3 involves ____ of the epithelial thickness.
Match the CIN grade to thickness: 1) CIN I 2) CIN 2 3) CIN 3 with A) 1/3-2/3 B) <1/3 C) >=2/3.
questions.why: The grades ascend with the fraction of involved epithelium.

questions.q: Full-thickness involvement without involvement of the overlying membrane is ____.
questions.why: Complete thickness without involvement of overlying membrane -> Carcinoma in situ (CIS).

questions.q: Involvement of the overlying membrane defines ____.
questions.why: Involvement of overlying membrane -> Invasive carcinoma of cervix.

questions.q: CIN I, II or III is diagnosed by ____.
questions.why: CIN I, 2, or 3: Dx by biopsy or tissue sample.

questions.q: A Pap smear is a ____ test that identifies dysplasia.
questions.why: Pap smear: Cytological test; Identifies dysplasia.

questions.q: A Pap smear cannot assess the ____ of dysplasia.
questions.why: Extent cannot be assessed; inference is only dysplasia + or dysplasia -.

questions.q: An abnormal Pap smear should be followed by ____.
questions.why: Abnormal pap smear -> Biopsy.

questions.q: Management ____ based on the Pap smear report alone.
questions.why: mx is not based on pap smear report.

questions.q: I) Pap smear can grade the depth of CIN. II) CIN is diagnosed on a biopsy or tissue sample.
questions.why: Pap smear is cytological and cannot assess extent; tissue diagnosis is required for CIN.

questions.q: A screening Pap smear reports dysplasia. Which source-consistent next step follows?
options: Proceed to biopsy for tissue diagnosis
questions.why: Management is not based on the smear; an abnormal result leads to biopsy.

questions.q: Which is NOT a Pap smear inference in the source?
options: Exact depth of invasion in millimetres
questions.why: Pap smear gives a dysplasia +/- cytology result; extent requires tissue.

sections.name: Conventional Pap smear instruments and samples

questions.why: Instruments: Ayres spatula, Endocervical brush.

questions.why: From transition zone with bifid end of Ayer's spatula.

questions.q: The other end of the Ayres spatula is used for ____ cytology and buccal smear.

questions.why: Using endocervical brush is the endocervical sampling line.

questions.why: 00:22:42 is on the Pap Smear heading.

questions.q: Match the instrument to its use: 1) Ayres spatula 2) Endocervical brush with A) Endocervical sample B) Ectocervical/transition-zone sample.
questions.why: The spatula scrapes the ectocervix; the brush samples the canal.

questions.why: The two-sample technique needs both the spatula and the brush.

sections.name: Pap smear procedure, liquid-based cytology and Bethesda counts

questions.why: Relative contraindication: Active bleeding.

questions.why: Separate cervico-vaginal swab is taken for HPV DNA testing.

questions.q: Liquid-based cytology can be performed ____.

questions.q: Which is NOT a listed advantage of liquid-based cytology?

questions.q: The leading risk factor listed for cancer cervix is ____.

questions.q: Early coitarche is defined in the source as before ____ years.
questions.why: Early coitarche < 18 yrs.

questions.q: Early childbirth is defined as before ____ years in the risk list.
questions.why: Early childbirth <20 yrs.

questions.q: OCPs are described as a ____ risk factor for adenocarcinoma of the cervix.

questions.q: Smoking is linked in the source to ____ carcinoma of the cervix.
questions.why: Smoking -> Squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.q: Match the risk factor to its associated cancer: 1) OCPs 2) Smoking with A) Squamous cell carcinoma B) Adenocarcinoma of cervix.
questions.why: The two arrows point to different histologies.

questions.q: The source lists ____ as an immunocompromising risk factor.

questions.q: Which is NOT a cancer-cervix risk factor in the source?

questions.q: The source says cervical cancer ____ relation to early menarche and late menopause.
questions.why: Cervix ca has no relation to early menarche & late menopause.

questions.q: The source states there is ____ role of familial inheritance in cancer cervix.
questions.why: No role of familial inheritance in ca cervix.

questions.q: HRT ____ the risk of cancer cervix according to the source.
questions.why: HRT does not increase risk of ca cervix.

questions.q: A student assumes cervical cancer is strongly inherited because it clusters in families. Which source line corrects this?
options: There is no role of familial inheritance in cancer cervix
HRT is the main inherited cause
BRCA1/2 mutations cause most cervical cancers
questions.why: The notable-features line explicitly denies a familial-inheritance role.

questions.q: I) Early coitarche (<18 yrs) is a risk factor. II) Late menopause is a risk factor.
