questions.q: True/False: Cryoablation yields a tissue specimen for histopathology.
options: False - it yields fluid for culture
questions.why: The printed disadvantage is that no tissue specimen is obtained.

questions.q: How many criteria must all be fulfilled before cryoablation in CIN 1?
questions.why: The prerequisites list four bullets: entire TZ visible, lesion completely visible, not HIV +ve, lesion not > 2 quadrants.

questions.q: Fill up: The entire ____ should be visible before cryoablation is done in CIN 1.
questions.why: 'Entire TZ should be visible' heads the prerequisites.

questions.q: Which HIV status is printed as acceptable for cryoablation in CIN 1?
questions.why: 'Not be HIV +ve' is the third prerequisite.

questions.q: The lesion must not involve more than how many quadrants of the cervix?
questions.why: 'Lesion not > 2 quadrants of cervix' closes the list.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed cryoablation prerequisite?
questions.why: The prerequisites are visibility of TZ and lesion, HIV negativity and lesion within 2 quadrants; cryoablation is for CIN 1.

questions.q: True/False: A CIN 1 lesion spanning three quadrants of the cervix still satisfies the printed prerequisites for cryoablation.
questions.why: The lesion must not exceed 2 quadrants.

questions.q: Fill up: In LLETZ/LEEP the total ____ area is removed.
questions.why: 'Total dysplastic area is removed' opens the LLETZ block.

questions.q: What is passed into the LLETZ instrument according to the printed chain?
questions.why: The chain prints 'Current -passed into-> Instrument'.

questions.q: The loop in LLETZ is printed to:
options: Cut and coagulate at the same time
questions.why: 'Cut & coagulate at the same time' follows the instrument box.

questions.q: The printed duration of the LLETZ procedure is:
questions.why: 'Short procedure : 10-15 mins' under advantage.

questions.q: Up to what depth are tissues removed in LLETZ?
questions.why: 'Tissues removed until 10 mm depth'.

questions.q: LLETZ is printed as the treatment of choice for which grades, at any age and parity?
questions.why: 'TOC for CIN 2 & 3 for any age & parity'.

questions.q: Which advantage allows histopathology after LLETZ but not after cryoablation?
options: Tissue sample can be sent for HPE
questions.why: The indented note under TOC is 'Tissue sample can be sent for HPE', unlike cryoablation.

questions.q: The printed disadvantage of LLETZ is:
questions.why: 'Disadvantage : Bleeding (minimal)'.

questions.q: LLETZ shares which setting advantage with colposcopy?
questions.why: Both lists print 'OPD procedure'.

questions.q: Match each LLETZ attribute with its printed value - 1) Energy 2) Time 3) Depth 4) Disadvantage ... A) 10 mm B) Minimal bleeding C) Current D) 10-15 mins ... choose:
questions.why: Current is passed into the loop, the procedure lasts 10-15 mins, depth is 10 mm and bleeding is minimal.

questions.q: The figure captioned on page 241 with panels A to F shows:
questions.why: The six-panel photograph is captioned 'LLETZ'.

questions.q: In special scenario 1, a positive endocervical curettage leads next to:
questions.why: The chain prints 'Endocervical curettage positive -> Cone biopsy'.

questions.q: Fill up: In special scenario 1, cone biopsy revealing adenocarcinoma in situ ends in ____.
questions.why: 'Adenocarcinoma in situ -> Hysterectomy' closes scenario 1.

questions.q: In special scenario 2, a pap smear of HSIL is followed by:
questions.why: 'PAP smear : HSIL -> Colposcopy & biopsy' opens scenario 2.

questions.q: Which colposcopic biopsy results create the printed 'discrepancy in reports' in scenario 2?
questions.why: 'Colposcopy & biopsy : CIN 1 or Normal' with the arrow labelled discrepancy in reports.

questions.q: The discrepancy in scenario 2 is resolved by:
questions.why: The arrow from discrepancy in reports ends at cone biopsy.

questions.q: Arrange scenario 1 in printed order - 1) Adenocarcinoma in situ 2) Endocervical curettage positive 3) Hysterectomy 4) Cone biopsy ... choose:
questions.why: The printed chain is curettage positive, cone biopsy, adenocarcinoma in situ, hysterectomy.

questions.q: Scenario: A 40-year-old with HSIL pap has colposcopic biopsy reading CIN 1. According to the printed special scenario, what should be done next?
options: Accept the CIN 1 and follow up
questions.why: HSIL pap against CIN 1 biopsy is the printed discrepancy that mandates cone biopsy.

questions.q: True/False: Adenocarcinoma in situ found on cone biopsy is managed by hysterectomy in the printed scenario.
questions.why: Scenario 1 ends 'Adenocarcinoma in situ -> Hysterectomy'.

questions.q: Fill up: In cone biopsy a ____ shaped area of cervix is cut.
questions.why: 'Cone shaped area of cervix is cut' on page 241.

questions.q: Which three zones must the cone include?
options: Exo/ecto cervix, transformational zone and endocervix
questions.why: The 'To include' list is exo/ecto cervix, transformational zone, endocervix.

questions.q: Cone biopsy is performed in which setting?
questions.why: 'Done in OT under GA' closes the cone biopsy bullets.

questions.q: The cone biopsy diagram on page 241 labels which three cervical regions from above down?
questions.why: The figure leader lines read endocervix, TZ, ectocervix.

questions.q: Odd one out - which structure is NOT inside the printed cone specimen?
questions.why: The cone includes exo/ecto cervix, transformational zone and endocervix only.

questions.q: True/False: Unlike colposcopy and LLETZ, cone biopsy needs the operating theatre and general anaesthesia.
options: False - it needs only local anaesthesia
False - it is an OPD procedure
questions.why: 'Done in OT under GA' contrasts with the OPD label on colposcopy and LLETZ.

questions.q: Which three diagnostic indications for cone biopsy are printed on page 242?
options: Suspecting adenocarcinoma or adenocarcinoma in situ, poorly visualised TZ on colposcopy, and discrepancy in pap smear and colposcopy reports
Microinvasive cancer, visible growth, and positive punch biopsy
Suspecting squamous cancer, satisfactory colposcopy, and concordant reports
HSIL pap, ASCUS pap and AGCUS pap
questions.why: The diagnostic bullets list exactly those three indications.

questions.q: Fill up: A poorly visualised ____ on colposcopy is a printed diagnostic indication for cone biopsy.
questions.why: 'Poorly visualised TZ on colposcopy' is the second diagnostic bullet.

questions.q: The therapeutic indications place cone biopsy as management of Ca cervix in which group?
questions.why: 'Mx of Ca cervix in young females' heads the therapeutic bullets.

questions.q: Which FIGO stage is printed as microinvasive Ca under the therapeutic indication?
questions.why: The sub-bullet prints 'Stage IA : microinvasive Ca'.

questions.q: Cone biopsy gives evidence of what key feature in the therapeutic list?
questions.why: 'Evidence of microinvasion' is the last therapeutic bullet.

questions.q: Match each cone biopsy indication class with its printed items - 1) Diagnostic 2) Therapeutic ... A) Evidence of microinvasion, mx of Ca cervix in young females B) Suspected adenocarcinoma in situ, poorly visualised TZ, discrepant reports ... choose:
questions.why: The diagnostic arm lists suspicion of adenocarcinoma in situ, poor TZ view and report discrepancy; the therapeutic arm lists microinvasion and young females.

questions.q: P-16 protein testing is invoked when the pap smear shows confusion between which two categories?
questions.why: The flow prints 'Confusion between LSIL & HSIL : Indeterminate'.

questions.q: An increased p-16 protein result points to:
questions.why: The raised arrow arm is labelled HSIL.

questions.q: Fill up: A normal p-16 protein result leaves the report as ____.
questions.why: The normal arm of the p-16 tree ends at LSIL.

questions.q: Arrange the p-16 pathway in printed order - 1) P-16 protein 2) Pap smear 3) Indeterminate confusion between LSIL and HSIL 4) HSIL or LSIL answer ... choose:
questions.why: Pap smear precedes the indeterminate confusion, then p-16 protein, then the HSIL or LSIL split.

questions.q: Scenario: A pap smear cannot decide between LSIL and HSIL and p-16 staining is strongly increased. The printed inference is:
questions.why: The upward arrow from p-16 leads to HSIL when the protein is raised.

questions.q: True/False: A normal p-16 result downgrades the indeterminate report towards LSIL.
questions.why: The normal arm of the printed tree terminates at LSIL.

questions.q: The most common type of cancer cervix printed is:
questions.why: 'Squamous cell cervix : m/c type of cancer cervix' on page 243.

questions.q: Within squamous cell cancer cervix, the most common subtype is:
questions.why: The first branch prints 'Large cell non-keratinising type (m/c type)'.

questions.q: Which squamous subtype carries the printed poor prognosis?
questions.why: 'Small cell (poor prognosis)' is the third branch.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common HPV association printed for squamous cell cervix is HPV ____.
questions.why: 'm/c association : HPV 16' under the squamous arm.

questions.q: Adenocarcinoma of cervix is printed as which commonest rank?
questions.why: 'Adenocarcinoma : 2nd m/c' opens that block.

questions.q: Adenocarcinoma of cervix is most common in which group?
questions.why: 'm/c in young female' is printed under adenocarcinoma.

questions.q: The printed risk factor for adenocarcinoma of cervix is:
questions.why: 'Risk factor : OCP' under adenocarcinoma.

questions.q: Fill up: Adenocarcinoma of cervix is most commonly associated with HPV ____.
questions.why: 'm/c association : HPV 18' under adenocarcinoma.

questions.q: The most common site printed for adenocarcinoma of cervix is:
questions.why: 'm/c site : Endocervix' closes the adenocarcinoma list.

questions.q: Match each cancer type with its printed attribute - 1) Squamous cell 2) Adenocarcinoma ... A) HPV 18, OCP risk, endocervix B) HPV 16, large cell non-keratinising m/c ... choose:
questions.why: Squamous pairs with HPV 16 and the large cell non-keratinising subtype; adenocarcinoma with HPV 18, OCP and endocervix.

questions.q: Odd one out - which feature belongs to squamous rather than adenocarcinoma of cervix?
questions.why: HPV 16 sits under the squamous arm; the other three under adenocarcinoma.

questions.q: True/False: Small cell squamous carcinoma of cervix carries the printed poor prognosis.
questions.why: The bracket prints 'Small cell (poor prognosis)'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common site of cancer cervix printed is the ____ zone.
questions.why: 'm/c site : Transitional zone' under features.

questions.q: The bimodal most common age printed for cancer cervix is:
questions.why: 'm/c age : 35-39 yrs & 60-64 yrs'.

questions.q: The most common symptom of cancer cervix printed is:
questions.why: 'Irregular bleeding : m/c symptom'.

questions.q: Which symptom is printed as the most specific for cancer cervix?
questions.why: 'Post coital bleeding : most specific symptom'.

questions.q: Fill up: The discharge printed in cancer cervix is a ____ vaginal discharge.
questions.why: 'Dirty vaginal discharge' is the third symptom bullet.

questions.q: The most common carcinoma causing pyometra printed is:
questions.why: 'Pyometra (m/c Ca causing pyometra : Ca cervix)'.

questions.q: Dyspnoea, cough, haemoptysis and chest pain in cancer cervix point to:
questions.why: That symptom cluster is labelled 'Lung metastasis'.

questions.q: Sciatica, haematuria and lymphedema together indicate:
questions.why: The cluster is labelled 'Pelvic side wall involvement'.

questions.q: Fill up: The most common cause of death in cancer cervix printed is ____ failure.
questions.why: 'm/c cause of death : Renal failure'.

questions.q: Match each symptom cluster with its printed meaning - 1) Irregular bleeding 2) Post coital bleeding 3) Dyspnoea with haemoptysis 4) Sciatica with lymphedema ... A) Most specific symptom B) m/c symptom C) Pelvic side wall involvement D) Lung metastasis ... choose:
questions.why: Irregular bleeding is m/c, post coital is most specific, respiratory features mean lung metastasis and sciatica with lymphedema means pelvic side wall.

questions.q: Scenario: A 62-year-old with treated cancer cervix presents with unilateral sciatica and leg lymphedema. Which printed site of involvement explains this?
questions.why: Sciatica, haematuria and lymphedema are the printed pelvic side wall involvement triad.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed symptom line of cancer cervix?
options: Painless haematuria as the m/c symptom
questions.why: Haematuria appears only inside the pelvic side wall cluster; the m/c symptom is irregular bleeding.

questions.q: True/False: Post coital bleeding is printed as both a symptom of cancer cervix and the most specific one.
options: False - it is m/c but not specific
False - it is specific but not listed as symptom
questions.why: The bullets print it as the most specific symptom among the symptom list.

questions.q: Fill up: The printed symptom bullet between pyometra and the lung metastasis cluster reads post menopausal ____ (preserved as printed).
questions.why: Page 243 prints 'Post menopausal spread.' verbatim between the pyometra and dyspnoea bullets.

questions.q: Odd one out - which printed symptom bullet sits immediately before the pelvic side wall cluster?
options: Dyspnea, cough, hemoptysis and chest pain
questions.why: The respiratory cluster precedes the sciatica-hematuria-lymphedema line on page 243.

units.title: Route of Spread and Lymphatic Drainage

questions.q: Give the printed hierarchy of spread routes in cancer cervix:
questions.why: 'Direct > Lymphatic > Hematogenous' on page 243.

questions.q: Fill up: By the hematogenous route the most common metastatic site printed is the ____.
questions.why: 'm/c site : Lungs (Hematogenous route)'.

questions.q: The first two lymph node groups printed under drainage are:
options: Hypogastric (internal iliac) nodes and obturator node
questions.why: The drainage bullets open with hypogastric (internal iliac) nodes then obturator node.

questions.q: Fill up: The most specific symptom of cancer cervix printed on page 243 is ____ bleeding.
questions.why: 'Post coital bleeding : most specific symptom'.

questions.q: Numeric: Give the two printed peaks of the most common age in cancer cervix as a pair of ranges.
questions.why: The features line prints both peaks.

units.title: Route of Spread and Lymphatic Drainage (cont.)

questions.q: Which node is printed as the sentinel node of the cervix?
questions.why: Page 244 prints 'Paracervical node : Sentinel node'.

questions.q: Which nodal group completes the printed drainage list after obturator?
questions.why: 'External iliac nodes' is the second bullet on page 244.

questions.q: Fill up: The cervix does not drain into ____ lymph nodes, so they are not included in radiotherapy.
questions.why: 'Cervix does not drain into superficial lymph nodes : Not included in radiotherapy'.

questions.q: Why are superficial lymph nodes excluded from radiotherapy fields?
options: Because they lie outside the pelvis only
Because they drain the vulva only
Because the cervix does not drain into them
questions.why: The printed reason is the absent drainage of cervix into superficial nodes.

questions.q: Arrange the printed nodal drainage sequence from the cervix outward - 1) External iliac 2) Paracervical (sentinel) 3) Hypogastric and obturator ... choose the printed listing order:
questions.why: Page 243 lists hypogastric and obturator first, page 244 adds paracervical as sentinel then external iliac.

questions.q: True/False: Hematogenous spread is the least common of the three printed routes.
questions.why: The hierarchy Direct > Lymphatic > Hematogenous puts hematogenous last.

sections.name: Radiotherapy Fields, Sites Involved and Post Coital Bleeding Algorithm

questions.q: External beam radiotherapy is indicated for which nodal involvement?
questions.why: 'EBRT : Pelvic lymph nodes involvement' on page 244.

questions.q: Fill up: Extended EBRT equals EBRT plus ____ lymph node involvement.
questions.why: 'Extended EBRT : EBRT + Paraaortic lymph nodes involvement'.

questions.q: Match the radiotherapy field with its printed nodal indication - 1) EBRT 2) Extended EBRT ... A) Paraaortic nodes B) Pelvic nodes ... choose:
questions.why: EBRT covers pelvic nodes; extended EBRT adds paraaortic nodes.

units.title: Sites Involved and Post Coital Bleeding Algorithm

questions.q: List the printed sites involved in cancer cervix:
options: Parametrium, pelvic side walls, bladder, bowel, lungs and kidney
Parametrium, vagina, bladder, rectum and liver
Uterus, ovaries, bladder, bowel and lungs
Parametrium, pelvic side walls, urethra, rectum and spleen
questions.why: The line prints 'Parametrium, pelvic side walls, bladder, bowel, lungs, kidney'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which organ is absent from the printed sites involved list?
questions.why: Ovary is not in the printed list; involvement of ovaries is separately noted as under 1%.

questions.q: The post coital bleeding algorithm starts from which causative pathologies?
questions.why: The top box prints 'Ca cervix, polyp, endometrium'.

questions.q: After per speculum examination, a normal cervix in the algorithm leads to:
questions.why: The normal arm runs pap smear AB(N) then into colposcopy.

questions.q: A barrel shaped, friable or indurated cervix in the algorithm is directed to:
questions.why: The middle arm joins the colposcopy box.

questions.q: A visible cervical growth on per speculum examination in the algorithm goes to:
questions.why: The right arm ends in punch biopsy.

questions.q: Match the per speculum finding with its printed next step - 1) Normal cervix 2) Barrel shaped/friable/indurated cervix 3) Visible growth ... A) Punch biopsy B) Pap smear then colposcopy C) Colposcopy ... choose:
questions.why: Normal cervix gets pap then colposcopy, an indurated cervix goes to colposcopy and a visible growth to punch biopsy.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with post coital bleeding has a friable indurated cervix but no frank growth on speculum. The printed algorithm sends her to:
questions.why: The friable/indurated arm terminates at colposcopy.

questions.q: The general examination findings printed for cancer cervix are:
options: Thin built, cachexic and low socio-economic status
Thin built with high socio-economic status
questions.why: The two bullets are thin built, cachexic and low socio-economic status.

questions.q: Fill up: On P/A examination an abdomino pelvic lump may be felt due to ____ (collection of pus in the uterus).
questions.why: 'Abdomino pelvic lump d/t pyometra (Collection of pus in the uterus)'.

questions.q: The P/S examination growth is described as:
questions.why: 'Growth : Ulcerative/Fungating mass'.

questions.q: A friable cervix on speculum is defined on the page as one that:
questions.why: 'Friable cervix : Bleeds on touch'.

questions.q: The cervix in cancer cervix is also described on P/S as:
questions.why: 'Hard & nodular cervix' is the third P/S bullet.

questions.q: Per rectal or per vaginorectal examination is printed to assess which structures?
questions.why: 'Examination of parametrium and utero sacral ligaments' heads that block.

questions.q: The positive per rectal finding printed is:
questions.why: The sub-bullet prints 'Thickening & nodularity'.

questions.q: Match each examination with its printed finding - 1) General 2) P/A 3) P/S 4) Per rectal ... A) Ulcerative/fungating growth, friable cervix B) Cachexia and low socio-economic status C) Parametrial thickening and nodularity D) Abdomino pelvic lump from pyometra ... choose:
questions.why: General shows cachexia, P/A the pyometra lump, P/S the growth and friable cervix, per rectal the parametrial nodularity.

questions.q: True/False: Per vaginorectal examination in cancer cervix is aimed at the parametrium and uterosacral ligaments.
questions.why: The heading prints exactly those two structures.

questions.q: Fill up: The sentinel node of the cervix printed on page 244 is the ____ node.
questions.why: 'Paracervical node : Sentinel node'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which node is NOT in the printed cervical drainage list?
questions.why: The printed list is hypogastric, obturator, paracervical and external iliac; common iliac is absent.

questions.q: True/False: The cervix draining into superficial lymph nodes is the reason they are included in radiotherapy fields.
options: False - they are included for another reason
False - superficial nodes are always irradiated
questions.why: The page prints the opposite: no drainage, hence not included.

questions.q: True/False: Extended EBRT adds paraaortic nodal coverage to standard EBRT.
options: False - it adds pelvic coverage to brachy
questions.why: 'Extended EBRT : EBRT + Paraaortic lymph nodes involvement'.

questions.q: The printed prognostic hierarchy in cancer cervix is:
questions.why: 'Prognostic markers : Staging > Lymph nodes' on page 245.

questions.q: Fill up: The diagnostic investigation printed for cancer cervix is cervical ____.
questions.why: 'Diagnostic : Cervical biopsy'.

questions.q: For microinvasive cancer detected on LEEP, the printed next procedure is:
questions.why: 'For microinvasive cancer on LEEP -> Cone biopsy'.

questions.q: The printed rate of ovarian involvement in cancer cervix is:
questions.why: 'Note : Involvement of ovaries (<1%)'.

questions.q: Why are ovaries preserved when hysterectomy is done for Ca cervix in young females?
questions.why: 'Ovaries preserved : To avoid pre-mature menopausal symptoms'.

questions.q: True/False: Ovarian preservation at hysterectomy for Ca cervix is justified by the under-1% involvement rate.
options: False - preservation is only for fertility
questions.why: The note pairs the <1% involvement with preserving ovaries in young females.

questions.q: Cancer cervix staging is printed as clinical staging plus which addition?
questions.why: 'Clinical staging + Radiological investigation' heads the staging block.

questions.q: USG in the staging workup is printed to detect:
questions.why: 'USG : Presence of pyometra'.

questions.q: CT scan in the staging workup assesses:
questions.why: 'CT scan : Lymph node status'.

questions.q: Fill up: Involvement of the parametrium is assessed on ____.
questions.why: 'MRI : Involvement of parametrium'.

questions.q: PET CT in the staging list is printed for:
questions.why: 'PET CT : Lymph nodes involvement'.

questions.q: IVP in the staging workup looks at:
questions.why: 'IVP : Kidney & ureter involvement'.

questions.q: Match each endoscopic or plain study with its printed target - 1) Cystoscopy 2) Sigmoidoscopy 3) Chest X-ray ... A) Lung involvement B) Bladder involvement C) Rectum involvement ... choose:
questions.why: Cystoscopy sees the bladder, sigmoidoscopy the rectum and chest X-ray the lungs.

questions.q: The best investigation printed for parametrial involvement is:
questions.why: 'Involvement of parametrium : MRI' under best investigation for.

questions.q: For lymph node involvement the printed best hierarchy is:
questions.why: 'LN involvement : PET-CT > CT scan'.

questions.q: Match each staging question with its printed best tool - 1) Parametrium 2) Lymph nodes 3) Ureter and kidney 4) Bladder ... A) IVP B) Cystoscopy C) MRI D) PET-CT ... choose:
questions.why: MRI for parametrium, PET-CT for nodes, IVP for ureter and kidney, cystoscopy for bladder.

questions.q: Scenario: A cancer cervix patient needs accurate nodal mapping before chemoradiation planning. The printed best tool is:
questions.why: PET-CT outranks CT scan for lymph node involvement.

units.title: FIGO Staging Stages I and II

questions.q: Stage IA in the printed FIGO table is defined as:
options: Microscopic cancer up to 7 mm deep
Microscopic cancer up to 3 mm deep
Microscopic/microinvasive cancer up to 5 mm deep
questions.why: The IA row prints 'microscopic/microinvasive cancer <=5 mm deep'.

questions.q: Fill up: Stage IA1 is printed as up to ____ mm deep.
questions.why: 'IA1 <=3 mm deep'.

questions.q: Stage IA2 depth printed in the table is:
questions.why: 'IA2 4-5 mm deep'.

questions.q: Stage IB in the printed table begins beyond what depth?
questions.why: 'IB macroinvasive cancer >5 mm deep'.

questions.q: Match the IB substage with its printed size - 1) IB1 2) IB2 3) IB3 ... A) Size > 4 cms B) Size <= 2 cms C) Size <= 4 cms ... choose:
questions.why: IB1 is <=2 cms, IB2 <=4 cms and IB3 >4 cms.

questions.q: Stage II in the printed table is defined by involvement of:
questions.why: The stage II row prints 'Involvement of upper 2/3rd of vagina'.

questions.q: In stage IIA the parametrium is printed as:
questions.why: 'IIA Parametrium not involved'.

questions.q: The printed size cut-offs for IIA1 and IIA2 are:
questions.why: The table prints IIA1 size <=4 cms and IIA2 size >4 cm.

questions.q: True/False: A 6 mm deep invasive cancer with a 3 cm lesion falls in stage IB1 on the printed table.

questions.q: Scenario: A cervical cancer measures 5 cm with invasion 8 mm deep and no vaginal or parametrial involvement. The printed stage is:

questions.q: Scenario: A 45-year-old with cancer cervix has tumour involving the upper vagina with free parametrium and a 3.5 cm lesion. The printed stage is:

questions.q: True/False: Cone biopsy follows LEEP when microinvasive cancer is reported on the LEEP specimen.

questions.q: Match each printed 'best' with its subject - 1) Best for parametrium 2) Best for nodes 3) m/c cause of death 4) Most specific symptom ... A) Renal failure B) Post coital bleeding C) MRI D) PET-CT ... choose:

units.title: FIGO Staging Stages III and IV with Notes

questions.q: Stage IIB in the printed table means:
questions.why: The IIB row prints 'Parametrium involved'.

questions.q: Stage III is defined by involvement of:
questions.why: 'III Involvement of lower 1/3rd of vagina'.

questions.q: In stage IIIA the pelvic side wall is printed as:
questions.why: 'IIIA Pelvic side wall not involved'.

questions.q: Stage IIIB adds pelvic side wall involvement with which printed consequences?
questions.why: The IIIB row prints hydroureter/hydronephrosis with ureter and kidney involvement.

questions.q: Stage IIIC denotes:
questions.why: 'IIIC Lymph nodes involvement'.

questions.q: Match the IIIC substage with its printed nodal site - 1) IIIC1 2) IIIC2 ... A) Para aortic lymph nodes B) Pelvic lymph nodes ... choose:
questions.why: IIIC1 is pelvic and IIIC2 para aortic nodal involvement.

questions.q: Stage IV in the printed table is summarised as:
questions.why: The IV row prints simply 'metastasis'.

questions.q: Stage IVA is printed as regional metastasis to:
questions.why: 'IVA Regional metastasis : Bladder/Bowel'.

questions.q: Stage IVB includes distant metastasis and which nodal involvement?
questions.why: 'IVB Distant metastasis/Superficial inguinal lymph node involvement'.

questions.q: Spread of cancer cervix to the uterus does what to staging?
questions.why: 'Spread of cancer cervix to uterus : Does not change staging'.

questions.q: Bullous oedema of bladder is printed as:
questions.why: 'Bullous edema of bladder : Not a metastasis'.

questions.q: Fill up: Bladder metastasis must be confirmed by histopathological evidence ____.
questions.why: 'Metastasis of bladder : Histopathological evidence +'.

questions.q: Match each stage with its printed defining feature - 1) IIB 2) IIIB 3) IIIC2 4) IVA ... A) Bladder/bowel regional metastasis B) Parametrium involved C) Para aortic nodes D) Hydronephrosis from side wall spread ... choose:
questions.why: IIB is parametrial, IIIB side wall with hydronephrosis, IIIC2 paraaortic nodes and IVA bladder or bowel.

questions.q: Scenario: Imaging shows unilateral hydronephrosis from tumour reaching the pelvic side wall, nodes negative. The printed stage is:
questions.why: Pelvic side wall involvement with hydroureter/hydronephrosis defines IIIB.

questions.q: Odd one out - which finding does NOT by itself make stage IVB?
questions.why: Bullous oedema is explicitly printed as not a metastasis.

questions.q: Surgery is printed as indicated up to which stage?
questions.why: 'Uptil stage IIa' heads the surgery indications.

questions.q: The printed tumour size limit for surgery is:
questions.why: 'Size of tumor < 4 cm'.

questions.q: Surgery is preferred in early stage except which substage?
questions.why: 'Preferred in early stage (except IB3)'.

questions.q: The printed relationship between radiotherapy and chemoradiation is:
questions.why: The arm heading prints 'Radio-therapy < Chemoradiation'.

questions.q: Chemoradiation can be done in which stages?
questions.why: 'Can be done in all stages' under the chemoradiation arm.

questions.q: Chemoradiation is preferred when what is contraindicated?
questions.why: 'Preferred when Sx is contraindicated'.

questions.q: The printed radiosensitizers are:
questions.why: 'Radiosensitizer : Cisplatin, 5FU'.

questions.q: Match each treatment arm with its printed attribute - 1) Surgery 2) Chemoradiation ... A) All stages, preferred when surgery contraindicated B) Uptil stage IIa, tumour < 4 cm ... choose:

questions.q: The outcome status printed for Bursch colposuspension is:
questions.why: 'Good outcome : Gold standard'.

questions.q: Match each Bursch attribute with its printed value - 1) Route 2) Structures suspended 3) Anchor 4) Status ... A) Gold standard B) Abdominal C) Proximal urethra and bladder neck D) Iliopectineal/Cooper's ligament ... choose:
questions.why: Abdominal route, proximal urethra with bladder neck, Cooper's ligament anchor and gold standard outcome.

questions.q: The two tension-free tapes printed are:
questions.why: The tree prints tension-free transobturator tape (TOT) and tension-free transvaginal tape (TVT).

questions.q: TOT and TVT share which three printed attributes?
options: Day care Sx, abdominal route and bladder neck suspended
Day care Sx, vaginal route and proximal urethra suspended
Hospital stay, vaginal route and middle urethra suspended
Day care Sx, vaginal route Sx and middle urethra suspended
questions.why: The shared bracket prints day care Sx, vaginal route Sx and middle urethra is suspended.

questions.q: The tape in TOT is passed via:
questions.why: 'Tape passed via obturator foramen' under TOT.

questions.q: The more common surgery between the two tapes printed is:
questions.why: 'm/c Sx (TOT > TVT)'.

questions.q: The tape in TVT is passed via:
questions.why: 'Tape passed via retropubic space' under TVT.

questions.q: TVT carries increased risk of injury to which structures?
questions.why: 'up risk of injury to bladder & venous plexus' under TVT.

questions.q: The TOT/TVT figure on page 261 labels which pelvic spaces and foramen?
questions.why: The leader lines print retropubic space and obturator foramen with TVT and TOT tapes.

questions.q: Match each tape with its printed route and risk - 1) TOT 2) TVT ... A) Retropubic space with bladder and venous plexus injury risk B) Obturator foramen and m/c Sx ... choose:
questions.why: TOT goes through the obturator foramen and is m/c; TVT goes retropubic with bladder and plexus risk.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman with SUI wants a day-care vaginal procedure with the lowest bladder injury risk. The printed choice is:
questions.why: TOT is the m/c day-care vaginal tape and the bladder injury risk is printed for TVT.

questions.q: Odd one out - which attribute belongs to Bursch colposuspension rather than the tapes?
questions.why: The tapes are day care vaginal with middle urethra suspended; Bursch needs hospital stay.

questions.q: True/False: Both TOT and TVT suspend the middle urethra rather than the bladder neck.
options: False - TOT suspends bladder neck only
False - they suspend the bladder neck
questions.why: The shared bullet prints middle urethra is suspended.

questions.q: Constant dribbling of urine from the vagina with normal micturition indicates:
questions.why: Complaint 1 prints that combination for ureterovaginal fistula.

questions.q: Constant dribbling of urine from the vagina with no normal micturition indicates:
questions.why: Complaint 2 prints that combination for vesicovaginal fistula.

questions.q: Urine passed from both urethra and vagina during micturition indicates:
questions.why: Complaint 3 prints urethrovaginal fistula.

questions.q: The types diagram numbers the three fistulae from above down as:
questions.why: The sketch prints 1, 2, 3 with that legend.

questions.q: The types diagram labels which four pelvic structures?
questions.why: The leader lines print ureter, uterus, bladder and vagina.

questions.q: Match each complaint with its fistula - 1) Dribbling with normal micturition 2) Dribbling with no normal micturition 3) Urine per urethra and vagina during micturition ... A) Urethrovaginal B) Ureterovaginal C) Vesicovaginal ... choose:
questions.why: The complaint box pairs them in that order.

questions.q: Scenario: A woman after hysterectomy dribbles urine continuously yet passes normal volumes per urethra. The printed fistula is:
questions.why: Preserved normal micturition with continuous dribbling is the ureterovaginal pattern.

questions.q: True/False: In vesicovaginal fistula the bladder empties wholly through the vagina, so normal micturition stops.
options: False - only half the urine leaks
questions.why: Complaint 2 prints no normal micturition with vesicovaginal fistula.

questions.q: The printed method of collecting a urine sample in fistula workup is:
questions.why: 'Collection of urine sample : Suprapubic catheterization'.

questions.q: Menouria is defined on the page as:
options: Menstrual blood in urine sample only
Urine passing per vagina during menstruation
questions.why: 'Menouria : Hematuria during menstruation'.

questions.q: The two causes printed for menouria are:
options: Endometriosis of bladder and ureterovaginal fistula
Endometriosis of bladder and vesicouterine fistula
questions.why: The bullets print endometriosis of bladder and vesicouterine fistula.

questions.q: Fill up: Blood in urine appearing only during menstruation is printed as ____.
questions.why: The box prints menouria with that definition.

questions.q: Odd one out - which cause is NOT printed for menouria?
questions.why: Only endometriosis of bladder and vesicouterine fistula are printed.

questions.q: The methylene blue three swab test is the IOC for which fistula?
questions.why: 'IOC for vesicovaginal fistula' under the test heading.

questions.q: How many swabs are placed in the vagina for the test?
questions.why: '3 swabs placed at vagina'.

questions.q: The upper swab corresponds to which fistula?
questions.why: 'a. Upper part : Corresponding to ureterovaginal fistula'.

questions.q: The middle swab corresponds to which fistula?
questions.why: 'b. Middle part : Corresponding to vesicovaginal fistula'.

questions.q: The lower swab corresponds to which fistula?
questions.why: 'c. Lower part : Corresponding to urethrovaginal fistula'.

questions.q: The dye is injected into bladder and urethra using which catheter?
questions.why: 'Methylene blue dye injected into bladder & urethra by Foley's catheter'.

questions.q: An upper swab that is wet but unstained implies:
questions.why: The table row prints upper swab wet, but unstained -> ureterovaginal fistula.

questions.q: A middle swab wet and stained blue implies:
questions.why: The table row prints middle swab wet & stained blue -> vesicovaginal fistula.

questions.q: Only the lower swab wet and stained blue implies:
questions.why: The table row prints only lower swab wet & stained blue -> urethrovaginal fistula.

questions.q: Why is the upper swab unstained in a ureterovaginal fistula?
options: The dye enters below the ureteric leak, so ureteric urine bypasses the bladder dye
Because the swab is too dry
questions.why: The dye is instilled into bladder and urethra; a ureteric leak above delivers unstained urine, matching the wet-but-unstained row.

questions.q: Match each swab position with its printed inference - 1) Upper wet unstained 2) Middle wet stained 3) Lower wet stained ... A) Urethrovaginal B) Ureterovaginal C) Vesicovaginal ... choose:
questions.why: The table prints those three inferences in order.

questions.q: Scenario: After the three swab test the middle swab alone is wet and blue. The printed diagnosis is:
questions.why: The middle swab wet and stained blue row is vesicovaginal fistula.

units.title: Vesicovaginal Fistula: Causes and Timing of Repair

questions.q: The most common cause of vesicovaginal fistula in developed countries is:
questions.why: 'Developed countries : Total abdominal hysterectomy (TAH)'.

questions.q: The most common cause in developing countries is:
questions.why: 'Developing countries : Obstructed labour'.

questions.q: If a fistula is identified immediately after surgery, the printed repair timing is:
questions.why: The immediate arm prints immediate repair.

questions.q: If identified after 24 hours of surgery, repair is deferred to:
questions.why: The bracket prints repair after 6 wks.

questions.q: The same 6-week delay applies to which other group?
questions.why: The bracket joins identified after 24 hrs of Sx with post obstructed labour.

questions.q: The reason printed for waiting 6 weeks is:
questions.why: 'After infection & inflammation subsides'.

questions.q: Match each identification timing with its printed repair plan - 1) Immediately after Sx 2) After 24 hrs of Sx 3) Post obstructed labour ... A) Repair after 6 weeks B) Immediate repair C) Repair after 6 weeks ... choose:
questions.why: Immediate identification repairs at once; both late groups wait 6 weeks.

questions.q: Scenario: A vesicovaginal fistula is recognised on day 5 after TAH. The printed plan is:
options: Repair after 6 weeks once infection and inflammation subside
questions.why: Identification beyond 24 hours routes to the 6-week arm.

questions.q: True/False: Obstructed labour remains the commonest cause of vesicovaginal fistula in developing countries.
questions.why: The two-country split prints exactly that.

questions.q: Name the two techniques printed for vesicovaginal fistula repair.
options: Chassar moir technique and Latzko technique
questions.why: The technique bullets print Chassar moir technique and Latzko technique.

questions.q: Post-operatively the bladder is drained with which catheter and for how long with antibiotics?
options: Foley's catheter with antibiotics for 2 weeks
Foley's catheter with antibiotics for 1 week
Ureteric stent with antibiotics for 2 weeks
Suprapubic catheter with antibiotics for 4 weeks
questions.why: 'Bladder drainage with Foley's catheter + antibiotics x 2 wks'.

questions.q: Which examinations are forbidden for 3 months after repair?
questions.why: 'No P/S or P/V examinations' bracketed for 3 months.

questions.q: Intercourse is prohibited for how long after repair?
questions.why: 'No intercourse' sits inside the same 3-month bracket.

questions.q: Pregnancy is contraindicated for how long after fistula repair?
questions.why: 'Pregnancy C/I x 1 year'.

questions.q: Match each post-op instruction with its printed duration - 1) Foley drainage with antibiotics 2) No P/S or P/V and no intercourse 3) Pregnancy contraindicated ... A) 3 months B) 2 weeks C) 1 year ... choose:
questions.why: The brackets print 2 weeks for drainage, 3 months for examinations and intercourse and 1 year for pregnancy.

questions.q: Odd one out - which instruction is NOT printed after vesicovaginal fistula repair?
options: Foley drainage with antibiotics for 2 weeks
questions.why: Catheter drainage is mandated, not avoided.

questions.q: Fill up: The two eponymous repairs printed are Chassar ____ and Latzko techniques.
questions.why: The bullets print Chassar moir technique.

questions.q: OHSS is printed as which category of complication?
questions.why: The pathophysiology box opens with 'Iatrogenic complication : Inj. HMG'.

questions.q: The injection printed as the iatrogenic trigger at the top of the chain is:
questions.why: The first line prints Inj. HMG.

questions.q: Excessive stimulation of the ovaries produces:
questions.why: The chain prints multiple large follicles.

questions.q: The estrogen threshold printed in the chain is:
questions.why: 'Estrogen (>=2500 pg)' in the follicle box.

questions.q: The factor released from follicular fluid in the chain is:
questions.why: 'VEGF from follicular fluid'.

questions.q: Failure of monitoring leads to which injection in the chain?
questions.why: The chain prints failure of monitoring then Inj. hCG.

questions.q: Rupture of the follicle releases:
questions.why: 'Rupture of follicle -> Release of VEGF'.

questions.q: The two monitoring methods printed are:
options: USG of ascites and estrogen levels
Follicular monitoring to monitor size of follicles and estrogen levels
questions.why: The monitoring bullets print follicular monitoring for size and estrogen levels.

questions.q: The ultrasound image on page 264 is captioned:
questions.why: The caption under the scan reads 'Large follicles'.

questions.q: Arrange the OHSS chain in printed order - 1) Release of VEGF 2) Inj. HMG 3) Multiple large follicles 4) Inj. hCG after failed monitoring 5) Rupture of follicle ... choose:
questions.why: The box prints HMG, large follicles, then failed monitoring with hCG, rupture and VEGF release.

questions.q: True/False: VEGF release follows follicle rupture in the printed OHSS chain.
questions.why: The chain ends rupture of follicle then release of VEGF.

questions.q: Name the eight printed risk factors for OHSS.
options: Young females, PCOS, thin female, raised follicle number, raised antral count, raised AMH, raised estradiol and pelvic TB
Young females, PCOS, obese female, raised follicle number, raised AMH, raised estradiol, multiple pregnancy and smoking
Young females, PCOS, thin female, raised follicle number on TVS, raised antral follicle count, raised AMH >3.3, raised estradiol >=2500 pg and pregnancy
Older females, PCOS, thin female, raised follicle number, raised AMH, raised estradiol and pregnancy
questions.why: The risk box lists exactly those eight items.

questions.q: The AMH threshold printed as a risk factor is:
questions.why: 'up AMH >3.3'.

questions.q: The estradiol risk threshold printed is:
questions.why: 'up Estradiol (E2) >=2500 pg'.

questions.q: Body habitus printed as a risk factor is:
questions.why: 'Thin female' in the risk list.

questions.q: Which final physiological state completes the risk list?
questions.why: The last risk bullet prints pregnancy.

questions.q: Odd one out - which item is NOT a printed OHSS risk factor?
questions.why: The printed habitus is thin female; obesity is absent.

questions.q: Match each risk factor with its printed threshold - 1) AMH 2) Estradiol 3) Follicle monitoring ... A) >= 2500 pg B) > 3.3 C) Number of follicles on TVS ... choose:
questions.why: AMH >3.3, estradiol >=2500 pg and TVS follicle number are the printed entries.

questions.q: The printed complaints of OHSS are:
options: Abdominal pain, bleeding, dyspnoea and syncope
Nausea, diarrhoea, abdominal pain and cough
Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and dyspnoea
questions.why: The complaints box prints those four with clinical diagnosis.

questions.q: OHSS is diagnosed how, according to the box?
questions.why: The arrow from complaints ends at clinical diagnosis.

questions.q: The drug with the highest risk of OHSS printed is:
questions.why: 'hMG : Highest risk'.

questions.q: Clomiphene citrate carries which printed risk level?
questions.why: 'Clomiphene citrate : Low risk'.

questions.q: Letrozole carries which printed risk level?
questions.why: 'Letrozole : No risk'.

questions.q: The triggering factor printed for OHSS is:
questions.why: 'Triggering factors : Inj. hCG'.

questions.q: Fill up: The mediator printed for OHSS is ____.
questions.why: 'Mediator : VEGF'.

questions.q: Match each drug with its printed OHSS risk - 1) hMG 2) Clomiphene citrate 3) Letrozole ... A) No risk B) Highest risk C) Low risk ... choose:
questions.why: The drugs box prints highest, low and no risk respectively.

questions.q: Scenario: A PCOS patient on ovulation induction asks which agent least risks OHSS. The printed answer is:
questions.why: Letrozole is printed with no risk while clomiphene is low and hMG highest.

questions.q: Early OHSS is due to:
questions.why: 'Early OHSS : D/t exogenous Inj. of hCG'.

questions.q: Early OHSS occurs within how many days of hCG injection?
questions.why: 'Within 9 days of Inj. hCG'.

questions.q: Late OHSS is due to:
options: Endogenous hCG produced by placenta during pregnancy
questions.why: 'Late OHSS : D/t endogenous hCG produced by placenta during pregnancy'.

questions.q: In the late OHSS line, after how many days does endogenous production dominate?
questions.why: The line prints Inj. hCG struck through at 9 days with up endogenous production.

questions.q: Match each OHSS timing with its printed hCG source - 1) Early 2) Late ... A) Endogenous placental hCG B) Exogenous injected hCG ... choose:
questions.why: Early follows the injected trigger; late follows placental hCG.

questions.q: True/False: Late OHSS implies the induction cycle has conceived.
options: False - late OHSS occurs without pregnancy
False - late OHSS is drug induced
questions.why: Late OHSS is printed as due to placental hCG during pregnancy.

questions.q: Odd one out - which statement contradicts the printed early/late split?
options: Early OHSS occurs within 9 days of injection
Early OHSS is due to placental hCG
questions.why: Placental hCG defines late, not early, OHSS.

questions.q: The first prevention step printed is:
options: Monitoring of follicles in TVS and estrogen levels
questions.why: The prevention box opens with monitoring of follicles in TVS & estrogen levels.

questions.q: hCG should be withheld if estrogen reaches:
questions.why: 'Withhold hCG if estrogen >=2500 pg'.

questions.q: Cabergoline prevents OHSS by:
questions.why: 'Cabergoline : down VEGF'.

questions.q: Embryo transfer is avoided in which situation?
options: If risk of OHSS is positive
questions.why: 'No embryo transfer : If risk of OHSS +'.

questions.q: The ideal estrogen range printed for hCG induction is:
questions.why: The cloud prints estrogen 500 - 1500 pg.

questions.q: The ideal follicle number printed for hCG induction is:
questions.why: 'Number : 2-3' in the follicles box.

questions.q: The ideal follicle size printed for hCG induction is:
questions.why: 'Size : >17 mm'.

questions.q: The note at the foot of page 264 prints the amount of E2 released per follicle as:
questions.why: 'Amount of E2 released per follicle : 200 pg'.

questions.q: Match each prevention measure with its printed trigger - 1) Withhold hCG 2) Cabergoline 3) No embryo transfer ... A) Risk of OHSS positive B) Estrogen >= 2500 pg C) To lower VEGF ... choose:
questions.why: Withholding follows the estrogen threshold, cabergoline lowers VEGF and transfer is skipped when OHSS risk is positive.

questions.q: Scenario: A stimulated cycle shows estradiol 2600 pg with eight follicles. The printed preventive actions are:
options: Withhold hCG and avoid embryo transfer
Proceed with hCG as follicles are ideal
questions.why: Estrogen >=2500 pg mandates withholding hCG and a positive OHSS risk mandates no embryo transfer.

questions.q: Scenario: Using the printed per-follicle E2 figure, three mature follicles would contribute approximately:
questions.why: Each follicle releases 200 pg, so three give about 600 pg, inside the ideal 500-1500 pg window.

questions.q: True/False: The ideal conditions cloud prints follicle size above 17 mm with number 2-3 for hCG induction.
questions.why: The cloud prints number 2-3 and size >17 mm.

questions.q: Fill up: Cabergoline prevents OHSS by lowering ____.
questions.why: 'Cabergoline : down VEGF'.
